title: Centralize validator class-name sets / discriminators into one Tensile-lite category() map (NO rocisa changes)
description:
## Why

Audit `rocm-libraries-8t9` (commit 33a116f272, Section 2 Category A) identified the largest cluster of validator-side workarounds: the validator hand-maintains 10+ class-name sets (`_LR_CLASS_NAMES`, `_LW_CLASS_NAMES`, `_GR_CLASS_NAMES`, `_MFMA_CLASS_NAMES`, `_SWAIT_CLASS_NAMES`, `_SBARRIER_CLASS_NAMES`, `_SNOP_CLASS_NAMES`, `_SSETPRIO_CLASS_NAMES`, `_CVT_PACK_CLASS_NAMES`, `_MIDDLE_PACK_CLASS_NAMES`, `_SMEM_CLASS_NAMES`, `_FLAT_CLASS_NAMES`, `_VECTOR_STORE_CLASS_NAMES`), 10 `_is_*` discriminator predicates, two tag mappers (`_class_tag`, `_class_tag_from_category`), two type maps (`PACK_TYPE_MAP`, `GR_TYPE_MAP`), and a wrapper dataclass (`TaggedInstruction`) — all because rocisa instruction classes don't expose a semantic-category attribute.

## Scope

- rocisa C++: add a class-level `category` attribute returning a member of an `InstructionCategory` enum (LR / LW / GR / MFMA / SWAIT / SBARRIER / SNOP / SSETPRIO / PACK / SMEM / FLAT / STORE plus finer Pack subdivisions per current PACK_TYPE_MAP).
- rocisa nanobind: expose the attribute to Python.
- Validator: replace class-name-set lookups with `inst.category == X` comparisons. Eliminate the discriminator family. Collapse tag mappers.
- Optional: also add `validator_kind` and `asm_label` for the PACK_TYPE_MAP / GR_TYPE_MAP entries.

## Hard rules

- Additive on the rocisa side; validator can read the new attribute when present and fall back to the existing class-name set when absent (incremental migration).
- Snapshot test: every captured opcode in CI must produce identical category assignments before and after migration.

## Acceptance

- All 13 `*_CLASS_NAMES` sets deleted.
- All 10 `_is_*` discriminators deleted (or reduced to one-line attribute reads).
- `PACK_TYPE_MAP` and `GR_TYPE_MAP` deleted; `resolve_pack_type` and `is_gr_load` query rocisa class attributes.
- `TaggedInstruction` reduced to (slot,) wrapper or deleted entirely if the per-instance scheduler-role tag can travel on the rocisa instance.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `rocm-libraries-br4` (validator consolidation; migration target should be stable first).
- Audit reference: `rocm-libraries-8t9` (commit 33a116f272), section 2 Category A and section 3 Step 1.

## Audit reference

Spawned from `Tensile/Components/ROCISA_WORKAROUNDS_AUDIT.md` (the 8t9 audit, commit 33a116f272; status update at the top reflects subsequent reframings).

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.
close_reason: Re-scoped Python-only refactor in commit 08fd38cff1a; rocisa untouched; unblocks rocm-libraries-s5g1

comments.author: user-rescope
comments.text:
RE-SCOPED per user direction (2026-05-08).

The original framing — push semantic-category attribute onto rocisa instruction classes — is REJECTED. Pushing scheduler categories (LR/LW/GR/MFMA/PACK/...) into rocisa is a layer-violation: rocisa should know 'this is a DSLoadB128 with these operands'; whether something is 'LR' vs 'LW' is Tensile-lite's scheduling vocabulary, not an intrinsic rocisa property.

NEW SCOPE: centralize the existing validator-side workarounds into ONE Tensile-lite-side mapping, without touching rocisa C++ at all.

Concretely:
1. Replace the 13 *_CLASS_NAMES sets (_LR_CLASS_NAMES, _LW_CLASS_NAMES, _GR_CLASS_NAMES, _MFMA_CLASS_NAMES, _SWAIT_CLASS_NAMES, _SBARRIER_CLASS_NAMES, _SNOP_CLASS_NAMES, _SSETPRIO_CLASS_NAMES, _CVT_PACK_CLASS_NAMES, _MIDDLE_PACK_CLASS_NAMES, _SMEM_CLASS_NAMES, _FLAT_CLASS_NAMES, _VECTOR_STORE_CLASS_NAMES) with one Python-side dict[str, InstructionCategory] (or class -> category map).
2. Replace the 10 _is_* discriminator predicates with one-line attribute reads against the central map: _is_mfma_producer(inst) -> classify(inst) == InstructionCategory.MFMA, etc.
3. Collapse _class_tag / _class_tag_from_category tag mappers.
4. Rewrite resolve_pack_type and is_gr_load to query the central map (no PACK_TYPE_MAP / GR_TYPE_MAP duplication).
5. Reduce TaggedInstruction to (slot,) wrapper (or delete) if the per-instance scheduler-role tag can travel on the wrapped rocisa instance via the central map.

Hard rule: NO rocisa C++ changes. The InstructionCategory enum lives in Tensile-lite (likely Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py or a new Tensile/Components/InstructionCategory.py). Snapshot test: every captured opcode in CI must produce identical category assignments before vs after consolidation.

Acceptance unchanged: all 13 *_CLASS_NAMES sets deleted; all 10 _is_* discriminators reduced to one-line lookups; PACK_TYPE_MAP / GR_TYPE_MAP deleted (data lives in the central map). The previous worktree (users/alvasile/009-impl) had ~7 rocisa C++ files modified — DISCARDED; branch deleted. Start fresh from vlt.

title: Update stale cmw-formula docstrings in test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py
description:
## Discovered by

Bead `c44` end-to-end verification (critical-eye pass on docstrings).

## The stale comments

`Tensile/Tests/unit/test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py:694-705` still describes the cmw formula `slot_delta * (1 + finish) - 1 + subiter_delta` as the live behavior of the gap calculation.

After bead `nk0` migrated `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` to delegate to `cumulative_issue_cycles`, the slot-delta formula is no longer accurate for the MFMA->MFMA path it documents. The formula IS still in use inside `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` (separately tracked in bead `2yk` for that helper's own docstring lie).

## Why this matters

The next reader trying to understand the test will read the comment, assume the formula is the live behavior, and either:
1. Trace it through the wrong code path, OR
2. Modify the formula in the test fixture's expected-value calculation and find the test still passes (because the actual formula in `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` is now `cumulative_issue_cycles`).

Doc rot wastes future-reader time and erodes trust in surrounding documentation.

## Action

Update the docstring at `test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py:694-705` to describe the current behavior:

- `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` (MFMA->MFMA) uses `cumulative_issue_cycles` for cycle-exact accounting (post-`nk0`).
- `_mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok` (PackMFMA->CVT1) also uses `cumulative_issue_cycles`.
- `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` (CVT->MFMA) still uses the slot-delta formula (see bead `2yk`).

Drop any references to the cmw formula as a generic gap calculator.

## Why P3

Pure documentation defect. Easy fix; high reader-impact.

## Related

- `2yk` — `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` docstring lie (same family of doc rot).
- `nk0` — the bead that made the cmw formula obsolete for `_quad_cycle_gap_ok`.
- `c44` — verification bead that surfaced the gap.

title: Final naming-quality pass over everything touched by validator-branch work
description:
## Why this exists

After the multi-wave validator refactor (Phase 2/3 audits + 5gd timeline decoupling + l6q.1 ArchProfile + zq3 whole-kernel coverage), do a final naming-quality pass over everything the work touched. Names accumulated organically across many beads, many agents, and many shifts in scope:

- File names chose during the structural era may not describe their post-graph contents (`CMSValidator.py` is no longer "the" validator; `ScheduleCapture.py` is now the load-bearing surface).
- Function names from the structural era survived the graph-native migration and may not reflect what the function now does (e.g. `validate_*` helpers that no longer follow the structural-rule contract).
- Helper functions added incrementally have names that fit their original narrow purpose but are vague after subsequent unification (`_quad_cycle_gap_ok` after the `2bu` unification — does the name still describe what it does?).
- Variable names inside long functions accumulated short, context-dependent abbreviations (`prod`, `cons`, `pos`, `bd`) that read fine while editing one helper but obscure intent across the whole module.

## Scope

Everything **touched** by the validator-branch work (commits since `users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans` diverged from `develop`). Use `git diff --name-only develop...HEAD -- '*.py'` to scope.

For each file:

1. **Filename.** Does it still describe the file's contents? Does the file name match the dominant abstraction inside it? (e.g. `ScheduleCapture.py` contains the dataflow graph + comparison engine + Failure formatters — is that the right name?)
2. **Module-level constants and types.** `_OPERAND_RULES`, `POSITION_INF`, `ValidationConcern`, `PipelineStage`, etc. — do the names match what they represent?
3. **Class names.** `GraphNode`, `DataflowEdge`, `DataflowGraph`, `LoopBodyCapture`, the 12 `Failure` subclasses, `ValidatorInstruction`, `SchedulePosition`. Does each name communicate the abstraction at first read?
4. **Function names.** Public and private. The `_*_gap_ok` helpers, `cumulative_issue_cycles`, `validate_edge_wait_coverage`, `compare_graphs`, `diagnose_missing_edge`, `_node_label`, `_node_with_pos`, `_iter_note`, `_logical_position`, the resolver functions, the four pair helpers, the `_OPERAND_RULES` dispatch entries, the `_GenericALURule` family.
5. **Variable names** (the surface area that matters most; do not be exhaustive). Focus on long functions where local scope is large enough that variable names matter. Top targets: `cumulative_issue_cycles`, `validate_edge_wait_coverage`, `compare_graphs`, `diagnose_missing_edge`, the per-rule emit logic.
6. **Test file names + test method names.** Long test files where the file name no longer scopes its contents; test methods where the `test_` prefix is followed by a vague clause.
7. **Audit / report markdown filenames.** `EKZ_AUDIT.md`, `F80_AUDIT.md`, `FNF_STUB_AUDIT.md`, `LCC_AUDIT.md`, `ONT_AUDIT.md`, `WX93_RESEARCH_REPORT.md`, `YX3_AUDIT.md`, `CMSValidator_LIMITATIONS.md`. Do these names describe their contents to a reader who didn't live through the bead history? Bead-name-prefixed files are unfriendly to new readers.

## Process

This is a **judgment-heavy pass**, not a mechanical rename. Bias toward keeping a name unless the rename meaningfully improves clarity. Cosmetic renames (e.g. `idx` → `index`) are noise; semantic renames (e.g. `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` → `_can_issue_consumer_after_producer`, hypothetical) earn their place.

For each candidate rename:

1. Propose the new name with a one-line justification ("current name says X; function now does Y; rename to clarify").
2. Audit call sites (`grep -rn` or LSP rename) to confirm rename is mechanical and complete.
3. Verify no public-API rename is silently breaking external callers (Tensile is consumed by `hipblaslt`/`rocBLAS`; check for cross-repo usage of any renamed public symbol).
4. Land in batched commits (`[rename]` prefix) per logical group.

## Coordination with prior audits

The wave-2/3 audits (`fnf`, `ont`, `ekz`, `f80`, `yx3`) produced migration tables in `*_AUDIT.md` files. **Do NOT rename or delete those audit files in this bead** — they are historical records. Rename only their references inside the code (if any). New audit table from this bead lives at `Tensile/Components/RENAME_AUDIT.md` (or similar).

## Verification

- `pytest Tensile/Tests/unit/` MUST stay green after each rename batch.
- `grep -rn '<old_name>' .` should return zero hits after the rename batch (excluding the audit doc).
- For public symbols renamed: check no external repo currently imports the old name.

## Hard rules

- **Pure rename.** No behavior changes. Function bodies untouched except where they reference the renamed symbol.
- **No speculative renames.** Only rename when you can articulate why the new name is concretely clearer than the old.
- **No abbreviation expansion noise.** `idx` → `index` only if `index` actually clarifies in context.
- **No bead references in new names.** Names should make sense to a reader who has never seen a bead.
- **Public-API renames need extra care.** Add deprecation alias if any external repo imports the old name; search before assuming nothing imports it.

## Why this is at the end

Renaming before the major refactors land (5gd Timeline decoupling, l6q.1 ArchProfile, zq3 whole-kernel coverage) wastes work — those refactors will create new abstractions that need their own naming pass. Doing this last lets us name everything against the final architecture once.

## Why P3

Quality / clarity work; not gating any current functionality. Best done as one focused sweep rather than piecemeal during other work. Priority elevates if a new contributor reports finding the codebase hard to navigate.

## Activation trigger

Run after these have all landed (or been explicitly deferred):
- `5gd` epic (Timeline decoupling)
- `l6q.1` (ArchProfile)
- `zq3` (whole-kernel coverage)
- `2yg` (design doc — gives the canonical vocabulary the renames should align with)
- `wx9.3` if implemented (canonical-form / value-numbering names)

If any of those are deferred indefinitely, run this bead after the ones that did land.

## Related beads

- `2yg` — design doc; should land before this so the rename pass aligns with documented vocabulary.
- All wave-2/3 audit beads (`fnf`, `ont`, `ekz`, `f80`, `yx3`) — closed; their audit docs are historical records and not renamed by this bead.
- `fxl` — closed (ScheduleCapture.py won't be split into a package). This bead operates on the current single-file structure.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: Pin: SWaitCnt counter value of -1 correctly does NOT guarantee any producer (test gap)
description:
## Why this exists

In the AMD SWaitCnt encoding, a counter field of -1 means "no constraint" (the counter is ignored). This is the OPPOSITE of "strictest" — -1 leaves the counter unbounded, so an SWaitCnt with dscnt=-1 does NOT drain any LDS-load FIFO entries.

The validator's _swait_drains helper (Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:1356) correctly handles this:

    if v is None or v < 0:
        return None  # treats -1 as 'no constraint'

The drain logic (_wait_drains_producer, _queue_depth_at, _producer_queue_position) all skip SWaitCnts that return None for the relevant counter, so producers behind a -1 SWait are correctly NOT considered guaranteed.

## The gap

There is no explicit pinning test for this behavior. The two existing _swait_drains tests cover:
- test_no_edge_when_swait_drains_wrong_counter (counter mismatch case)
- test_two_LR0s_swait_drains_only_one (drain-cap selectivity)

Neither asserts that -1 alone fails to drain. If a future refactor accidentally treats -1 as 'drain everything' (the intuitive but wrong reading), no test would catch it.

## What to add

A test in Tensile/Tests/unit/test_dataflow_graph_builder.py (or wherever _swait_drains is most exercised) that:
1. Constructs an SWaitCnt with dscnt=-1 (vlcnt and vscnt arbitrary).
2. Constructs an LDS producer (LRA0) before the SWait.
3. Constructs an LDS consumer (MFMA) after the SWait.
4. Asserts validate_edge_wait_coverage emits MissingWaitFailure on the LRA0 -> MFMA edge — because the -1 SWait does NOT drain the producer.

Symmetric tests for vlcnt=-1 (GR producer) and vscnt=-1 (vector store producer) optional but cheap to add.

## Why P3

Coverage gap, not a known bug. Important to lock in because the semantic of -1 is confusing (intuitive reading is wrong) and easy to regress in a refactor that touches counter handling. Surfaced during the hof Failure-formatter review.

## Related

- WaitInsufficientFailure formatter (Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py): documents the -1 semantic in its formatter comments. The new test makes the documentation enforceable.
- _swait_drains helper (line 1356).
- _wait_drains_producer (line 3459).
close_reason: Pin tests added in commit a66b8a8aba on users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans. Tests assert SWaitCnt(dscnt=-1) and SWaitCnt(vlcnt=-1) do not drain LRA0/GRA producers; symmetric vscnt case skipped (no producer category). 594 passed (+2 from baseline 592).

title: C3c: build_dataflow_graph rewrite consuming UnrolledCapture
description:
Implementation step 4 of the unrolled-walk transition. See UNROLLED_VALIDATION_PLAN.md §5 Commit 3c + §3.

Scope:
1. Switch build_dataflow_graph to call UnrolledCapture.from_four_part_capture(fpc) and walk the result.
2. Phase 1: walk unrolled iter sequence producing one GraphNode per stream position. Multiple ML iter copies of the same TaggedInstruction get distinct GraphNode objects sharing the same identity (iter-blind).
3. Phase 2: single linear latest_writer walk over the unrolled stream, no per-body resets except the existing SCC-boundary clearing (barriers reset SCC's latest_writer entry — preserved). Populate byte_key_writers from C3b alongside.
4. Extend DataflowEdge with diagnostic annotations: producer_iter_index, consumer_iter_index, producer_body_label, consumer_body_label, producer_unrolled_position, consumer_unrolled_position. These are for display + Phase 1 order checks; NOT in edge_keys().

Acceptance:
- build_dataflow_graph walks one unrolled stream; no per-body dispatch in the walk.
- The 11 break-list tests pass under the new walk (either same answers OR the exemption deletion + new walk produce different-but-correct answers).
- Validator state still partly RED — edge_keys() and compare_graphs haven't switched to byte-key basis yet (lands in C3d, C3e).

Re-fixture scope (mandatory — do NOT defer):
- test_dataflow_graph_builder.py:519-523: This block uses a list comprehension [n.identity for n in g.nodes if n.category == "LRA0"], then asserts len(ids_a) == 1 and ids_a[0] == ids_b[0]. Under C3c, LRA0 nodes from the ML body appear twice in the unrolled stream (once per ML iter copy, since ML_MAT_COUNT == 2). The assertions must become len(ids_a) == ML_MAT_COUNT (or equivalent symbolic constant), and the cross-graph identity pin ids_a[0] == ids_b[0] must be re-examined — under iter-copy duplication both iter copies share the same identity, so all entries in ids_a and ids_b will be identical; the pin should compare the full lists (ids_a == ids_b) or compare the unique set (set(ids_a) == set(ids_b)) depending on what the test is pinning. This site was identified by rocm-libraries-teym (the teym bead) as a C3c re-fixture obligation.

Standing rules apply.

title: Investigate Option (e) for intra-graph 7a fix: in-stream RegSet directive consumption
description:
## Why this exists

`rocm-libraries-wx9.3` (topology-equivalent comparison) has Approach A as the recommended cross-graph mechanism. A's correctness depends on the builder canonicalizing intra-graph references — the 7a problem.

Of the four mechanisms originally listed (a/b/c/d), (b) and (d) reduce to needing a name-resolution layer, (c) doesn't solve 7a, and (a) was previously rejected for coupling to writer state.

A fifth option **(e) — in-stream RegSet directive consumption** — is the most defensible candidate but needs verification. rocisa emits `RegSet` directives into the assembly stream that bind names to indices (e.g., `RegSet name='ValuA_X0_I0' idx=8`). If the capture pipeline retains these directives, the graph builder could parse them as it walks the body and build a body-local name→index map. Subsequent `vgpr('ValuA_X0_I0+N', K)` references resolve to `vgpr(8+N, K)` within that body's lookup.

This is essentially (a) re-scoped from 'external writer state' to 'in-stream metadata' — cleaner because the lifetime question disappears (the map is body-local) and there's no coupling to per-thread C++ globals.

## Phase 1 — Investigation using REAL capture data

**Hard rule: use real capture data, NOT synthetic.** Run actual captures via `generate_real_idmap` (`Tests/unit/cms_test_utils.py`) — the TF32 4x4 path (`test_tf32_4x4_tn_capture_shape` at `test_ScheduleCapture.py:673`) is the canonical real-codegen test. Inspect what's actually in the captured `FourPartCapture.main_loop[0].instructions` etc.

### Q1: Does the capture pipeline retain RegSet directives?

- Walk `ScheduleCapture.py`'s capture machinery (`LoopBodyCapture`, `expand_cms_macro`, `build_cms_four_part_capture`).
- Run a real capture and dump the captured instruction stream. Look for RegSet instances (rocisa class name probably `RegSet` or similar) — present in the stream, dropped, or filtered out?
- If retained: where in the data structure? At what granularity (per-body, per-codepath, per-instruction-position)?
- If dropped: at what stage are they dropped? What would it cost to retain them?

### Q2: Do real captures actually exhibit the 7a hazard?

- The d0xd Phase 1 memo's empirical claim was that 7a is rare/latent today because both captures consume the same writer state. Verify with real data.
- Walk a real captured body's instruction stream. Enumerate every `RegisterContainer` that appears as an operand. For each physical register (defined as `(reg_type, byte_range)`), tally how many forms it appears in (symbolic-only, numeric-only, mixed).
- Specifically check the TF32 4x4 capture: does ANY physical register appear under both forms?
- If 7a hazard is empirically zero in real captures, the urgency of the 7a fix drops — file a comment on wx9.3 noting this and the question becomes 'should we even fix 7a until a triggering kernel appears?'

### Q3: Sketch (e)'s implementation against the real data

- Assuming Q1 answers 'RegSets are retained,' sketch how the builder would consume them. Pseudocode is fine.
- Walk-order: does the builder process instructions in emission order? (It must, for in-stream resolution to work.)
- Lookup-table: where does the body-local name→index map live? On the LoopBodyCapture? Per-codepath? Per-body?
- Edge-formation impact: when forming an edge for an operand reference, what's the resolution flow? Pseudocode the change against `_byte_keys_for_resource`.

### Q4: Compare (e) against (a)

- (a) reads writer state externally; (e) reads RegSet directives in-stream.
- Both produce the same name→index mapping in principle. Are they ALWAYS equivalent, or are there cases where they diverge (e.g., RegSet emitted but the symbolic name is later re-bound to a different index, OR writer state gets mutated mid-build via undefine+redefine)?
- If (a) and (e) ever diverge, which one is correct for the validator's purposes?

### Q5: Capture-pipeline modifications required

- If RegSets are dropped today, what's the minimum change to retain them? Is it a single line in `expand_cms_macro`? A new field on `LoopBodyCapture`? A separate parallel stream?
- Estimate LoC for the capture-side change and the builder-side consumer.

## Hard rules

- Phase 1 is research only. No code changes. Memo only.
- **Use real capture data**, NOT mocks or synthetic instruction streams. Acceptable sources:
  - `generate_real_idmap` from `Tests/unit/cms_test_utils.py`

title: Remove cross-body 'body_delta * 1000' placeholder; count real cycles (requires LCC capture)
description:
## Why this exists

While auditing which Failure subclasses could carry a cross-iteration `(of next iteration)` note (the one added to `MissingWaitFailure` in bead `hof`), `TimingTooCloseFailure` came back as "structurally suppressed cross-body" rather than genuinely not applicable.

THREE helpers in `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py` collapse cross-body quad-cycle gaps to `body_delta * 1000`:

- `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` (~lines 3757-3762, MFMA->MFMA): `if producer.body_label != consumer.body_label: actual = abs(body_delta) * 1000; return True, expected, actual`
- `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` (~lines 3805-3811, CVT->MFMA): same shape
- `_mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok` (~lines 3868-3874, PackMFMA->CVT1): same shape

Effect: any cross-body producer/consumer pair always reports an enormous "actual" cycle gap, so the `actual < expected` comparison never trips. **Cross-iter Pack/MFMA timing failures are not detectable.**

## Confirmed: this fires in production (NOT hypothetical)

Per bead `x9i` end-to-end audit (Opus 4.7 sub-agent, commit `5b4afa4ba0`):

`KernelWriter.py:5211` constructs the default `FourPartCapture` with `main_loop_prev = clone_loop_body(main_loop)` — a verbatim deepcopy. So **every BF16/F8 output kernel** that uses `v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32` produces CVT-in-ML-1 -> MFMA-in-ML edges in the unified 4-body graph. The cross-body branch fires on every one of these.

The 9 `TestRealKernelCapture` failures the c44 audit observed when mutating the cross-body branch are consistent with this — every one of those captures triggers the placeholder.

x9i pinned the current sentinel behavior (`body_delta * 1000`) so any rewrite under this bead will trip a clear test.

## What this bead must do

**Remove the placeholder. Count real cross-body cycles.**

This is NOT optional. The placeholder is silently always-passing for a large slice of real production kernels; any timing violation crossing a body boundary is currently invisible.

## Hard requirement: LCC scheduling

To count real cross-body cycles correctly, the validator must be aware of the **Loop Counter Code (LCC)** instructions — the SALU group that increments/decrements loop counters and checks exit conditions. Today these are deliberately EXCLUDED from the graph (`ScheduleCapture.py:2682-2683`):

> "and LCC (out-of-scope: default emits it outside _loopBody, CMS bakes it into the macro)"

And from the per-body sidecar (lines 2765-2767):

> `if ... and node.identity[0] != "LCC": ...`

Per the validator design doc (`CMSMajorRefactorPlan.md:1045`):

| | CDNA 4 | RDNA 3.5 |
|---|---|---|
| LCC in schedule | No | Yes |

So LCC currently flies under the radar entirely. Real cycle counting across a body boundary must include the LCC issue cycles, or the count is wrong.

**Pre-requisite step**: capture LCC into the graph (or otherwise account for its issue cycles in the cross-body math). This is non-trivial — LCC is bucketed separately by the scheduler today. Decide whether to:

1. Capture LCC as graph nodes (alongside MFMA, LR, GR, etc.) and have `cumulative_issue_cycles` walk through them naturally.
2. Compute LCC's contribution as a constant per-body adder (sum of LCC issue cycles known at capture time, baked into the cross-body delta).
3. Some hybrid.

Option 1 is most honest (cycle-exact). Option 2 is simpler if LCC issue cycles are deterministic per kernel.

## Investigation plan

1. **Audit LCC issue cycles**: enumerate the SALU classes used in LCC (look at `CustomSchedule.py:920-1370` for LCC slot ranges across kernels). Are they all 1 quad-cycle? Or do some have wait-state?

2. **Decide LCC accounting strategy** (option 1, 2, or 3 above). Document the choice with rationale.

3. **Implement**:
   - If option 1: extend `build_dataflow_graph` to include LCC nodes; ensure `cumulative_issue_cycles` walks them.
   - If option 2: add a `body_lcc_cycles(body_label)` helper that returns the body's LCC contribution; cross-body math becomes `body_lcc_cycles(prev_body) + same_body_cycles_to_end + same_body_cycles_from_start`.
   - Either way: replace the three `body_delta * 1000` sentinels with the real math.

4. **Verify**:
   - The 3 unit tests added by `x9i` (currently pinning the sentinel) will need updates to assert real cycle counts. This is a behavior change; update them deliberately, document the new pinned values.
   - The 9 integration tests in `test_ScheduleCapture.py` that exercise cross-body should still pass — but they'll now exercise real math, not the sentinel.
   - Real-kernel captures (BF16/F8 output kernels) should not start emitting new TimingTooCloseFailures unless there's a genuine production timing bug. If they do: triage each as a real bug or a fixture issue.

5. **New strict-xfail tests** documenting any borderline scenarios surfaced (a Pack-then-MFMA pair across the iteration boundary with a tight gap that the sentinel was hiding).

## Related beads

- `nk0` — populated `GraphNode.issue_cycles`; precondition for option 1.
- `8nz` — deleted structural-side cycle simulators; established `cumulative_issue_cycles` as single source of truth (now must extend to cross-body).
- `c44` — verification bead that surfaced the placeholder.
- `x9i` — pinned the current sentinel behavior; tests there need to flip when this bead lands.
- `2yk` — `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` docstring lie (already filed; pre-requisite cleanup).

## Why P2 (upgraded from P3)

The x9i finding showed the suppressed branch fires on every BF16/F8 kernel, not as an edge case. This is load-bearing missed coverage in production. Bumped from P3 to P2.

title: Capture LCC instructions as graph nodes (no behavior change to cross-body validation)
description:
## Sub-task of bead `2bu`

Foundation step: include LCC in the dataflow graph so cross-body cycle counting can walk through it. **This sub-task makes NO behavior change to validation** — the three `body_delta * 1000` placeholders stay in place. Only the graph's contents change.

## Pre-requisite

Sub-bead `2bu.1` (LCC inventory audit) must be done first. The audit's output drives the per-class issue-cycle assignment in `_min_issue_quad_cycles_for`.

## Specific changes

1. **`Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:2682-2683`** — drop the LCC exclusion comment + the LCC filter in `build_dataflow_graph`'s Phase 1 walk. LCC instructions become graph nodes.

2. **Same file, ~lines 2765-2767** — drop the `node.identity[0] != "LCC"` filter in the per-body sidecar (`_graph_nodes`). LCC nodes appear in the per-body stream so wait/barrier helpers can find them in stream order.

3. **`_min_issue_quad_cycles_for`** (~line 2633) — extend the dispatch table to handle LCC SALU classes correctly per the `2bu.1` audit. Most will be 1 quad-cycle; SCC-chain classes may differ.

3. Assert `cumulative_issue_cycles(graph, producer_mfma, consumer_mfma)` correctly accounts for any LCC instructions between producer and consumer in the SAME body. (This exercises the new walk path; cross-body still uses the placeholder.)

The graph having more nodes is a no-op for any code that doesn't read them. The cross-body math stays placeholder. title: Replace cross-body placeholder in _quad_cycle_gap_ok (MFMA->MFMA) with cumulative_issue_cycles
description:
## Sub-task of bead `2bu`

Replace BOTH branches of `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` (MFMA->MFMA pair) with a single unified call to `cumulative_issue_cycles`. There should be ONE function that computes the actual cycle gap between two instructions; the cross-iteration distinction is a red herring because the graph has all instructions laid out in execution order regardless of which body they belong to.

## Pre-requisite

`2bu.2` (LCC graph capture) — done (commit `69330ea9f1`). LCC nodes are now in the graph and `cumulative_issue_cycles` walks through them naturally.

## Specific change

`Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py` ~lines 3754-3770:

CURRENT:
```python
finish = _mfma_finish_cycles_for(getattr(producer, "rocisa_inst", None))
expected = finish

if producer.body_label != consumer.body_label:
    body_delta = consumer.position.loop_index - producer.position.loop_index
    actual = abs(body_delta) * 1000
    return True, expected, actual

if graph is None:
    return False, expected, 0

actual = cumulative_issue_cycles(graph, producer, consumer)
return actual >= expected, expected, actual
```

TARGET:
```python
finish = _mfma_finish_cycles_for(getattr(producer, "rocisa_inst", None))
expected = finish

if graph is None:
    return False, expected, 0  # Strict: no graph -> conservative fail.

actual = cumulative_issue_cycles(graph, producer, consumer)
return actual >= expected, expected, actual
```

The cross-body branch goes away. `cumulative_issue_cycles` already supports cross-body walks (post-`2bu.2`), so the placeholder is no longer needed. Same-body and cross-body share the SAME code path.

## Tests to update

Update the 3 unit tests `x9i` added that pin the sentinel behavior. The MFMA->MFMA cross-body tests in `test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py::TestMFMAQuadCycleGap` need their assertions updated to assert the REAL cycle count from `cumulative_issue_cycles`, NOT `body_delta * 1000`. Document the new pinned values explicitly with arithmetic showing how the count was derived.

Add a NEW negative test: MFMA producer at the END of ML-1 with MFMA consumer at the START of ML, with intermediate instructions tight enough that the real cross-body cycle gap is BELOW `QUAD_CYCLES_STANDARD_MFMA_FINISH=3`. Assert `TimingTooCloseFailure` fires. This is the timing violation the placeholder was hiding.

## Production-code regression triage (CRITICAL)

Real-kernel captures (`test_ScheduleCapture.py::TestRealKernelCapture` and friends) may surface NEW `TimingTooCloseFailures` that the placeholder was hiding. **Each surfaced failure MUST be investigated and fixed.** No "fixture artifact, suppress it" escape hatch.

For each new failure:
1. Investigate the actual cross-body cycle gap.
2. If it's a real production timing bug (the schedule genuinely violates CDNA 4 ISA section 7.6 cycle requirements): fix the production code emitting that schedule. File a sibling bead if the fix is large enough to warrant separate review.
3. If the test fixture's expected behavior was wrong (e.g. the fixture set up an artificial schedule that wouldn't appear in real production): fix the fixture and document why.
4. Either way: the failure gets resolved in this bead's commit (or its sibling bead chain). It does NOT get suppressed.

## What stays UNCHANGED

- `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` and `_mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok` are handled by sibling beads `2bu.4` / `2bu.5` (which run in parallel).

## Why this is safe to land independently

Only one of three pair helpers changes. CVT->MFMA and PackMFMA->CVT1 paths still use their existing logic. If MFMA->MFMA cross-body real math surfaces a production bug, the blast radius is limited to that pair shape.

## Hard rule for the implementer

**ONE function, no branches on body_label.** The data structure already encodes execution order; the walker doesn't need to know which body a node belongs to. Any code that looks at `producer.body_label != consumer.body_label` to make a decision about cycle counting is now wrong.

title: Replace cross-body placeholder in _cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok (CVT->MFMA) with cumulative_issue_cycles
description:
## Sub-task of bead `2bu`

Replace BOTH branches of `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` (CVT->MFMA pair) with a single unified call to `cumulative_issue_cycles`. **This is the highest-impact placeholder removal** — per the `x9i` audit, every BF16/F8 production kernel triggers this branch (KernelWriter.py:5211 deepcopies main_loop into main_loop_prev, so any v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32 chain produces CVT-in-ML-1 -> MFMA-in-ML edges).

There should be ONE function that computes the actual cycle gap between two instructions. The cross-iteration distinction is a red herring; the graph has all instructions laid out in execution order regardless of which body they belong to.

## Pre-requisites

- `2bu.2` (LCC graph capture) — done (commit `69330ea9f1`).
- `2yk` (docstring lie cleanup) — done (commit `67d32c2c9f`).

## Specific change

`Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py` ~lines 3805-3835:

CURRENT (today's `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` has TWO different code paths — same-body uses slot-delta formula, cross-body uses `body_delta * 1000`):
```python
if producer.body_label != consumer.body_label:
    body_delta = consumer.position.loop_index - producer.position.loop_index
    actual = abs(body_delta) * 1000
    return True, expected, actual

# Same-body: slot-delta formula (NOT cumulative_issue_cycles)
slot_delta = consumer.position.vmfma_index - producer.position.vmfma_index
intervening = _count_intervening_instructions(producer, consumer, subj_graph)
actual = slot_delta * (1 + finish) - 1 + intervening
return actual >= expected, expected, actual
```

TARGET (one unified path):
```python
if subj_graph is None:
    return False, expected, 0  # Strict: no graph -> conservative fail.

actual = cumulative_issue_cycles(subj_graph, producer, consumer)
return actual >= expected, expected, actual
```

Both branches go away. Same-body and cross-body share the SAME code path. The slot-delta formula (the docstring-lie target of `2yk`) is deleted as a side effect.

The `_2yk` docstring update needs to be re-touched: the helper now ACTUALLY uses `cumulative_issue_cycles`. Update the docstring accordingly.

## Why the unification is safe

Per the `2yk` validation: the only difference between `cumulative_issue_cycles` and the slot-delta formula is MFMA-contention bookkeeping (`mfma_free_at`) and type-switch +1 stall — both gated on `is_mfma=True` for the producer. CVT producers have `is_mfma=False`, so those code paths add nothing for CVT->MFMA. **The two formulas produce the SAME numerical result for CVT->MFMA pairs.** Unification is purely a code-cleanup; no behavior change for the same-body case.

The cross-body case IS a behavior change: `body_delta * 1000` (always-pass) becomes a real cycle count.

## Tests to update

The 3 unit tests `x9i` added that pin the sentinel:
- `test_cvt_to_mfma_cross_body_actual_reflects_body_delta_sentinel`
- `test_cvt_to_mfma_cross_body_ml_to_ngl_also_uses_sentinel`
- `test_cvt_to_mfma_cross_body_helper_directly`

Update each to assert real cycle counts. Document the new pinned values explicitly with arithmetic showing how the count was derived.

Add a negative test: CVT producer at the END of ML-1 with MFMA consumer at the START of ML, intermediate instructions tight enough that the real gap is BELOW `QUAD_CYCLES_CVT_BEFORE_MFMA=2`. Assert `TimingTooCloseFailure` fires.

## Production-code regression triage (CRITICAL)

This is the path that fires on every BF16/F8 kernel. Real-kernel captures (`test_ScheduleCapture.py`) WILL surface new `TimingTooCloseFailures` that the placeholder was hiding. **Each surfaced failure MUST be investigated and fixed.** No "fixture artifact, suppress it" escape hatch.

For each new failure:
1. Investigate the actual cross-body cycle gap.
2. If it's a real production timing bug (the BF16/F8 kernel genuinely violates the 2-quad-cycle CVT->MFMA settle window): fix the production code emitting that schedule. File a sibling bead if the fix is large enough to warrant separate review.
3. If the test fixture's expected behavior was wrong: fix the fixture and document why.
4. Either way: the failure gets resolved. No suppression.

## What stays UNCHANGED

- `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` and `_mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok` are handled by sibling beads `2bu.3` / `2bu.5` (which run in parallel).

## Hard rule for the implementer

**ONE function, no branches on body_label.** The data structure already encodes execution order. Any code that looks at `producer.body_label != consumer.body_label` is now wrong. The slot-delta formula is deleted, not preserved.

## Why P2

Same as parent `2bu`. This is the load-bearing branch.

title: Replace cross-body placeholder in _mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok (PackMFMA->CVT1) with cumulative_issue_cycles
description:
## Sub-task of bead `2bu`

CURRENT:
```python
if producer.body_label != consumer.body_label:
    body_delta = consumer.position.loop_index - producer.position.loop_index
    actual = abs(body_delta) * 1000
    return True, expected, actual

# Same-body: cumulative_issue_cycles already used (per existing code).

```

```python
if graph is None:
    return False, expected, 0  # Strict: no graph -> conservative fail.

actual = cumulative_issue_cycles(graph, producer, consumer)
return actual >= expected, expected, actual
```

## Hard rule for the implementer

**ONE function, no branches on body_label.** The data structure already encodes execution order. Any code that looks at `producer.body_label != consumer.body_label` is now wrong.

title: Stop CMS schedule bodies from mutating kernel-level flags; move flag declarations into YAML/schedule-metadata
description:
## Background

CMS per-tile schedule body functions (Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/*.py) mutate kernel-level flags inside their function bodies during Solution.__init__ via hasCustomSchedule. Examples:

- _128x192x32_TF32.py:50-53 sets UsePLRPack=True, UseMFMAF32XEmulation=False, UseDot2F32XEmulation=False inside the TN branch.
- _192x128x32_TF32.py:45-49, _256x192x32_TF32.py:48-51, _256x128x32_TF32.py:48-51 do similar.
- Most of the gfx950 TF32 schedule bodies set UseMFMAF32XEmulation=True inside their bodies too (see grep in ldm5 audit).

## Problem (surfaced by ldm5, nyb5 Cycle 2, 3IJA §3.A)

The Approach A validator builds a non-CMS reference (UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=0) for comparison. That build short-circuits at dispatch.py:401-402 and NEVER runs the per-tile body, so it never sees the flag mutations. The two builds end up with inconsistent flag state, producing structural divergences that compare_graphs flags as residuals.

Concrete consequences observed:
- UsePLRPack mutation: GR-stream OrderInverted residuals (nyb5/p39d-class)
- UseMFMAF32XEmulation mutation: missing 4x4x4 MFMA helper identities in CMS capture vs ref (ldm5)
- UseDot2F32XEmulation mutation: not yet surfaced but same mechanism

## Test-site patches mask this in the runner

_3ija_residual_triage_runner.py now maintains _PER_TILE_REF_FLAG_OVERRIDES to mirror the body mutations onto the reference Solution._state post-construction (BEFORE _getKernelSource runs). This works as a triage workaround but:
- Has to be manually maintained as schedule bodies are added/edited.
- Doesn't fix the underlying contract violation: the schedule body is supposed to provide *scheduling content*, not mutate the kernel flag state out from under the Solution constructor.

## Proper fix

Move per-tile flag declarations OUT of the schedule body bodies and INTO the YAML side (or into the ScheduleMetadata / TileConfig registration) so:
1. Both the CMS Solution and the non-CMS reference Solution derive the flags identically from the same YAML/metadata source.
2. The schedule body is purely scheduling content — no side effects on kernel flag state.
3. The test-site override map in _3ija_residual_triage_runner.py can be deleted.

Concretely: each schedule body's flag mutation block should become a declarative field on RegisterSchedule (e.g. kernel_flag_overrides={'UseMFMAF32XEmulation': False, ...}) that the dispatch layer applies to the kernel dict at the same point hasCustomSchedule is called — but applies regardless of whether UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=1 or 0.

## Scope

All gfx950 schedule files that contain 'kernel[' mutations inside their function body. Sweep:

```
grep -rn 'kernel\[' Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/*.py
```

## Definition of done

- All kernel["..."] = ... mutations removed from CustomSchedule/gfx950/*.py schedule bodies.
- Flag declarations live on the RegisterSchedule decorator / a sibling metadata structure.
- Both Approach A reference and CMS build pick up the same flag state.
- _PER_TILE_REF_FLAG_OVERRIDES in _3ija_residual_triage_runner.py deletable; 3ija residual count for ldm5-class drops to 0 without the test-site patch.
- ldm5 closeable post-implementation.

## Related

- rocm-libraries-ldm5 (surfaced via UseMFMAF32XEmulation; test-site patch landed)
- rocm-libraries-p39d (surfaced via UsePLRPack; partly resolved by dfd8 source_module_id machinery, residual GR OrderInverted shape remains)
- rocm-libraries-nyb5 IMPLEMENTATION.md Cycle 2 surprise (same mechanism, different flag)
- Tensile/Components/3IJA_RESIDUAL_TRIAGE.md §3.A
- Tensile/Components/LDM5_INVESTIGATION.md §6 Option (ii)

Squash-merged into users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans as commit 5fbe10db5e4 (from 23 working commits on users/alvasile/2bww_option_c; side branch + worktrees cleaned up).

Definition-of-done met:

* Schedule bodies are PURE for the 5 target flags (UsePLRPack, SwapGlobalReadOrder, UseMFMAF32XEmulation, UseDot2F32XEmulation, MfmaInitCVgprs) — zero kernel[...] = ... writes anywhere in Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/*.py.
* @RegisterSchedule(required_flags={...}) declares per-branch flag preconditions on the decorator.
* wrapped_func in dispatch.py uniformly validates: any declared (flag, value) pair must match kernel state or schedule returns UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT. No allowlist.
* YAML is the source of truth for UsePLRPack and SwapGlobalReadOrder; framework derives the rest in Solution.py (UseMFMAF32XEmulation defaults True, framework only DISABLES for unsupported hardware; MfmaInitCVgprs and UseDot2F32XEmulation purely framework-derived).

title: Investigate: shadow default-capture sees CMS-mutated kernel dict (UsePLRPack etc.) — are we comparing against true Tensilelite default?
description:
**P0 — concrete evidence of validator-vs-reality mismatch as of 2026-05-11.**

## TL;DR

The validator's reference graph is NOT a faithful image of any real Tensile-emitted kernel. Empirically:

- **cms.s graph order ↔ kernel_cms.s emission order: PERFECT MATCH** (instruction-by-instruction, MAINLOOP body, lined up).
- **default.s graph order ↔ kernel_default.s emission order: DOES NOT MATCH** (different shape entirely — the shadow records a Pack-front-loaded, double-tagged sequence; real default Tensile emits per-mfmaIndex Pack/MFMA-interleaved chunks).

So the validator passes `compare_graphs(ref, subj)` against a fictional `ref` that no real build would produce. `subj` (cms.s) is real; `ref` (default.s) is a shadow extraction shaped by CMS-mutated kernel flags.

## Reproducing the evidence

Run the dump script (already in-tree, untracked → committed via this bead update):

```bash
cd projects/hipblaslt && \
  python -m pytest tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/_dump_carveout_assembly.py -s -v \
    --ignore=tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/test_MatrixInstructionConversion.py
```

Produces FOUR side-by-side artifacts in `tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/`:

- `kernel_cms.s` — REAL Tensile assembly with `UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=1` (CMS path; the kernel the assembler actually consumes for this tile in production).
- `kernel_default.s` — REAL Tensile assembly with `UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=0` (CMS dispatch bypassed; closest thing to native default Tensilelite emit for the same problem).
- `cms.s` — graph view of the validator's CMS subject capture (`subj_graph`), per body, in stream-position order.
- `default.s` — graph view of the validator's shadow default capture (`ref_graph`), per body, in stream-position order.

The script source: `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/_dump_carveout_assembly.py` (committed alongside this bead update).

Investigator should diff:
1. `cms.s` mainloop body vs `kernel_cms.s` MAINLOOP macro body (line ~1846+) — should be 1:1.
2. `default.s` body ML-1/ML head (line 1+) vs `kernel_default.s` Unrolled Loop body (line ~1834+) — will diverge by structure, not just by ordering.

## Specific evidence beyond the prior framing

The earlier description (above this update) framed the problem as 'shadow shares the kernel dict so flags differ from non-CMS Tensile.' Today's evidence sharpens this:

1. **The shadow capture itself records the same physical instruction TWICE under two different category names.** Lines 4-15 of `default.s` show identical `v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32` text rendered at `stream_index=1` (cat=PackA3) AND `stream_index=2` (cat=PackA0), `stream_index=3` (PackA3) AND `stream_index=4` (PackA0), etc. This is the LRSwap/Pack-style category-tagging divergence (cf. `Z012_ALTERNATIVE_FIXES_INVESTIGATION.md`) hitting the shadow capture itself. Two implications:
   - The shadow's data-flow node count is inflated relative to anything a real default-emit would produce (we observed default ML-1 = 242 data-flow nodes vs CMS ML-1 = 184 nodes — a 58-node delta from a kernel that's supposed to differ ONLY in scheduling, not in instruction count).
   - The reference graph is not the shape of any real kernel; it's an internal artifact of the CMS-side category-tagging machinery interacting with default-emit's append path.

2. **The CMS-side capture IS faithful.** `cms.s` body ML stream_index 0..16 matches `kernel_cms.s` MAINLOOP mfmaIndex:0..3 chunks line-for-line. The slot-lex sort `(slot.mfma_index, slot.sequence)` does correctly recover CMS emission order. So the brokenness is on the reference side only — the validator IS evaluating real CMS-emit, but against a fiction.

## Bead conclusion (raised priority)

This is no longer 'a concern worth investigating.' It's 'the validator's premise is broken in a way we can demonstrate with two file diffs.' Bumping P2 → P0. Decisions needed BEFORE any further validator hardening lands:

1. What is the validator's intended contract? (Three candidates: (a) 'CMS preserves what a real non-CMS Tensile build would emit for this problem'; (b) 'CMS-emit and default-emit produce equivalent dataflow when given identical kernel flags'; (c) something else.) The current code does NEITHER (a) NOR (b) cleanly — it's closer to (b) but the shadow capture has artifacts that distort even that comparison.
2. If we want (a), how do we get a true non-CMS reference into the validator? The dump script's two-build approach (one with UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=0) is one way; another would be capturing from a real second build at a different code path.
3. If we want (b), we need to fix the shadow's category-tagging to not double-record the same physical instruction, AND make sure the slot indexing is consistent between the shadow's append path and the CMS schedule registration.

## Original concern (kept for context — see also `PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §'Concrete in-tree divergence')

`enable_capture_default_schedule()` (`Tensile/KernelWriter.py:478`) does NOT rebuild the kernel with different flags. It just sets `self.states._captureDefaultSchedule = True` after `setupNewTile` returns, telling the writer to ALSO emit into a shadow `FourPartCapture` while a single kernel build runs. There is one `kernel` dict, one `_initKernel`, one set of mutations. Whatever the CMS schedule registration mutated on the kernel dict — e.g. `kernel["UsePLRPack"] = True` set at `Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/_128x128x32_TF32.py:120` (and similarly across ~20 other per-tile schedules) — is what BOTH the CMS-emission path and the shadow default-emission path see.

Concrete example (canonical TF32 4x4 TN kernel, MatrixInstruction=[16,16,32,1,1,4,4,2,2], TLDS=1, useLDSTr=0):
- Dispatch matches `@RegisterSchedule` decorator on `_get_schedule_128x128x32_TF32` (`_128x128x32_TF32.py:35`); MacroTile=128x128, MI=[16,16,32], MIWG=[2,2], DepthU=32 all align.
- TN/TLDS=1/no-useLDSTr branch (line 52) sets `UseMFMAF32XEmulation=True`; line 120 sets `UsePLRPack=True` and `MfmaInitCVgprs=True`.

## Pointers

- Capture entry: `Tensile/KernelWriter.py:478` (`enable_capture_default_schedule`)
- Capture flag check sites: `Tensile/KernelWriter.py:3766, 4418, 4450, 4544, 4571, 4756, 4980, 5080, 5138, 5296`
- Schedule mutation (this canonical kernel): `Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/_128x128x32_TF32.py:120`
- Default-baseline: `Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/dispatch.py:546` initializes `UsePLRPack=False`
- Existing memo: `Tensile/Components/PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §'Concrete in-tree divergence: UsePLRPack' (lines ~329-346)
- Dump script (THIS bead's evidence generator): `Tensile/Tests/unit/_dump_carveout_assembly.py`
- Test it builds on: `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_cross_subiter_alu_carveout_real_kernel.py`

## Out of scope for THIS bead
Implementation. Decisions and direction first. The dump artifacts (`cms.s`, `default.s`, `kernel_cms.s`, `kernel_default.s`) are regenerable on demand; do NOT commit them — only the script that produces them is committed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Cross-link: rocm-libraries-oram.1 (body_label-sensitivity in compare_graphs)

Filed sibling bead `rocm-libraries-oram.1` (P1, question, child of `rocm-libraries-oram`): "Investigate compare_graphs body_label-sensitivity for cross-body pipelining (UsePLRPack)".

That bead documents that `compare_graphs` builds identity tuples that bake `body_label` into identity (`(class_tag, loop_index, canonical_render)` at `ScheduleCapture.py:507-536`), and edge_keys further encode `loop_index` via `producer.position` (`CMSValidator.py:1238`). When dataflow-equivalent producers drift across bodies (e.g., a Pack producer in PRO body on the CMS+UsePLRPack=True side vs ML/ML-1 body on the default+UsePLRPack=False side), `compare_graphs` fires spurious failures despite the dataflow being identical. title: Final pass on validator design doc (revise interim draft after all refactors land)
description:
## Why this exists

This bead has been **re-scoped (2026-05-06)**. An interim draft of the validator design doc was produced ahead of schedule at commit `60ab43850e` (`Tensile/Components/VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md`, 489 lines / ~3,121 words) so the design surface is documented while the validator is mid-refactor.

**This bead now tracks the FINAL pass:** revising that interim draft once every open refactor / cleanup epic has landed. The interim doc explicitly notes which line citations and import paths are mid-migration; the final pass corrects those, locks the architecture description against the post-refactor surface, and removes any "interim" framing.

## Pre-requisites (the "very end" condition)

Run after ALL of these close. The interim draft was produced before any of them landed; the final pass is what makes the doc match the real final surface.

- `br4` — CMS validator consolidation epic (10 sub-beads). After this lands, every symbol the interim doc cites in `ScheduleCapture.py` will live in `CMSValidator.py` instead. Citations need full re-verification.
- `nn0` — methods-on-classes refactor. May rename/relocate functions cited in §7.
- `c70` — Register abstraction class. Changes how register identity is described in §4 (Invariants) and §7 (Key technical details).
- `09y` — naming-quality pass. May rename files (`CMSValidator.py`, `ScheduleCapture.py`) and audit reports referenced in the doc.
- `l6q` — multi-ISA framework placeholder; may close without code (see its done definition).
- `yvx` — mock-instruction infrastructure scalability.
- Any other open refactor/cleanup bead at execution time. Re-evaluate the open-bead list before dispatching.

If a bead opens AFTER the interim draft but BEFORE the final pass, the executor should consider whether it changes the validator's described surface; if yes, defer the final pass.

## What the final pass does

1. **Read the interim doc** at `Tensile/Components/VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md`. Treat it as a starting outline, not a finished product.
2. **Re-verify every file:line citation** against the post-refactor source. The interim doc explicitly flags these as mid-migration.
3. **Update Status section** — drop the "interim, 2026-05-06" framing; replace with "current as of <commit>".
4. **Re-evaluate Future Work (§8)** — most of the beads listed there will be closed by the time this runs. Drop closed-bead refs; keep only genuinely open future work.
5. **Adopt the persona** described below (verbatim from the original framing) and apply the house-style pass: short sentences, concrete examples, no AI tropes, no ceremony.
6. **Length budget:** stay in the 5–10 page target. The interim doc is at 489 lines (~9 pages); the final pass should not bloat it.

## Persona for the dispatched agent

> You are an EXPERT technical writer AND an experienced staff software engineer with 15+ years of compiler / scheduler / validator domain expertise. You write design docs that engineers actually read — every section earns its place, every paragraph has a point, every diagram conveys something a paragraph couldn't.
>
> Your house style: short sentences, concrete examples over abstract description, cite line numbers where it helps the reader navigate to the live code, never restate what the code already shows. You are allergic to corporate documentation tropes ("In this section we will discuss..."), bullet-list hedging ("might, could, may"), and decorative ASCII art.
>
> Your audience: a new engineer joining the project who has never seen this codebase but is competent in Python and familiar with compiler scheduling concepts. They will read this document ONCE and need to navigate the live code afterward.

## Required document structure (preserved from interim — do not reinvent)

1. **Executive summary** (≤ 1 page) — what the validator does, what problem it solves, the core architectural choice, and the bottom line for someone deciding whether to read further.
2. **Goals** — numbered, concrete, testable. Explicit out-of-scope items.
3. **High-level approach** — the two-phase model: build a unified dataflow graph + per-edge wait coverage. Diagram acceptable if it conveys something a paragraph couldn't.
4. **Invariants leveraged** — each invariant: state it, cite where enforced (file:line), state the violation consequence.
5. **Assumptions made** — what the validator REQUIRES of inputs but does not enforce.
6. **Scope** — covered vs. not-covered table.
7. **Key technical details** — the non-obvious mechanics. Each item: what it is, why it exists, where it lives.
8. **Future work** — ≤ 1 paragraph + bead links for genuinely open items only.

## What this document is NOT

- A history of the migration (commit messages and beads cover that).
- A line-by-line code walkthrough (the code documents itself; this doc cites it).
- A user manual for `pytest Tensile/Tests/unit/`.
- A roadmap of unfinished work (use beads).
- Anyone's pet-feature pitch.

## Where the document lives

`Tensile/Components/VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md` (already exists from the interim draft — overwrite, don't add a sibling). Plain markdown.

## Verification

The design doc has no tests. Quality is reviewed by the user. Acceptance criteria:

1. A new engineer can read sections 1–3 in 10 minutes and understand what the validator does.
2. They can navigate to any subsystem they care about via §7's file:line citations — verify each citation post-refactor.
3. No section reads like AI-generated boilerplate. No section restates what other sections already said.
4. Total length: 5–10 pages of plain markdown. Longer is a smell.
5. No "interim" framing remains; no references to mid-migration state.

## Hard rules for the dispatching agent

- The agent must be Opus with the persona prompt verbatim.
- No diagrams unless they convey something a paragraph wouldn't.
- The agent must read the live source — the doc must cite real file:line, not invented references.
- The agent overwrites `VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md` in place; single commit on the long-term branch.
- Run `br list --status open` first; if non-doc refactor beads remain open AND change the validator's surface, defer.

## Why P2

The validator is core infrastructure. Without an accurate, up-to-date design doc, every new contributor has to grep beads + commits. P2 reflects "important but not blocking active work."

## Related (final pass — most will be closed by then)

All open beads as of execution time. Update this list when running.

## Interim draft — for reference

- Doc: `Tensile/Components/VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md`
- Commit: `60ab43850e`
- Produced by: an Opus subagent on 2026-05-06, executing this bead's spec against the validator at commit `18cbf1e59b` (post br4.1 + br4.2, pre br4.3..br4.10).
- Tricky sections noted by the interim author: §4 (Invariants) and §7.5 (pair-specific quad-cycle helpers) — the dispatch-order reasoning for PackMFMA→CVTPack vs. generic MFMA-producer is mid-migration; the interim doc grounded the explanation in live in-line comments at `_classify_edge_coverage:4438,4458,4483` rather than guessing the post-consolidation shape. The final pass should re-derive these against the post-br4 layout.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: Fix _cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok docstring lie (claims cycle-exact, isn't)
description:
## Discovered by

Bead `c44` end-to-end verification (critical-eye pass on docstrings).

## The lie

`_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` docstring at `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:3787` claims:

> Approach: CYCLE-EXACT via `cumulative_issue_cycles`

But the actual implementation at `ScheduleCapture.py:3811-3832` uses the slot-delta formula `slot_delta * (1 + finish) - 1 + intervening` and **never calls `cumulative_issue_cycles`**. The other two pair helpers (`_quad_cycle_gap_ok`, `_mfma_pack_to_cvt_gap_ok`) DO call it.

This means CVT->MFMA timing is not actually MFMA-contention-aware (no `mfma_free_at` gating, no type-switch +1 stalls in this path). For pure CVT producers the gating may not matter — but the docstring will mislead the next reader.

## Action

Rewrite `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` docstring (`ScheduleCapture.py:3787`) to honestly describe the slot-delta formula it uses, and explain WHY this helper diverges from the cycle-exact pair helpers (e.g. CVT producers don't compete for MFMA issue slots, so the contention model is simpler).

Optionally: convert the slot-delta math in `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` to actually call `cumulative_issue_cycles` for consistency. This is a separate, larger change — file as follow-up if pursued.

## Why P3

Pure documentation defect — no runtime behavior bug. Easy fix; matters for future readers of the quad-cycle code.

## Related

- `034` — stale cmw-formula docstrings in test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py (same doc-rot family, split for per-item bead tracking).
- `c44` — verification bead that surfaced the lie.

title: Validator equivalence for variable-width LR/LW (same data, different op shape)
description:
## Why this exists

Today the validator distinguishes between scheduled LR/LW shapes by operation count and width. Two graphs that load (or store) the same logical data via different decompositions compare as different:

```
2x LR (b64 each) -> SWait(dscnt=0) -> MFMA
1x LR (b128)     -> SWait(dscnt=0) -> MFMA
```

If both forms read the **same 128 bits** into the **same MFMA-input register range** with the **same wait coverage**, the validator should treat the graphs as equivalent. Today it surfaces them as a topology divergence (or worse, a wait-coverage failure if the dscnt accounting differs between the two shapes).

This matters because:

- **CMS scheduler experimentation** — the scheduler may legitimately choose between equivalent decompositions based on memory-latency / register-pressure heuristics. Comparing two scheduler runs of the same kernel should not flag the choice itself as a divergence.
- **SIA0-vs-SIA3 comparison** (the long-term goal in `5gd`) — different scheduling algorithms will frequently pick different op widths for the same data movement. Width-blind comparison is required for that comparison to be meaningful.
- **Codegen-vs-codegen comparison** — register allocator + LDS layout decisions can change op widths between two compilations of the same kernel.

**The same problem applies symmetrically to LW** (Local Write) instructions, with the additional wrinkle that LWs can be reordered around their consumer's address calculations.

## Why this is hard / why it's an epic

This is **not** a register-renaming problem (that's `wx9.3`). It's a **semantic-equivalence-modulo-decomposition** problem. To recognize the two shapes above as equivalent, the validator needs to:

1. Reason about which physical bytes are being moved (LDS offset + width per op, NOT just register names).
2. Reason about which destination register bytes receive those bytes.
3. Reason about whether the consumer (MFMA) is invariant to the decomposition choice (it usually is, but register-class / alignment constraints can break this).
4. Reason about wait-counter accounting across decompositions: 1x b128 contributes 1 to dscnt; 2x b64 contributes 2. The validator currently checks "dscnt drained to 0 before consumer" which is invariant — but tighter checks ("dscnt drained to N at point P") would diverge.
5. Decide whether this is configurable (strict mode = exact decomposition, relaxed mode = width-equivalent) or always-on.

Each of these is its own investigation. Hence: epic with sub-beads.

## Pre-implementation requirement

**Discuss with the user before any implementation work.** This is exactly the kind of feature that's easy to over-design. Before writing canonicalization code, agree on:

- What "equivalent" means in scope (just decomposition? or also reordering of independent LWs? or also memory-aliased LR/LW pairs?).
- Whether width equivalence is always-on or behind a comparison-mode flag.
- Which consumer types invalidate equivalence (MFMA register-class constraints; CVT operand alignment; etc.).
- Where in the pipeline normalization happens (pre-graph during construction, or post-graph during comparison).

Expect 1-2 design-review iterations with the user before Phase 6.

## Sub-bead structure

1. **Brainstorm + design alignment with user.** Define semantic equivalence; agree on scope; pick the configurable-vs-always-on policy.
2. **Assembly-level inventory.** What do real `ds_read_b32` / `b64` / `b128` and `ds_write_*` instructions look like at the GCN level? What register-class / alignment constraints apply?
3. **Enumerate valid decompositions.** Which splits/merges preserve semantics? Alignment, ordering, swizzling — what can vary, what can't?
4. **Consumer-invariance audit.** For each consumer type (MFMA flavors, CVT, Pack, scalar usage), determine when it cares about decomposition and when it doesn't.
5. **LW symmetric case.** Same question for writes — including the additional question of whether independent LWs can be reordered.
6. **Design proposal.** Pre-graph normalization vs post-graph canonicalization; data structures; comparison-mode flag plumbing. Discuss with user before implementing.
7. **Implementation.** Only after design alignment.
8. **Tests + documentation.** Pin equivalence + non-equivalence pairs; document the rules.

## Open questions to surface during sub-bead 1

- What happens when the two sides have **different LDS-buffer layouts** but conceptually load the same logical data? Is that in scope?
- What about **coalesced** vs **scalarized** LDS access (one wide op vs many narrow ops staggered across waves)? The latter is rare in CMS but possible in codegen.
- Does this interact with **SwapGlobalRead** / **PrefetchLocalRead** transforms that change LR ordering?
- Should the validator surface "equivalent under width-relaxation" as a distinct outcome (not failure, not strict-pass), so the user can see a width difference happened without it being an error?

## Risks

- **Over-fitting.** It's easy to build a width-equivalence engine that handles every edge case in 5000 lines of code; it's hard to build one that handles the 80% case in 500 lines and acknowledges the rest as "outside scope; surface as divergence with explanation". Discuss with user which point on that curve we want.
- **Consumer constraints** (register-class alignment, MFMA operand layout) can silently invalidate "equivalent" decompositions. Building this without an exhaustive consumer audit risks false equivalences — i.e. reporting "match" when the kernels actually do different things.
- **Wait-counter accounting under decomposition.** dscnt counts the number of ops, not the bytes. If consumer-side accounting changes meaning under decomposition, every wait-coverage rule needs auditing.

## Related beads

- `wx9.3` — register-name canonicalization. **Foundational.** Width equivalence layers on top: it assumes you can already compare graphs that differ only in register names. This bead probably gates on `wx9.3` being implemented.
- `5gd` — Timeline interface refactor. Width equivalence is best implemented at the Timeline level (after CMS-shape decoupling), not in the CMS-specific path. Likely gates on `5gd.A.4` (validator routes through Timeline).
- `WX93_RESEARCH_REPORT.md` — note that the report's recommended algorithm (SSA value-numbering + 1-WL) handles renaming but does NOT handle width equivalence. This bead is the next layer up.

## Why P3

Strategic, research-heavy, not gating current work. The bead `5gd` tree should land first; this work is a natural extension once codegen-comparison is real.

title: rocm-libraries-udqg root-cause description is empirically wrong: SHADOW/CMS name_to_idx are IDENTICAL, only 9/192 extra SHADOW edges are sentinel-byte-key, and Approach E DOES fix the divergence (0 mismatches on both failing fixtures)
description:
## Summary

The `rocm-libraries-udqg` bead (filed by the n7og investigation) describes the SHADOW-vs-CMS edge_keys divergence mechanism INCORRECTLY. Its load-bearing claims are empirically refuted by direct inspection of the failing fixtures. As a result, the recommended fix direction is wrong and the rejection of Approach E is unfounded.

## Empirical findings (verified on `bpg11-tf32-4x4-tn` and `oplb-tf32-6x8-tn`)

Inspecting SHADOW and CMS DataflowGraphs directly via writer._last_default_capture / _last_cms_capture (BPG#11 fixture, MI=16x16x32 4x4, UsePLRPack+UseMFMAF32XEmulation, F32XdlMathOp='X'):

| metric | SHADOW | CMS |
|---|---|---|
| total edges | 647 | 471 |
| edges with `(-1)` sentinel in producer byte-key | **9** | **1** |
| pack→MFMA edges total | 416 | 224 |
| pack→MFMA with sentinel producer byte-key | **9** | **1** |
| extra-in-SHADOW pack→MFMA edges | 192 | — |
| extra-in-SHADOW edges with **numeric** byte-keys | **184** | — |
| extra-in-SHADOW edges with **sentinel** byte-keys | **8** | — |

**Implication:** Of the 192 extra-in-SHADOW edges, only ~4% have the sentinel byte-key the udqg bead identifies as the root cause. The other ~96% have numeric VGPR byte-keys like `(('v', 31),)`, `(('v', 32),)`, `(('v', 33),)`, `(('v', 34),)` — fully resolved, not sentinel-collapsed.

## SHADOW vs CMS `name_to_idx` are IDENTICAL

Direct comparison of `LoopBodyCapture.name_to_idx` on every body (PRO, ML-1, ML, NGL, NLL) for the BPG#11 fixture:

```
SHADOW PRO/ML-1/ML/NGL/NLL all have:
    ValuA_T0_I0=76
    ValuA_X0_I0=-1  (sentinel)
    ValuA_X0_I0_BASE=-1  (sentinel)
    ValuB_T0_I0=92
    ValuB_X0_I0=31
    ValuB_X0_I0_BASE=31

CMS PRO/ML-1/ML/NGL/NLL: IDENTICAL VALUES.
```

CMS has the SAME sentinel for `ValuA_X0_I0=-1` as SHADOW does. The bead's claim that "SHADOW's `LoopBodyCapture.name_to_idx` is MISSING the bindings for `ValuA_X0_I0`, `ValuA_T0_I0`, `ValuB_X0_I0`, `ValuB_T0_I0`" is empirically false:

- `ValuA_T0_I0` is bound to 76 in BOTH SHADOW and CMS.
- `ValuB_T0_I0` is bound to 92 in BOTH.
- `ValuB_X0_I0` is bound to 31 in BOTH.
- `ValuA_X0_I0` is `-1` (sentinel) in BOTH.

The harvest pipeline (`collect_regset_stream`, ScheduleCapture.py:2293 — bead misnames it `harvest_name_to_idx`) produces the SAME table for SHADOW and CMS. Whatever the divergence cause is, it is NOT name_to_idx asymmetry.

## Approach E (byte-key matching) DOES fix the divergence

Bead claims: "Verified Approach-E byte-key matching ... does NOT fix this — it ALSO collapses on the bad sentinel key."

Empirical test (build SHADOW and CMS DataflowGraphs, compare on `(producer_write_byte_key, consumer_read_byte_key, edge_kind)` basis instead of identity-tuple basis):

| fixture | SHADOW byte-key set | CMS byte-key set | SHADOW \ CMS | CMS \ SHADOW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bpg11-tf32-4x4-tn | 139 | 139 | **0** | **0** |
| oplb-tf32-6x8-tn | 255 | 255 | **0** | **0** |

**All 192 "extra-in-SHADOW" edges on bpg11 have a byte-key equivalent in CMS** (matched=192, unmatched=0). Approach E byte-key matching would fully resolve the divergence, contrary to the bead.

## What the divergence actually is

The two graphs are emitting the SAME logical edges with the SAME byte-key footprints but DIFFERENT canonical_render strings (n7og's original framing). The identity-tuple in `edge_keys()` (CMSValidator.py:1300-1303) embeds `producer.identity` which embeds `canonical_render` — so two edges that name the same physical register via different syntactic operand-numbering conventions (e.g. SHADOW renders `vgprValuB_X0_I0+0` vs CMS rendering as `vgprValuB_X0_I0+24`, both resolving to the same VGPR) produce DIFFERENT identity tuples and thus DIFFERENT edge_keys — even though they describe the same dataflow.

## Why this matters

1. **udqg's acceptance criterion** requires SHADOW byte_keys to be NUMERIC (not sentinel) on the failing fixtures. They ALREADY ARE numeric on 184/192 of the failing-fixture extra edges. The acceptance criterion is misaimed.
2. **udqg's rejection of Approach E** is unfounded — Approach E genuinely fixes both failing fixtures.
3. **The principled fix (a)** the bead recommends ("extend SHADOW harvest pipeline so name_to_idx is populated for ALL ValuA/B X*/T* registers") will not help: both pipelines already produce identical name_to_idx, and only 9 of 192 failing edges have sentinel byte-keys.
4. The actual fix surface is Approach E (or equivalent: making `edge_keys()` allocation-invariant) — exactly what n7og originally proposed.

## Verified via

- Diagnostic harness reproduced under the n7og worktree (`.claude/worktrees/n7og-impl/projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite`).
- Direct introspection of `DataflowEdge.producer_write_byte_key`, `consumer_read_byte_key`, and `LoopBodyCapture.name_to_idx` on the two failing fixtures.
- Custom byte-key edge-set comparison shows 0 mismatches on both fixtures.

## Recommended action

1. Update `rocm-libraries-udqg`: correct the root-cause description (it is NOT missing name_to_idx bindings; it IS allocation-variant canonical_render in identity-tuple edge_keys). Update the acceptance criteria to align with the actual mechanism.

title: Quad-cycle Sub-B: CVTPack -> MFMA 2-cycle settle in graph
description:
## Rule

`QUAD_CYCLES_CVT_BEFORE_MFMA = 2` (CMSValidator.py:275). CVT packs
(`v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32` and friends, validator class `CVTPack`) need 2
quad-cycles before a downstream MFMA can use their result.

## Currently checked at

`CMSValidator.py:1786-1788` sets `pack.min_quad_cycles_before_result_used = 2`
for `CVTPack`. `Pack.validate` (CMSValidator.py:423-429) compares
against `estimated_quad_cycles_before_result_used` populated by
`estimate_quad_cycles` (CMSValidator.py:2701-2759, which calls
`precompute_issue_times` at 2742 and walks `pack.needed_by`).

## Migration

1. Identify the graph edge: CVTPack writes a vgpr that the next MFMA
   reads. The per-byte resolver should emit this RAW edge naturally
   provided register flow is captured. Verify with a fixture
   (CVTPack writing v[0:1], MFMA reading v[0:1]).
2. Inside `_classify_edge_coverage`, add a new branch BEFORE the
   ALU-producer exemption (`_is_alu_producer` returns True for any
   "Pack*" category, including CVTPack — that's where it currently
   gets silently skipped):

   ```python
   if _is_cvt_pack(p_node):
       expected = 2
       actual = _actual_gap(p_node, c_node, num_mfma_per_subiter)
       if actual < expected:
           return [TimingTooCloseFailure(producer=p_node, consumer=c_node,
                                          expected_quad_cycles=expected,
                                          actual_quad_cycles=actual)]
       return []
   ```
3. `_is_cvt_pack(node)` helper: dispatch on node.category startswith "Pack"
   AND wrapped instruction class is `VCvtPkF32toBF16` (or whatever the
   exact rocisa class is — confirm against `PACK_TYPE_MAP` at
   CMSValidator.py:660ish).
4. Issue-cycle estimation: same slot-delta formula as `_quad_cycle_gap_ok`,
   but the producer's "finish cycles" for CVT is 0 (CVT issues + finishes
   in one cycle on the vector ALU). actual_qc = slot_delta - 1.
5. Add `TestCVTPackQuadCycleGap` in `test_dataflow_graph_register_gaps.py`.

## Open question

How does the structural side measure the gap between a CVTPack and its
MFMA consumer? `precompute_issue_times` walks the entire timeline
including SWaitCnt stalls. Can the slot-delta-only graph approximation
under-estimate (false fail) or over-estimate (false pass)? See umbrella
bead Q6.

## Files

- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1786-1788` — current site
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:434-436` — CVTPack class
- `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ValidatePack.py:578` — TimingTooCloseFailure assertion (CVT case)
