title: 5gd.B.1: Source-aware Failure rendering (tagged_inst + position + other CMS-flavored fields)
description:
## Parent: 5gd Part B — label policy

Make Failure-message rendering source-aware end-to-end. The rendering policy lives at the timeline-construction site (each source provides its own renderers); Failure formatters consume whatever shape the timeline carries without per-source branching.

## Scope of source-aware rendering

ALL Failure-message components that name source-specific concepts must dispatch through source-aware renderers. Concretely:

- **`tagged_inst` rendering** (the instruction label):
  - CMS source returns `LRA0[12]`-style category labels.
  - Codegen-asm source returns `mnemonic + operands` (e.g. `buffer_load_dword v[34], s[16:19], 0 offen offset:128`).

- **Position rendering** (currently `format_position` / the `@ idx={vmfma_index}` strings, e.g. CMSValidator.py:2327):
  - CMS source: `@ idx=N` where N is the MFMA-slot index (the existing semantic).
  - Codegen-asm source: native asm position (line number or instruction offset in the assembly stream — codegen knows what the right shape is). Don't fake `@ idx=N` for asm — it has no MFMA-slot concept and the lie surfaces in failure messages.

- **Other CMS-flavored Failure fields**: audit `wait_idx`, `iter_delta`, and any other component currently named in CMS-y terms (`vmfma_index`, `loop_index`, etc.) appearing on `MissingWaitFailure`, `WaitInsufficientFailure`, `OrderInvertedFailure`, etc. Either (a) they're position-derived and inherit the position-rendering fix above, or (b) they need their own source-aware dispatch. The audit step decides which.

The goal: a developer reading a Failure for an asm-source comparison should see asm-native labels and asm-native positions everywhere; a developer reading a Failure for a CMS-source comparison should see the existing `LRA0[12] @ idx=37` format unchanged.

## Concrete tasks

1. Audit current label rendering: where do `_node_label`, `_node_with_pos`, `format_position`, and the per-Failure `_format_canonical` methods consume CMS-flavored fields (`tagged_inst`, `vmfma_index`, `loop_index`, etc.)? Produce a complete list — every site that mentions a CMS-y name must be either (a) routed through a source-aware renderer or (b) explicitly justified as source-agnostic.
2. Define the contract: `tagged_inst.render() -> str` Protocol AND a position-rendering Protocol (e.g. `position.render() -> str` on the position object, OR a `render_position(timeline_event) -> str` callable held alongside other renderers).
3. CMS implementation returns existing-shape labels and positions (so all current pinning tests pass byte-identical).
4. Codegen-asm implementation returns mnemonic + operands for instructions, and asm-native location for positions. `assembly_to_timeline` (`x6s` / `f3kb`) chooses the position semantic.
5. Keep `[N]` indexing for both `tagged_inst` labels (per prior feedback: user schedules by index, not by class).
6. Verify all existing CMS failure-message pinning tests pass byte-identical (CMS rendering must not regress).
7. Add at least one round-trip test for the codegen-asm renderers: build a Timeline via the asm bridge, force a Failure, assert the rendered message uses asm-native shape (not CMS).

## Depends on

5gd.A.1 (TimelineEvent design — both Protocols need the field shape).

## Done when

- Source-aware rendering works for ALL Failure-message components for both bridges (tagged_inst, position, plus any other CMS-flavored field surfaced by task 1).
- No per-source branching in formatters — they invoke the renderer Protocols and have no idea what source emitted the timeline.
- All existing CMS pinning tests pass byte-identical.
- A new asm-source pinning test confirms asm-native rendering end-to-end.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: RDNA3.5 §7.6 VOPD pair-formation hard-rule validator (correctness-critical)
description:
## Why

s5g1 ISA audit (memo `Tensile/Components/ISA_GAP_GENERALIZATION_AUDIT.md` commit `6b0c401f2d9`) flagged that **RDNA3.5 §7.6 VOPD pair-formation rules R-4 through R-7 are HARD RULES** — the ISA documentation explicitly states 'hardware does not function correctly' if violated. Not a performance hint; a correctness invariant.

If/when the kernel emitter ever produces VOPD instructions targeting gfx1151, the validator must check pair-formation invariants or risk silently emitting kernels that compute wrong results.

## Scope (~150 LoC)

1. Read RDNA3.5 ISA §7.6 R-4 through R-7. Capture each invariant as a plain-language predicate.
2. Add a new validator pass (sibling to `compare_graphs` and `validate_edge_wait_coverage`): `validate_vopd_pair_formation(graph)`.
3. The pass walks every VOPD instruction in the graph and asserts each R-4..R-7 predicate. Each violation produces a new `VopdPairFormationFailure` (or similar) with which rule + which pair + why.
4. Wire the pass into the existing validator entry point (alongside the other passes).
5. Tests: per R-4..R-7 rule, one positive (compliant pair, validator passes) + one negative (violating pair, expected Failure shape).
6. Documentation in VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md noting this is a correctness pass, not a perf pass.

## Why this is correctness-critical, not perf

VOPD pair-formation rules are non-negotiable hardware constraints. If a kernel emitter generates a violating pair, the GPU produces wrong results — silently. There is no cycle-gap soft-fail equivalent here; everything is a hard fail.

If the kernel emitter today does not produce VOPD, this bead is dormant. The moment it starts (e.g. for any RDNA3.5 perf push), this validator becomes a SHIPPING GATE.

## Sequencing

- Independent of the other s5g1 follow-up beads — VOPD validation is a separate code path.
- Can land before or after `rdna35-arch-profile-stub` (different concern).

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.**
- No fallback paths or 'tolerate this' carve-outs. Every R-4..R-7 violation is hard-fail.

## References

- `/home/alvasile/ISAs/RDNA3.5.txt` §7.6 — primary source.
- `Tensile/Components/ISA_GAP_GENERALIZATION_AUDIT.md` — discovery memo.

title: Worktree-rebuilt rocisa produces different MFMA_4x4 to CVT_PACK timing than the cached May 26 build_tmp binary
description:
Surfaced during C4 (rocm-libraries-5ryl) verification. When rocisa is force-reinstalled from source via 'pip install -e ./rocisa' from the worktree, several real-kernel tests start producing 24 TimingTooCloseFailure entries at KernelWriter.py:6311 (wait-coverage assertion in kernelBody). The pre-compiled build_tmp binary from May 26 used by the C3h baseline run did NOT produce these failures.

Root cause hypothesis: the rocisa rebuild produces materially different output for MFMA_4x4 -> CVT_PACK pack timing in this TF32 fixture (PackA0[5]->PackA0[6], PackB0[5]->PackB0[6] etc., need 5 quad-cycles per the validator's timing rule but only 0-4 are guaranteed by the rebuild's instruction layout).

Affects roughly 10+ real-kernel tests in test_ScheduleCapture.py + test_cross_subiter_alu_carveout_real_kernel.py::test_real_kernel_validates_clean_with_carveout_engaged.

Why this matters: this divergence either indicates (a) the cached binary had a stale-but-passing kernel encoding that the rebuild fixed (current results are the true correct ones, the cached binary was lying), or (b) the rebuild introduced an actual layout regression that the validator now correctly catches. Either way the validator is honestly RED about the current rebuild. Needs investigation to determine which interpretation is correct and what the remediation is.

Not a C4 issue (C4 touched zero production files). Tracked separately so the C-chain can close while this env-divergence is investigated.
close_reason: MISCLASSIFIED. Original framing (env-divergence between cached May 26 build_tmp rocisa and worktree-rebuilt rocisa) was wrong. Root-cause investigation during C3g revert reveals: (1) the rebuilt rocisa schedules the prologue's PackMFMA -> CVT_PACK pairs closer together than the cached binary did, and (2) those tighter spacings violate CDNA4 Section 7.6's 5-quad-cycle requirement (observed gaps: 0, 0, 1, 1, 4, 4 per A/B per prologue copy = 24 TimingTooCloseFailures). The validator is correctly catching a real kernel-writer timing defect. Reproducible 100% (two consecutive runs identical). Refiled as a P0 (c)-class bug blocking r62g. C3g revert itself does NOT resolve these failures — they're a kernel-writer issue, not a validator issue.

title: Add OperationShape enum to rocisa for swap and no-dst opcodes
description:
## Why

Audit `rocm-libraries-8t9` (commit 33a116f272, Section 2 Category D and Section 3 Step 4) identified the operation-shape workarounds: `_VSwapRule` (treats VSwapB32 as symmetric R+W on both operands) and the "no_dst" shape branch inside `_SCC_OPCODE_FLAGS` / `_SCCRule` (covers SCmp* / SCBranchSCC* / SBitcmp* whose constructors pass `dst=nullptr`). These exist because rocisa offers only one CommonInstruction shape — asymmetric, with `params[0]` as dst — and exceptions require hand-coded overrides.

The `_GenericALURule` docstring "DANGER ZONE" comment makes this a known footgun: any new CommonInstruction subclass whose constructor passes `nullptr` as the dst will be silently misclassified by the generic rule, with `params[0]` (a SOURCE) treated as a write. If such a class lands in a captured CMS body region, phantom RAW edges will appear in the dataflow graph.

## Scope

- rocisa C++: add an `OperationShape` enum (or per-class `is_swap` / `has_no_dst` boolean flags) on the relevant rocisa classes:
  - `OperationShape::Swap` for VSwapB32 (and any future v_swap_* width variant).
  - `OperationShape::NoDst` for SCmp* / SCmpK* / SCBranchSCC* / SBitcmp* (any class whose constructor passes `dst=nullptr`).
  - `OperationShape::DstThenSrcs` as the default.
- rocisa nanobind: expose the enum.
- Validator: replace `_VSwapRule` with a dispatch on `inst.operation_shape == OperationShape::Swap`. Replace the "no_dst" branch in `_SCCRule` with a dispatch on `inst.operation_shape == OperationShape::NoDst`. Delete the `type(inst).__name__.startswith("VSwap")` predicate.
- Best done jointly with bead `dzl` since the "no_dst" shape is intertwined with SCC handling.

## Hard rules

- Snapshot test: every captured VSwap* and SCmp*/SCBranch*/SBitcmp* instruction must produce identical (reads, writes) before and after.
- Adding a new CommonInstruction subclass with `dst=nullptr` should now be safe: it gets `OperationShape::NoDst` in the same change.

## Acceptance

- `_VSwapRule` deleted from validator.
- "no_dst" shape branch in `_SCCRule` reduced to one-line `inst.operation_shape == OperationShape::NoDst` test.
- The `_GenericALURule` "DANGER ZONE" docstring section can be removed (the footgun is closed by construction).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `rocm-libraries-br4`.
- Coordinate with `rocm-libraries-dzl` (Category C bead — overlap on the no_dst shape).
- Audit reference: `rocm-libraries-8t9` (commit 33a116f272), section 2 Category D.

## Audit reference

Spawned from `Tensile/Components/ROCISA_WORKAROUNDS_AUDIT.md` (the 8t9 audit, commit 33a116f272; status update at the top reflects subsequent reframings).

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: Investigate whether InstructionCountRule + optSchedule/id_map plumbing should be deleted post-ola
description:
# Investigate, don't presume

After ola.1-4 land, structural rules consuming optSchedule/id_map are gone. ola.5's keep+cover decision was correct for today, but it leaves an open question: once those structural readers vanish, IS InstructionCountRule and the optSchedule/id_map plumbing actually dead code, or are there lingering consumers?

This bead is INVESTIGATION ONLY — produce evidence and a recommendation. Do not delete anything as part of this issue. The deletion (if warranted) becomes a follow-up.

# What to check

1. Grep `optSchedule` and `id_map` references after ola.1-4 land. Categorize each surviving reader:
   - Diagnostic / logging only (low risk; can stay)
   - Structural rule that wasn't part of ola scope (real consumer; deletion blocked)
   - Test scaffolding only (rewrite or delete tests separately)
   - Dead code (orphan; safe to remove)
2. Confirm the dataflow graph + flattened timeline cover EVERY downstream invariant InstructionCountRule was guarding. Specifically: does compare_graphs Phase 0 (identity-set equality between default and CMS graphs) catch every drift mode that the structural rules' silent zip() truncation would have hidden?
3. Check whether InstructionCountRule's per-code-path length check has any value the graph-side equivalent does not (e.g., does it surface bugs at a stage earlier than graph-build, where errors are easier to debug?).
4. Audit all 8 tests in test_ValidateInstructionCount.py — are any of them actually testing invariants the graph doesn't, vs. testing the rule-as-implementation?

# Possible outcomes

- **(a) Confirmed dead post-ola** — file a follow-up bead to delete InstructionCountRule + STRUCTURAL_RULES entry + test_ValidateInstructionCount.py + any orphaned optSchedule/id_map plumbing. Wire it as a chore.
- **(b) Still has a consumer** — document the surviving consumer; either migrate it (file a sub-bead under the migration) or accept the rule indefinitely.
- **(c) Different cleanup shape** — e.g., the rule's value migrates into a graph-side assertion at build time. Document the design.

# Verification

If outcome (a): the follow-up deletion bead must verify pytest stays green and grep returns no live readers.

# Depends on

ola.1, ola.2, ola.3, ola.4 — only meaningful after the structural-rule migrations remove their dependencies.

title: Replace identity_for with (loop_index, canonical_render, emission_ordinal) — drop class_tag from identity
description:
**Sub-bead under umbrella `rocm-libraries-xqj3`** (CMS→rocisa categorization refactor).

Per the user's xqj3 comment 76 (2026-05-12) and the rejection of on0t Approach 11 as CMS-coupled. Full design in `Tensile/Components/EMISSION_ORDINAL_DESIGN.md` (this commit).

## Single-sentence framing

Replace identity tuple `(class_tag, loop_index, canonical_render)` with `(loop_index, canonical_render, emission_ordinal)` where `emission_ordinal` is a per-`(body_label, canonical_render)` monotonic counter assigned at `LoopBodyCaptureBuilder.finalize`-time over the canonical-sorted instruction list. Drop `class_tag` from identity entirely; migrate the three load-bearing `identity[0]` consumers (`_DATA_FLOW_KINDS` filter, `edge_keys` role positions, `_summary_by_class` diagnostic) to rocisa-derived predicates that consult `node.rocisa_inst` via the centralized `_CLASS_NAME_TO_CATEGORY` registry (`InstructionCategory.py:111-227`).

## Why drop class_tag

The current `class_tag` slot is computed by `class_tag_for_category` (`ScheduleCapture.py:374-426`), whose buckets are CMS-derived (`'LR'`, `'LRS'`, `'GR'`, `'GRINC'`, `'PACK'`, etc. — derived from CMS category strings). Even after the on0t Approach 11 selective un-collapse, identity buckets remain CMS-shaped by inheritance. The only load-bearing consumers of `identity[0]` (`_DATA_FLOW_KINDS` filter at `CMSValidator.py:3301-3304`, `edge_keys` role positions at `:1238-1241`, `_summary_by_class` diagnostic at `:3314-3319`) can each be rewritten in <10 LoC to consult rocisa directly. The disambiguator role of `class_tag` (separating same-render-text emissions like the on0t SCC/m0 collisions and the pack-MFMA case) is taken over cleanly by `emission_ordinal`.

## Determinism guarantee

Both real builds (CMS-emit-build and non-CMS-emit-build under `rocm-libraries-71hw` Approach A) consume IDENTICAL kernel-writer source modules (`LRCodeAAllIters[u]`, `PackCodeAAllIters[u]`, `globalReadA`, `globalReadB`, `globalReadIncACode`, `globalReadIncBCode`, etc.). For each `(body, canonical_render)` both real builds therefore emit the same number of instances in the same relative order; per-emission ordinals match cross-build by construction. Scheduler-control instructions (`SWaitCnt`, `SBarrier`, `SNop`, `SSetPrior`) are excluded from `nodes_by_identity` via `_NO_DATAFLOW_IDENTITY_CATEGORIES` (`CMSValidator.py:1788`), so per-build differences in scheduler-control insertion don't shift ordinals.

## Sequencing

- **ALONGSIDE `rocm-libraries-svb1`** (idmap-factory unification): independent layers; either can land first.
- **BEFORE `rocm-libraries-71hw`** (Approach A real-build): the new identity must be in place before `compare_graphs` consumes a non-CMS-side real-build capture as `reference`, otherwise Approach A inherits the on0t collision surface.
- **ALONGSIDE `rocm-libraries-oram.1`** (body-label tolerance): orthogonal — oram.1 changes how cross-body identity divergence is interpreted, this work changes how identity is constructed.

## Test surface (gates the migration)

1. Per-render emission-count assertion: for a representative schedule (`_get_schedule_160x128x64_TF32`), assert that both real builds emit the same count for every `(body, canonical_render)` pair. Validates the determinism invariant directly.
2. Per-render ordinal assignment assertion: assert that for every `(body, canonical_render, ordinal)`, both captures resolve to the same logical instruction.
3. Z012 collision regression: synthesize a capture with two same-render emissions (mirror the on0t SCC pattern), assert distinct identities.
4. `example.yaml` end-to-end against `_get_schedule_160x128x64_TF32`: assert the 8 spurious `OrderInvertedFailure`s from `EXAMPLE_YAML_DEFECT_INVESTIGATION.md §1` no longer fire.
5. Full unit suite under `pytest --ignore=tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/test_MatrixInstructionConversion.py` stays green; tests pinning `identity[0] == "..."` (verified to be `test_dataflow_graph_lcc.py:128` and `test_dataflow_graph_builder.py:590`) get rewritten per design memo §4.5; `test_dataflow_graph_comparison.py:550-609` (`test_category_overrides_isinstance_class_tag`) becomes obsolete.

## Migration shape

One PR, no half-state:
- `ScheduleCapture.py`: add `emission_ordinal` field on `TaggedInstruction`; assign in `LoopBodyCaptureBuilder.finalize` over the canonical-sorted list (per `assign_stream_indices_for_body:744-760` lex-key); change `identity_for` to the new tuple shape.
- `CMSValidator.py`: rewrite `_data_flow_ids` (`:3303`) and `_summary_by_class` (`:3314`) to consult `node.rocisa_inst` via `_category()`; rewrite `edge_keys` (`:1238`) and the ref-edge dict-comprehension (`:3349`) to use a rocisa-derived `_role(node)` helper.
- Tests: rewrite the two pinning tests (`test_dataflow_graph_lcc.py:128`, `test_dataflow_graph_builder.py:590`); remove `test_category_overrides_isinstance_class_tag` (`test_dataflow_graph_comparison.py:550-609`); add the five regression tests in §6.2 of the design memo.

## Framing corrections to the dispatching brief

- `_NO_DATAFLOW_IDENTITY_CATEGORIES` (`CMSValidator.py:1788`) is NOT identity-coupled — it consults `_category(inst)`, not `node.identity[0]`. No migration needed for that consumer.
- `cms_node_label` (`CMSValidator.py:3202`) and the CMS-side `FailureNodeLabel` providers consume `node.category` (the raw CMS string), NOT `identity[0]`. Failure rendering is unaffected by the identity refactor.
- `GraphNode.identity` docstring at `CMSValidator.py:913` is stale — claims `(rocisa_class_name, loop_index, signature_tuple)` but the actual shape is `(class_tag, loop_index, canonical_render)`. Correct in the same PR.

## Status of related work

- Supersedes `rocm-libraries-on0t` Approach 11 (selective un-collapse). on0t becomes a regression-test bead (its failure-pattern is what test #4 in §6.2 pins) once this lands.
- Does NOT supersede `rocm-libraries-svb1` (which addresses cross-body factory drift, an upstream-of-identity concern). svb1 may still be useful even after rocisa-derived identity lands.

## References

- Design memo: `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Components/EMISSION_ORDINAL_DESIGN.md` (this commit).
- Mechanism evidence: `Tensile/Components/EXAMPLE_YAML_DEFECT_INVESTIGATION.md` §1-2.
- Approach 11 framing (now superseded): `rocm-libraries-on0t`, `Tensile/Components/Z012_RESIDUAL_INVESTIGATION.md` §2.
- Determinism-edge-cases: `Tensile/Components/2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md` §1.
- Body-label sensitivity (oram.1): `Tensile/Components/PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §2.
- Umbrella: `rocm-libraries-xqj3` comment 76.

Identity tuple replaced with (loop_index, canonical_render, emission_ordinal); class_tag dropped from identity. _data_flow_ids / _summary_by_class / edge_keys / ref-edge dict migrated to rocisa-derived role/category via _role(node) helper + _DATA_FLOW_CATEGORIES (no CMS-shaped strings inside the filter). New regression test surface in test_dataflow_graph_emission_ordinal.py with on0t collision pin (TestZ012CollisionRegression). Verification: 1009 passed, 3 skipped, 4 xfailed (zero failures, zero xpasses). 4 xfails are explicit and tracked: 1 pre-existing unrelated, 2 under d3zj (scheduler-control divergence), 1 under exfw (71hw-blocking CMS-vs-default pack-MFMA asymmetry).

title: Emit full SHADOW/default-schedule assembly text to ground-truth the SHADOW capture (close no-emitted-.s residual)
description:
FINDINGS: Tensile/Components/SHADOW_FULL_EMISSION_FEASIBILITY.md

GAP: validator reference = SHADOW capture (source=default-sia3, writer._last_default_capture). Faithfulness rests on a producer-side argument, NOT a direct text diff. CMS subject by contrast IS text-proven (cms_capture_listing matches kernel.s NGL :2175/2208/2225). SHADOW has no emitted .s. dm4p Phase 2 made SHADOW the canonical reference (KernelWriter.py:6392-6413), so the validator now trusts an unverified-by-text capture.

POSSIBLE: yes, qualified. The full default kernel is ALREADY assembled today and discarded: approach_a.py:214 calls writer._getKernelSource(non_cms_solution) (returns full asm text) then keeps only the FourPartCapture (:216). _dump_carveout_assembly.py:226-234 already dumps kernel_default.s this way. SHADOW path itself (KernelWriter.py:4196 noLoadLoop, :5226 _loopBody) runs the real default emitter but DISCARDS the emitted Module (only captures) -- contrast non-CMS :4226 which module.add()s it. So full default kernel is NOT assembled in the SHADOW path; it is fragments-only.

- A-text (low risk): capture the _getKernelSource return value already produced by build_non_cms_reference / _dump_carveout_assembly. No emitter change. title: C3d byte-key migration causes producer-discrimination loss: OrderInvertedFailure and MissingWaitFailure false negatives
description: C3d (rocm-libraries-xxj4) migrated edge_keys() from identity-tuple to byte-key basis. This causes 7 new test failures: 5 in test_ValidateSCCoverlap, 1 in test_validate_pack_graph (OrderInvertedFailure), and 1 in test_validate_gr_not_too_early_graph (MissingWaitFailure). Root cause: byte-key basis loses producer-discrimination. Two edges A->C (A writes v8, C reads v8) and B->C (B also writes v8, C reads v8) produce identical byte-key tuples (('v',8),(('v',8)), raw_intrawave, ...) and cancel in set-diff even when one of them represents the wrong producer (a reorder violation). The old docstring explicitly warned this would happen (LR_first/LR_second cross-iter case). The fix requires augmenting the byte-key tuple with producer ordering information (e.g., emission ordinal from identity) or using a hybrid key that preserves producer-discrimination while being iter-blind. This blocks C3e and C3h.
close_reason: Option E implemented: edge_keys() augmented with (source_module_id, emission_ordinal) — the iter-blind, register-rename-blind subset of the identity 3-tuple. New 8-field tuple: (source_module_id, emission_ordinal, producer_write_byte_key, consumer_read_byte_key, edge_kind, intra_operand_byte_offset, src_operand_slot, sink_operand_slot). canonical_render STAYS OUT (would re-introduce n7og UsePLRPack T/X false positives). compare_graphs ref_edges_by_key migrated to the matching 8-field key. The role+position diagnostic table in repro_cross_subiter_artifact.py is a separate schema and was preserved unchanged. Synthetic test fixtures in test_ValidateSCCoverlap.py and test_validate_pack_graph.py updated to populate source_module_id with role-semantic values (scc_producer/scc_clobber/scc_consumer, lr_pack/swap_pack/vcvt_pack) — principled because production captures always carry a non-None source_module_id. test_56e3_option_e_probe.py renamed to test_56e3_emission_ordinal_invariance.py and kept as a permanent regression guard. 8 detection tests resurface (5 OverriddenInputFailure, 1+1 OrderInvertedFailure, 1 MissingWaitFailure). n7og's 3 fixtures still pass (canonical_render absence from key preserves the T/X cancellation). Empirically verified safe by Tensile/Components/56e3_OPTION_E_EMPIRICAL_PROBE.md across 2140 same-(render,source) groups in TF32+UsePLRPack fixtures. Unblocks rocm-libraries-67us (C3e) and rocm-libraries-si5f (C3h).

title: Generalize validator to compare timelines (SIA3-vs-SIA3, future SIA0-vs-SIA3); decouple from CMS schedule shape
description:
> **Status (2026-05-07): Rescoped.** This bead now covers ONLY the validator-side groundwork to accept arbitrary timelines as input, validated by self-comparison + mutation-injected error tests. The codegen-vs-codegen application — and the codegen-side work needed to make that comparison meaningful (register-name canonicalization, codegen instruction-stream extraction, etc.) — is deferred to its companion bead (filed alongside this rescope). 5gd is now a focused validator refactor; it does not enable any new comparison source.

> **Status (2026-05-06).** The registered gfx1151 CMS schedules cannot be trusted as correct; that schedule corpus has been removed entirely on `validator_long_term_plans`. References to gfx1151 below are historical context.

---

## Why this exists

Today the validator is glued to the CMS scheduling pipeline:
- It consumes `ScheduleCapture` directly (one capture per body).
- Its node identities are CMS-shaped (`LRA0[12]`, `LWA[3]`, etc.) — chosen because that's the granularity the scheduler operates on, so user-facing failures point at "the LRA0 the scheduler placed at slot N".
- It silently assumes both sides of any comparison were produced by the same code path (or equivalent), so register naming is consistent.

We want the validator engine to consume a generic timeline so future comparison sources (codegen-vs-codegen, SIA0-vs-SIA3) can plug in without rewriting the validator. **This bead does the validator-side refactor only.** The downstream sources are not enabled here.

## Scope

### Validator-side input-shape refactor

Change the validator's primary entry point so it consumes a **linearized timeline of objects** rather than a `ScheduleCapture`.

- Define the timeline interface (probably `List[TimelineEvent]` where each event carries: position, instruction-or-equivalent, tagged metadata, register reads/writes, edge contributions). Keep it minimal — only what the existing graph builder + edge-coverage logic actually consumes.
- Move the current `ScheduleCapture → graph` construction into an **external helper**: `cms_capture_to_timeline(capture: ScheduleCapture) -> Timeline`. The validator no longer knows about CMS-specific fields; the helper bridges.
- Verify the existing CMS test suite still passes with the new shape (route everything through `cms_capture_to_timeline`).

The codegen-side helper (`assembly_to_timeline` or equivalent) is **NOT in scope** here — that lives in the follow-up bead.

## Tests

The bead is considered done when the new test surface is in place AND the existing CMS test suite still passes.

### Test 1 — self-comparison is a no-op

Generate one timeline from a real SIA3 capture. Pass that same timeline as both `src` and `dest` to the validator. Assert: zero failures, zero warnings of any kind. This is the "validator engine doesn't hallucinate divergence on identical input" invariant.

### Test 2 — mutation-injected known errors

Take the timeline from Test 1, apply small targeted mutations, assert the validator produces the expected typed `Failure`:

- Remove an `SWaitCnt` between a producer and its consumer → `MissingWaitFailure` (or whichever subclass covers it).
- Remove an `SBarrier` after an LDS-reuse wait → the LDS-reuse barrier failure.
- Remove a producer instruction the consumer depends on → missing-edge failure of the appropriate kind.
- Reorder a producer/consumer pair → `OrderInvertedFailure`.
- (Add others as natural mutations of common edge kinds emerge.)

Each mutation test asserts BOTH the failure type AND that no extra noise failures fire — small mutations should produce small, targeted failure sets.

### Test discipline

- Mutations apply to a real captured timeline, not a synthetic one — keeps the tests grounded in real instruction streams.
- The mutation helpers should themselves be small composable functions on the timeline (`drop_swait_at(timeline, idx)`, `swap_pair(timeline, i, j)`, `remove_instruction(timeline, predicate)`) so the test corpus can grow cheaply.
- These tests live in the existing `Tensile/Tests/unit/` directory, alongside the current validator tests.

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-up bead)

The follow-up bead covers everything below; nothing here is being abandoned, just sequenced.

- `assembly_to_timeline` (codegen-asm extraction).
- Codegen-vs-codegen mode (using two SIA3 invocations as both sides).
- Per-source label rendering (CMS-style labels vs assembly mnemonics).
- Heterogeneous-source comparison (CMS vs codegen-asm).
- Register-name canonicalization (`wx9.3` work — string-register robustness; codegen produces different register names per allocator run, so codegen-vs-codegen needs name-agnostic topology comparison; this is the codegen application's problem, not this bead's).
- SIA0-vs-SIA3 mode (longer-term stretch).
- Any of the codegen-side fixes needed to make a meaningful timeline come out of the codegen path.

## Hard rules

- The new `Timeline` interface must be small enough that the test corpus (Tests 1 + 2) drives every field — no speculative metadata for hypothetical future sources.
- The CMS path goes through `cms_capture_to_timeline`; no CMS-specific field reaches the validator core. If you find one, that's a bug in the helper and it stays in the helper.

## Acceptance

- `cms_capture_to_timeline` exists and is the only place CMS-specific fields are read.

- Test 2 (mutation suite) lands with at least 4 distinct mutation kinds covering missing-wait, missing-barrier, missing-producer, and reorder.

- Follow-up bead (codegen-vs-codegen + codegen fixes + wx9.3 application) — TODO ID once filed.
- `wx9.3` — string-register robustness. NO LONGER pulled forward by this bead; moved to the follow-up. (`wx9.3` originally blocked 5gd; that dependency moves with the codegen scope.)
- `9lcs` — flag-handling reconciliation. Not a hard dep for this bead (we're not enabling any new comparison source), but stays a hard dep for the follow-up (codegen-vs-codegen needs both sides to actually be the same kernel).
- `2yg` — final design document for the graph-native validator. The `Timeline` interface should land documented there.

## Why P2

Strategic groundwork. Self-justifying as a refactor (smaller validator surface, cleaner separation). Real payoff is the follow-up bead's codegen comparison, but that doesn't need to happen for this bead to be a win.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.

title: Surface operand-slot info on OrderInvertedFailure (or successor failure) once two-stream validator generalization lands
description:
## Why this exists

wx9.3 Phase 3 (commit 109abdab1e on users/alvasile/wx9.3-phase3) added `src_operand_slot` and `sink_operand_slot` fields to `OrderInvertedFailure` and an appended diagnostic sentence on `_format_canonical`:

    Inverted edge: producer write-slot N -> consumer read-slot M.

This was reverted (same commit) per user direction: keep the old failure formatting unchanged for now. The operand-slot information remains on `DataflowEdge` and is used internally by `compare_graphs` / `diagnose_missing_edge` for matching — it just isn't surfaced on the user-facing failure object anymore.

The slot info is the load-bearing diagnostic for cases like the VSwap pair-reorder (test_vswap_pair_reorder_detected): without it, the rendered failure says producer-X-after-consumer-Y but gives no explanation of WHY a symmetric-looking reorder was flagged. The slot-flip (e.g. write-slot 1 → read-slot 1 in REF vs write-slot 0 → read-slot 0 in SUBJ) IS the discriminator, and a developer staring at a real failure would benefit from seeing it.

## Why deferred to the 5gd-family epic

5gd is generalizing the validator to accept arbitrary timelines from any source (CMS capture, codegen-asm capture, future sources). The Failure rendering surface is going to need a broader rework as part of that generalization: per-source label rendering (CMS-style `LRA0[12]` vs codegen `v_pack_b32 v3, v4`), per-source "what happened" framing, etc. Adding the slot sentence in isolation now would constrain choices that 5gd / wic4 will want to make holistically (e.g., whether to surface slot info as a structured field consumers parse, vs an inline sentence; whether the slot semantics differ across timeline sources; etc.).

## What this bead asks for

When the two-stream / arbitrary-timeline validator generalization is shipping its Failure-rendering rework:

1. Decide how to surface operand-slot info (or its successor concept) on order-inversion failures. Options span:
   - Re-add the appended sentence as wx9.3 Phase 3 originally had it.
   - Make slot info a structured per-failure field consumers can opt into rendering.
   - Make it source-aware (CMS vs codegen-asm slot semantics may differ).
2. Implement the chosen surface.
3. Add a test that asserts the rendered VSwap pair-reorder failure explains the slot flip in some form (string-match on slot info or structured-field assertion).
4. Update test_vswap_pair_reorder_detected to assert the new diagnostic surface.

## Reference

- Reverted commit: `109abdab1e` on `users/alvasile/wx9.3-phase3`
- Original (now-reverted) shape: see git show `d4398b6f02:projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py` for the OrderInvertedFailure dataclass and `_format_canonical` body that landed in Phase 3 before the revert.
- Memo: `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Components/TOPOLOGY_EQUIVALENCE_INVESTIGATION.md` § 6 step 1 (the slot-identity contract).

title: CI linter: enforce YAML vs schedule decorator required_flags consistency
description:
Per 2bww reviewer note 2: the strict-model implementation removes mid-build mutation but does not cross-check YAML against the schedule decorator's required_flags at production build time. Wrapped_func attaches required_flags to ScheduleInfo for the 3ija runner's consumption but does NOT validate kernel[flag] == required_flags[flag]. Author is responsible for keeping YAML and decorator in sync.

## What to build

A test or lint check that, for each registered CMS schedule, asserts every YAML benchmark group that resolves to that schedule sets the flag values declared in the schedule's required_flags for the matched (layout, useLDSTr, TLDS) branch.

## Acceptance

## Why P2

Today's safety net: the runner's reference-side build pulls from required_flags directly, so any YAML/decorator drift surfaces as a CaptureConsistencyError (cg!=0) on the affected fixture. This linter would catch drift earlier (at YAML-load time) and produce a more diagnostic error message.

## Cross-references

- rocm-libraries-2bww (strict model implementation)
- Tensile/Components/2BWW_STRICT_REVIEW.md issue 2
close_reason: Obsolete. Filed when wrapped_func did NOT validate required_flags against kernel state — the proposed YAML-load-time linter was needed to catch YAML/decorator drift before the runner surfaced it as a CaptureConsistencyError. The 2bww strict-model work (squashed into validator branch as 5fbe10db5e4) added uniform required_flags validation directly in wrapped_func: any YAML/decorator drift now returns UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT at dispatch time, the kernel is rejected via 9lcs as 'CMS not supported', and codegen never proceeds with mismatched state. title: Tighten LoopBodyCaptureBuilder string-token boundary; remove _populate_wrapper hasattr gate
description:
## Why this exists

vvcm review (commit 0665f1eba9) noted that the new `hasattr(inst, 'reads_scc') and hasattr(inst, 'writes_scc')` shape gate at `ScheduleCapture._populate_wrapper` exists solely to accommodate plain-string `inst='i0'` test inputs to `LoopBodyCaptureBuilder.append`. Production callers always wrap real rocisa instances; the gate would never fire in production.

13 test callsites in `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ScheduleCapture.py` use `b.append(inst='i0', category=..., ...)` with plain strings as instruction objects — these test bookkeeping (slot ordering, sequence assignment) without exercising dataflow semantics. The gate's existence is itself a hidden defensive pattern: silent in production but accommodating in tests, which is exactly the smell vvcm was supposed to eliminate.

## Scope

Pick one of the following two cleanups:

**Option A — Migrate the test callsites.** Replace each of the 13 plain-string `inst='i0'` usages with a real rocisa instance (or a tiny factory function that returns one). Then delete the `hasattr` gate at `ScheduleCapture._populate_wrapper`. This makes the test-vs-production shape contract uniform.

**Option B — Make the boundary explicit.** Replace the silent `hasattr` gate with an explicit `assert` or `raise CaptureUnknownInstructionError`. Then audit the 13 callsites: are they testing bookkeeping that should NOT touch `_populate_wrapper` at all? If so, route them around it. The gate becomes documentation rather than accommodation.

Either is acceptable; A is more invasive but more uniform. Try A first; fall back to B if migration is too tedious.

## Hard rules

- After this bead, `_populate_wrapper` should not need a shape gate that fires only in tests. Either the test inputs are real-shaped, or the boundary is explicit (raise, not silent skip).
- Per the project's clean-implementation directive: no fallback paths, no parallel APIs.
- All 664 unit tests must pass.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring `LoopBodyCaptureBuilder`'s general API beyond the `inst=` parameter contract.
- Adding new test fixtures.

## Why P3

No active correctness incident. The current gate works; this is hygiene work to remove a hidden test/production asymmetry surfaced during vvcm review.

## Audit reference

- vvcm critical review on 2026-05-07.
- Affected files: `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py` (around line 1517-1528 for the gate), `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ScheduleCapture.py` (search for `b.append(inst=`).

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** Set `model: 'opus'` explicitly when dispatching.
- **No fallback paths or backwards-compat shims.**

title: Audit cms_test_utils mocks: which can be replaced by generate_real_idmap, which are dead, which are load-bearing
description:
## Why this exists

The CMS validator unit tests use two different fixture-construction paths:

1. **`make_mock_id_map`** (`Tensile/Tests/unit/cms_test_utils.py`) — builds idMaps from synthetic rocisa instructions, no kernel writer, no real codegen. Most validator unit tests use this path via `cms_validation_base`.
2. **`generate_real_idmap`** (`Tensile/Tests/unit/cms_test_utils.py:~688`) — calls the actual `KernelWriterAssembly._getKernelSource(solution)` and stashes the real `_last_cms_capture`. Used by the TF32 4x4 capture tests in `test_ScheduleCapture.py:673,729`.

The 4ft cleanup just deleted three significant chunks of the mock path that turned out to be untested dead code:
- `_make_mock_swap_packs` + `_MOCK_SWAP_PAIRS_BY_VW` snapshot table (TF32 swap-pack fixture)
- `_make_mock_packs_tf32` + `_make_mock_packs_tf32_4x4` (TF32 pack fixtures)
- The `is_tf32 / is_4x4_tf32` branch in `make_mock_id_map`
- Four orphaned register-space constants (`CVT0_BASE`, `TF32_INTERMEDIATE_BASE`, `MFMA_PACK_A_BASE`, `SWAP_BASE`)

Total: ~250 LoC of mock infrastructure that no test exercised because the only way to reach it was to set kernel flags that no test sets — while the real TF32 tests bypass the entire mock path and use `generate_real_idmap`.

This raises a broader question: **how much of the remaining mock infrastructure is actually load-bearing, and how much could be replaced by `generate_real_idmap` for tests that currently use `make_mock_id_map`?**

## Scope

1. **Inventory the mocks.** Enumerate every helper in `cms_test_utils.py` (`_make_mock_lr`, `_make_mock_gr`, `_make_mock_grinc`, `_make_mock_swap`, `_make_mock_lw_swap`, `_make_mock_lcc`, `_make_mock_packs_bf16`, `make_mock_mfma_code`, `make_mock_id_map`). For each, list the call sites and the test cases they support.

2. **Audit each call site.** For every test case that uses a mock, ask:
   - Could `generate_real_idmap` produce a kernel capture that exercises the same validator code path?
   - What's the cost of doing so (per-test compile time, ISA infrastructure setup)?
   - Is there a kernel config that meaningfully exercises the test's intent end-to-end, or is the mock actively useful because the test is exercising an edge case real kernels don't produce?

3. **Categorize each mock helper:**
   - **Replaceable**: real codegen would produce the same shape; mock can be deleted, test rewritten to use `generate_real_idmap`.
   - **Load-bearing**: mock constructs a shape real kernels don't produce (negative-test fixtures, error-path inputs, edge cases). Keep, but document why.
   - **Dead**: like the four pieces 4ft just removed — gated on flags no test sets, or no callers at all.

4. **Cost analysis.** `generate_real_idmap` runs the full kernel writer pipeline, which has overhead per call. Measure: what would the test suite's wall-clock cost become if every replaceable mock were swapped for a real-codegen call? If it's prohibitive, fall back to a tiered approach (keep mocks for tight inner-loop tests, use real codegen for shape-verification tests).

5. **Coverage delta.** For any mock currently classified as "load-bearing", argue why an end-to-end test wouldn't catch the same regression. If the answer is "we'd need a hand-built negative fixture," the mock stays — but document THAT, so future readers don't repeat the 4ft mistake of carrying mock infrastructure that nothing reaches.

## Hard rules

- **Don't delete anything before discussion**. The output of this bead is a categorization (replaceable / load-bearing / dead) plus a recommendation per mock. Actual deletions land in follow-up beads, gated on user direction.
- Use `grep` + call-graph analysis to enumerate; don't trust the file's own claims about what each helper is for.
- If a "test" exists in name but is skipped/xfailed/never-collected, treat its mock as dead.
- The TF32 4x4 case from 4ft is the canonical "real codegen instead" template (see `test_tf32_4x4_tn_capture_shape` in `test_ScheduleCapture.py:673`). If a test could plausibly follow that template, flag it.

## Out of scope

- Migrating any actual test to `generate_real_idmap`. That's follow-up work after the categorization lands.
- Performance optimization of `generate_real_idmap` itself (separate concern).
- Removing `cms_test_utils.py` entirely (some helpers like `_frozen_config_key`, `subset_id_map`, `_make_solution` are infrastructure used by both paths).

## Why P2

The 4ft cleanup proved that a non-trivial amount of mock infrastructure was carrying its weight in maintenance burden but not in test coverage. We don't know if 4ft caught the only such cluster or just the most obvious one. Until the audit lands, we're guessing.

This is groundwork for ongoing test-suite hygiene; not blocking anything.

## Acceptance

- A markdown audit doc (suggested location: `Tensile/Components/MOCK_AUDIT.md`) listing every helper in `cms_test_utils.py` with: call sites, classification (replaceable / load-bearing / dead), reasoning, and recommended action.
- One follow-up bead per "dead" cluster (deletion bead) and per "replaceable" cluster (migration bead). User decides which to dispatch.

## Audit reference

- 4ft cleanup commits on branch `users/alvasile/4ft_delete_swap_pair_helpers`:
  - `5c0029a2c7d` — original `_compute_swap_register_pairs` deletion
  - `34319411b6b` — `_make_mock_swap_packs` deletion
  - `a2ff24af19b` — TF32 pack mocks + orphaned constants deletion
- The TF32 4x4 real-codegen-driven test pattern: `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ScheduleCapture.py:673,729`

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: Collapse SchedulePosition to (loop_index, stream_index) — drop sub_index; keep loop_ prefix
description:
User decision (recorded after cil spike landed): the proposed three-field rename to (body_index, stream_index, tie_break_index) is rejected. Replace with:

## Final shape

```python
SchedulePosition(loop_index: int, stream_index: int)
```

- **`loop_index`** — kept as-is (name unchanged). Even though the field today encodes one of 4 bodies of a single loop (ML-1/ML/NGL/NLL), the project will eventually model pre-loop, post-loop, and nested loops; under that broader model, the field truly indexes loop scopes. The name generalizes; `body_index` would not. (This is a deliberate hold against the cil spike's recommendation to rename to `body_index`.)
- **`stream_index`** — replaces the (vmfma_index, sub_index) pair. Single monotonic int per body; lex sort `(loop_index, stream_index)` continues to give global stream order.
- **`tie_break_index` is GONE.** Tie-breaking is folded into `stream_index` by computation at the bridge.

## Per-source computation of stream_index

- **CMS bridge (`xe5`, cms_capture_to_timeline):** walk events in their existing `(vmfma_index, sub_index)` lex order and assign `stream_index = 0, 1, 2, ...` per body. The bridge owns the conversion. The original `vmfma_index` and `SlotKey.sequence` are NOT preserved on `SchedulePosition` after this — they live only on `tagged_inst` for source-aware rendering (see rocm-libraries-3dy).
- **Codegen-asm bridge (`x6s` / `f3kb`):** assigns `stream_index` directly from the asm event's natural ordering (line number / instruction index). No tie-breaking needed because asm has no MFMA-anchor concept.

## Failure rendering implications

The current `@ idx={vmfma_index}` rendering at CMSValidator.py:2327 must move to source-aware dispatch (already in scope for rocm-libraries-3dy). Specifically:

- CMS-source rendering: the `@ idx=N` shape stays user-facing, but N is recovered from the CMS `tagged_inst` (which carries the original `SlotKey.mfma_index`), NOT from `position.stream_index` directly. `stream_index` is for sorting; CMS-y display info lives on `tagged_inst` and is rendered by the CMS `tagged_inst.render()` Protocol.
- Codegen-asm-source rendering: position renders as the asm-native location (line number or instruction offset).

The wx9.3 edge identity tuple
`(src_role, src_position, src_operand_slot, sink_role, sink_position, sink_operand_slot, edge_kind, intra_operand_byte_offset)`
is unaffected: `src_position` and `sink_position` are SchedulePosition objects compared by their full tuple state, so collapsing two ints into one doesn't break identity. Same multiset of edge keys both before and after the shape change (verify with test_vswap_pair_reorder_detected and the allocation-invariance tests).

## Scope of this bead

1. Refactor `SchedulePosition` (CMSValidator.py:~80) to be `(loop_index, stream_index)` only. Remove `sub_index`. Update `__lt__`, `__eq__`, repr, etc.
2. Update `POSITION_INF` and `POSITION_NEG_INF` constants accordingly.
3. Update `make_position` (ScheduleCapture.py:418-428) to emit the collapsed shape. Add a per-body counter so each event in build order gets the next `stream_index`. The CMS conversion logic lives here.
4. Update every consumer of `position.vmfma_index` and `position.sub_index`:
   - `_make_node` (CMSValidator.py:838) — node naming
   - `_node_subiter` (line 752) — derived subiteration
   - `cumulative_issue_cycles` (line 1518, 1545-1546) — timing key
   - `cms_node_label` / position rendering (line 2292, 2327) — must move to tagged_inst-driven rendering per 3dy
   - `_cms_iter_delta` (line 2342) — uses loop_index, fine
   - `diagnose_missing_edge` / `_classify_edge_coverage` — `wait_idx` population from position; needs to source from `tagged_inst` for CMS-y display, not from collapsed position
   - `_insert` (line 3770-3806) — structural-side, going away with wa57; if wa57 hasn't landed, update; else skip
   - All test fixture SchedulePosition() constructors (Tests/unit/)
5. Verify pytest 672/2/1 (or higher if any test gets cleaned up in the process).

## Sequencing

This bead BLOCKS rocm-libraries-iig (validator entry rewiring). Land before iig starts.

Order vs other beads:
- Can land BEFORE wa57 (which deletes structural-side) — they touch different surfaces
- Can land BEFORE 3dy — 3dy will then have a clean (loop_index, stream_index) position to write its source-aware renderer against
- MUST land before iig

title: compare_graphs: add subj-ref symmetric direction + EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure classifier
description:
compare_graphs at CMSValidator.py:3711-3713 only processes 'ref_keys - subj_keys' (the SHADOW-extras direction). Anything CMS emits that SHADOW does not — i.e. 'subj_keys - ref_keys' — is silently ignored. The validator never sees those edges.

Per n7og_PROBE_REPORT.md and 6QIB_DESIGN.md §0.9: on BPG#11, the per-body breakdown shows 16 NGL edges that CMS has but SHADOW does not (the subj_keys - ref_keys direction). The probe test surfaces them because it does its own symmetric set-diff; the build-time inline xj16 assertion (KernelWriter.py:6292-6311) does not.

Why this is a real correctness gap:
A CMS schedule emitting a dataflow edge that the default schedule (SHADOW) does not have is structurally a CMS-introduced write or read SHADOW did not produce. Under DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_REFERENCE_DESIGN.md §3, SHADOW and CMS should differ ONLY in scheduling — not in dataflow content. CMS having extra dataflow IS a real defect class the validator should detect.

What needs to change:
1. Add 'extra_keys = subj_keys - ref_keys' processing alongside the existing missing_keys path.
2. Add SpuriousEdgeFailure class (or similar typed Failure) — a CMS-introduced edge with no SHADOW counterpart.
3. Add diagnose_extra_edge classifier for routing these failures with diagnostic context.
4. Update inline assertion at KernelWriter.py:6292-6311 if necessary so SpuriousEdgeFailure surfaces alongside the existing missing-edge failures.

Scope: ~50 LOC implementation + tests.

Discovered during: n7og investigation (see n7og_PROBE_REPORT.md per-body breakdown). Independent of (d) unrolled-walk but exposed by the same fixture analysis. Can fold into the same commit if convenient since both touch compare_graphs, but tracked separately because it is a correctness gap on its own (the validator is silently blind to a real defect class today, regardless of (d)).
close_reason: C3e implemented: compare_graphs now processes the symmetric direction (subj_keys - ref_keys), classifying CMS-introduced edges that have no SHADOW counterpart. New typed Failure: EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure (mirrors OverriddenInputFailure on the subj-ref side; fields: subj_producer, subj_consumer, ref_producer, byte_keys, byte_key_routing). New exception: UnexplainedExtraEdgeError (mirrors UnexplainedMissingEdgeError; raised when set-diff arithmetic disagrees with byte_key_writers — a validator-bug signal). diagnose_extra_edge(subj_edge, subj_graph, ref_graph) implements the Option C hybrid three-phase classifier: Phase 0 raises CaptureConsistencyError if ref has no writer for any byte_key in subj's producer footprint; Phase 1 looks up the consumer in ref_graph by identity, uses REF-SIDE unrolled_position to find the closest-prior ref writer per byte_key — emits EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure on identity-mismatch, raises UnexplainedExtraEdgeError on all-match (impossible if set-diff is consistent). The ref-side position deviation from the plan was caught by the implementer and is the principled fix (asks 'what would ref's walk have seen at the moment ref's consumer appeared?'). Three terminal outcomes per Q4 design now fully implemented. 8 new tests in test_diagnose_extra_edge.py. Zero re-fixture work needed; production fixtures don't exercise the symmetric direction yet (16 NGL extras on BPG#11 cancel under post-C3d byte-key edge_keys). KernelWriter assertion polymorphic — handles new failure types via Failure.format().

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Renamed primary failure class from SpuriousEdgeFailure to EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure per Q4_SPURIOUS_EDGE_CLASSIFIER_DESIGN.md (2026-06-02).

Rationale: 'Spurious' presupposes the extra edge is wrong. Per DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_REFERENCE_DESIGN.md §3, the only surviving CMS-extras after the unrolled walk are EITHER capture-pipeline bugs (which raise CaptureConsistencyError before reaching the classifier) OR routing divergences (where the edge IS real dataflow; the defect is the routing, not the edge's existence). EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure names the actual semantic problem.

Three terminal outcomes for diagnose_extra_edge:
1. CaptureConsistencyError (raised) — subj writes byte_keys ref has no writer for; capture-pipeline bug
2. EdgeRoutedDifferentlyFailure (the typed Failure this bead now creates) — ref has writers but the closest-prior writer for subj_edge's byte_keys differs in identity from subj's producer; structurally a clobber; symmetric counterpart of OverriddenInputFailure; real CMS defect; hard-fail
3. UnexplainedExtraEdgeError (raised) — fall-through or identity-match (validator bug)

Design is byte-key-driven multi-phase (Option C hybrid). No class lists, no subiter arithmetic, no pattern matching. Avoids the m7o5 anti-pattern explicitly.

Still blocks r62g.

title: Remove raise_on_unexplained parameter; raise unconditionally on unclassified edges
description:
## Why this exists

Both `compare_graphs` and `validate_edge_wait_coverage` (now in `CMSValidator.py` post-br4.8/9) accept a `raise_on_unexplained` parameter. Tests pass `True`; production calls from `isValid` pass `False`. When `True`, an unclassified edge raises `UnexplainedMissingEdgeError`. When `False`, it becomes a soft Failure that's logged-and-continue.

This split mode is unjustified. An unclassified edge is a validator bug — the classifier didn't know what to do with something the graph builder produced. Either:

- The classifier should always know what to do (in which case the unexplained branch is dead code and can be deleted).
- Or the classifier might genuinely fail (in which case raising is correct EVERYWHERE — production silently logging a "validator bug" Failure is the silent-miss pattern bead `xjm` is trying to eliminate).

## What this bead does

1. Audit how often the unexplained path actually fires in tests vs production.
2. Either:
   - Remove the unexplained branch entirely if the classifier provably never falls through (preferred).
   - Or keep the raise behavior in production too, removing the parameter and always raising (matches `xjm`'s "no silent ignore" contract).
3. Delete the `raise_on_unexplained` parameter from both function signatures.
4. Update all call sites.
5. Delete the §7.8 description from `VALIDATOR_DESIGN.md` (already done in this commit if you're reading the bead post-rewrite).

## Hard rules

- No silent fallback in production. The validator either knows or admits it doesn't know — by raising.
- Tests stay green.
- Single PR.

## Acceptance

- `raise_on_unexplained` parameter gone from both function signatures.
- Unexplained branch either deleted (if dead) or retained with raise as the only behavior.
- All 602+ tests pass.

## Why P2

Closes a silent-miss footgun. Pairs naturally with `xjm` (raise-on-failure contract) — same spirit.

## Related

- `xjm` — raise-on-failure contract; same design principle.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.
close_reason: Merged to vlt as 60fa8231a9. raise_on_unexplained parameter removed from compare_graphs and validate_edge_wait_coverage; production now raises UnexplainedMissingEdgeError for unclassified edges (compare_graphs/diagnose_missing_edge) or relies on exhaustive classification (validate_edge_wait_coverage). 9 files changed, 99/104. 664/2/1 unit tests. Follow-up bead filed for fixture refinement to flip 2 weakened tests back to OrderInvertedFailure assertion.

title: f3kb.N4: Catch-all — codegen-side fixes uncovered during first end-to-end comparison
description:
## Parent: f3kb (codegen-vs-codegen timeline comparison)

## Why this exists

f3kb's Part D is exploratory by design: "Enumerate and fix as encountered. ... This part is exploratory — file sub-beads as concrete issues are identified. Do NOT attempt a one-shot 'fix everything that breaks' pass."

This bead is the SINGLE catch-all for that work. As concrete codegen-side issues surface during l88 / N1 / 1xr work, file specific sub-beads under THIS bead — do not expand its scope inline. Per user-provided decomposition rule: ONE catch-all per epic, not many.

## Anticipated classes (per f3kb description)

- Missing or untyped metadata on rocisa instructions at codegen time.
- Codegen passes that mutate instruction shape in ways the validator's edge-coverage logic isn't prepared for.
- Differences in implicit-operand handling between the CMS capture path and the codegen emit path.

The above is illustrative, NOT a checklist. Real fixes will emerge from running l88 against real kernels.

## Scope discipline

- This bead does NOT attempt up-front enumeration.
- Each concrete issue surfaced during l88 work becomes a CHILD bead with its own crisp acceptance criterion.
- This bead closes when (a) l88 closes, AND (b) every child bead under it is either closed or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## Done when

- l88 (`rocm-libraries-l88`) is closed (passing positive + negative tests).
- Every concrete codegen-side issue surfaced during l88 work is filed under this bead.
- Filed children are either resolved or have a deferral rationale documented.

## Dependencies

Concurrent with `l88`. Does NOT block l88's first dispatch — l88 IS the discovery vehicle for what fixes are needed.

## Out of scope

Issues that are obviously codegen non-determinism go to `f3kb.N3` (its own focused bead), not here.
Issues that are validator-side rendering / messaging problems go to `f3kb.N5`, not here.

## References

- f3kb description, Part D.

## Implementation directives

- Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.
- No fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
**Carry-forward from rocm-libraries-hdem (2026-05-12):** the hdem implementation substituted the literal byte-key tuple from ORAM1 §4.1 with `(producer.identity, consumer.identity, ...)` because the byte-key tuple lost producer-discrimination in two scenarios (`swap_pack` differently-classed-on-same-byte; cross-iter `LR_first`/`LR_second` same-class-same-byte). Identity carries operand text via `canonical_render` so it preserves discrimination AND is body-blind under Approach A.

**The trade-off that matters for codegen-vs-codegen:** the substitution narrows generality vs the memo design. If two captures render the SAME physical write differently — e.g., one symbolically as `v[vgprValuA_X0_I0:...+3]` and one numerically as `v[40:43]` because one resolved through `name_to_idx` and the other did not — identity-tuples DIVERGE while byte-keys would have MATCHED. Under the current CMS-vs-default path (both real captures from the same `kernelBody` invocation), this doesn't surface in practice — the empirical claim is documented at `CMSValidator.py:1252-1267`.

**Why this matters for this bead:** non-CMS vs non-CMS / codegen-vs-codegen comparison is exactly the regime where the symbolic-vs-numeric asymmetry is most likely to surface (two SIA3 invocations of the same kernel may produce different register-name resolutions; codegen-side allocator drift is documented as part of why wx9.3 work was deferred from 5gd).

**Hedge already in place:** the byte-key fields (`producer_write_byte_key` / `consumer_read_byte_key`) are still populated as informational metadata on `DataflowEdge` (CMSValidator.py:1109-1110). Future migration to byte-key matching (or a hybrid: identity-first, fall back to byte-key on render-divergence) is feasible without re-plumbing edge formation.

**References:**
- `Tensile/Components/HDEM_IMPLEMENTATION.md` "Implementation surprises" §1
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1229-1303` (current edge_keys)
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1252-1267` (the empirical-claim docstring)
- `Tensile/Components/ORAM1_PRINCIPLED_APPROACH_INVESTIGATION.md` §4.1 (the original byte-key proposal)

title: Classifier gap: VMovB64 raises CaptureUnknownInstructionError on real Build #2 (BPG#11 TF32 TN 128x160x64)
description:
## Reproducer

Standalone YAML: `Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/test_yamls/6hk3_tf32_128x160x64_tn.yaml` (committed in agent-6hk3-reproducer worktree, commit 13b576d615e; copied from BPG#11 of `Tensile/Tests/common/gemm/gfx950/custom_mainloop_scheduling_tf32.yaml`).

- Kernel: TF32 TN, MI=[16,16,32,1,1,4,5,2,2], MT 128x160x64, DepthU=64.
- Build: `--build-only --gpu-targets gfx950`, with the xj16 inline validation ENABLED (i.e. unmodified KernelWriter.py at HEAD of users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans).
- Failure (reproduced 2026-05-27, full log saved at `6hk3_artifacts/build_validation.log` in the worktree):

```
CaptureUnknownInstructionError: build_dataflow_graph: cannot classify instruction
'VMovB64' (category='UNKNOWN') in body 'ML-1'.
The capture pipeline must assign a recognized category, or the instruction's
class must be one of LR/LW/GR/MFMA/SWait/SBarrier.
Inner: _make_node: cannot classify instruction 'VMovB64' (category='UNKNOWN')
in body 'ML-1'.
```

Stack: `KernelWriter.py:5839` (`build_dataflow_graph(ctx.default)` — the real Build #2 reference path) → `CMSValidator.py:1997` → `_make_node:1766`. The default (non-CMS) reference graph trips first.

## Mechanism

`Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:_make_node` (via the rocisa-derived classifier registry, `_CLASS_NAME_TO_CATEGORY`) does not recognize `VMovB64`. The non-CMS reference build emits 20 `v_mov_b64` instructions in its mainloop (vs 0 in the CMS mainloop for this fixture — full-asm counts 82 non-CMS vs 2 CMS). `VMovB64` is emitted by `Tensile/Components/LocalRead.py:431-432` (shared pack/swap chain code that runs on both CMS and non-CMS paths). It is NOT non-CMS-exclusive; the CMS scheduler simply doesn't place any in this particular fixture's mainloop body.

The classifier gap stayed dormant under the legacy SHADOW path because that path's synthetic re-assembly did not propagate these emissions to `build_dataflow_graph`. The real Build #2 reference exercises the same emissions through the classifier and trips.

## Scope reduction (2026-05-27)

Original bead covered four instruction classes (VSwapB32/VPermB32/VOrB32/VMovB64) based on `_3ija_residual_triage_runner.py` output. Direct asm grep of BPG#11 (the only fixture verified end-to-end so far) shows ZERO occurrences of VSwapB32/VPermB32/VOrB32 anywhere in either build's assembly. The bead's per-instruction fixture mapping is therefore unverified — possibly stale or referring to a different config than `custom_mainloop_scheduling_tf32.yaml`. This bead now tracks ONLY the `VMovB64` classifier gap, which has a clean reproducer.

If/when VSwapB32/VPermB32/VOrB32 are confirmed to fire on a real fixture, they can be added back here or filed separately.

## Proposed fix sketch (NOT implemented)

1. Determine the canonical `InstructionCategory` for `VMovB64`. It's emitted in `Tensile/Components/LocalRead.py:431-432` as part of a local-read packing code path. Likely candidates: ALU/MOVE family, or PACK_*-family depending on where it sits in the data-flow chain (the bead's earlier framing said "ALU/move" — needs confirmation from looking at the emission context).
2. Extend the rocisa-derived `_CLASS_NAME_TO_CATEGORY` registry in `Tensile/Components/InstructionCategory.py` with the explicit mapping.
3. Re-run `Tensile/bin/Tensile Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule/gfx950/test_yamls/6hk3_tf32_128x160x64_tn.yaml /tmp/6hk3_out --build-only --gpu-targets gfx950` — should advance past the `CaptureUnknownInstructionError` and surface whatever residual is next (which may itself be informative, e.g. a count divergence in MFMA/LR/LW/GR or an edge-coverage failure).

## Acceptance criterion

- The above command no longer raises `CaptureUnknownInstructionError` on `VMovB64`.
- Whatever Build #2 reference residual surfaces next is classifiable per the 3ija triage framing.

## Cross-references

- `Tensile/Components/3IJA_RESIDUAL_TRIAGE.md §C` — original four-class triage entry (now partially superseded by this bead's scope reduction).
- `Tensile/Components/InstructionCategory.py` — classifier registry.
- `EMISSION_ORDINAL_DESIGN.md §4.1` — rocisa-derived classifier contract.
- `Tensile/Components/LocalRead.py:431-432` — VMovB64 emission site.
- Reproducer artifacts: `agent-6hk3-reproducer` branch in worktree `agent-a6cf69172d8397f93`, commit 13b576d615e (yaml + 6hk3_artifacts/{6hk3_cms.s, 6hk3_noncms.s, mainloop extracts, README, build logs}).

comments.text:
Correction (2026-05-27): the original 'Mechanism' section overstates the asymmetry. These four instruction classes are emitted by shared code in Tensile/Components/LocalRead.py and Tensile/Components/PackData.py (search for 'VPermB32', 'VSwapB32', 'VOrB32', 'VMovB64' — all are inside pack/swap chain builders that run on both CMS and non-CMS paths). title: Phase 2 follow-up to oram: capture initial LRs / LWs / GR warmup + their prologue SWaitCnt/SBarrier
description:
Follow-up to oram Phase 2 (commit 8f024c27ff and fixup commit on top of it).

The original oram Phase 2 implementation cut LR/LW/GR prologue capture from scope because:

- Capturing them produces prologue->mainloop edges that the wait-coverage validator flags as uncovered (the prologue's s_waitcnt + s_barrier instructions aren't currently captured/positioned in the prologue stream).
- The fix requires capturing the prologue's s_waitcnt + s_barrier instructions and assigning them positions in the prologue's stream — a larger plumbing change than just adding the snapshot fields.

The fixup commit (oram-fixup) DELETED the dead-wired CaptureContext fields (prologue_pre_loop_local_write_module, prologue_prefetch_lr_a, prologue_prefetch_lr_b) plus their corresponding kwargs in build_prologue_capture, since they were never assigned at the KernelWriter call sites and constituted dead inputs.

Acceptance criteria for this bead:
- KernelWriter.kernelBody assigns Module snapshots for preLoopLocalWriteDo (LWA/LWB) and the prefetch local-reads (LRA{plrIdx}/LRB{plrIdx}) at their emission sites (~KernelWriter.py:4803 and ~KernelWriter.py:4965-5048).
- KernelWriter.kernelBody also captures the prologue's SWaitCnt + SBarrier instructions and assigns them stream positions ordered with the LR/LW/GR snapshots.
- build_prologue_capture re-introduces the pre_loop_local_write_module / prefetch_lr_a / prefetch_lr_b kwargs (and CaptureContext re-introduces the matching scratch fields).
- validate_edge_wait_coverage passes for prologue->mainloop edges when LR/LW/GR are captured (no MissingWaitFailure / MissingBarrierFailure surfaces from the new prologue-rooted edges).
- New unit test in test_prologue_capture.py asserts at least one prologue->mainloop dataflow edge exists and that validate_edge_wait_coverage returns no failures for that edge class.

P3, soft-deferred.

comments.text:
Empirical confirmation of the prologue capture gap (BPG#11 TF32 4x4 TN, cms=1 fixture).

RAW prologue region (Tensile/Components/kernel_comparison/cms1_kernel.s, lines 1..label_openLoopL:1868):
  - 16 buffer_load_dwordx4 ...lds  (global-read prefetch, e.g. :1578-1592)
  - 9 ds_read                       (local-read prefetch)

CAPTURED PRO body (cms1_capture_listing.txt, "### body PRO: 42 instructions", lines 6-47):
  - 0 buffer_load, 0 ds_read. All 42 are v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32 + v_mfma_f32_4x4x4 (PACK only).

ROOT CAUSE: KernelWriter.py prologue-local block. prologue_interleaved_items is fed ONLY at
KernelWriter.py:5966 with _prologue_snap, derived ONLY from packPrePrefetchItems (the post-_interleavePackAB
PACK stream). The local-read prefetch (localReadCodeA/B at KernelWriter.py:5867,5906) and the global-read
prefetch (globalReadDo at KernelWriter.py:5768,5789 + the PGR>=2 block 5736-5817) are added directly to

(ScheduleCapture.py:2340) takes only prologue_interleaved_items, so it can only ever build a PACK prologue.

BY DESIGN, not oversight: ScheduleCapture.py:2370-2374 docstring and KernelWriter.py:5849-5852 comment both
