title: Decide fate of verify_correct_number_of_instructions (zero unit-test coverage)
description:
# Surprising finding from the audit

`verify_correct_number_of_instructions` (CMSValidator.py:3317) is registered as `InstructionCountRule` (CMSValidator.py:3388) and is part of the `StructuralRule` family — but **has zero direct unit-test coverage** in `Tensile/Tests/unit/`. No `test_Validate*.py` file exercises it; no test imports it.

It checks that the count of each instruction in `optSchedule` matches `context.id_map[instruction_name]` — a structural shape sanity check that runs against the rocisa list before the timeline is built.

## Question to answer

Three options:

1. **Delete the rule** — if its invariant is implicit in `subset_id_map` / id_map construction (i.e. mismatched counts already fail earlier), the rule is dead.
2. **Add unit tests + keep as structural** — instruction-count is fundamentally NOT a dataflow property. The graph cannot express \"there must be exactly N entries of category X\" without ad-hoc instruction-counting (which is what the rule already does). Keeping it structural is correct; we just need test coverage.
3. **Lift count-checking into the graph builder** — make it a precondition validation step before edge formation. Equivalent to (2) but co-located with the graph code.

## Recommendation

Option (2) — instruction-count is an instruction-COUNT property, not a dataflow property, and graphs are inherently the wrong tool. Add a small test file `test_ValidateInstructionCount.py`. The rule itself stays as-is; the migration epic carries it as an explicit \"keep structural\" exception.

## Action

Verify whether the rule is still wired in any production path. If unused, delete. If used, add coverage.
close_reason: completed

title: Test rewrite infra: graph-native CMSValidationTestBase replacement
description:
# Scope

Build the test infrastructure that the four migration sub-beads (ola.1, ola.2, ola.3, ola.4) will all consume. Without this, each migration would re-roll its own fixture pattern.

## What's needed

`Tensile/Tests/unit/cms_validation_base.py` (the current base class) builds a `Timeline` and runs `validator_passes`. The graph-native equivalent should:

1. Take a `FourPartCapture` (constructed via existing `dataflow_fixtures.py` helpers — `make_lr`, `make_gr`, `make_mfma`, `make_swait`, `make_sbarrier`, `make_capture`) instead of the legacy `(optSchedule, syncCode, numCodePaths, ...)` tuple.
2. Build subj graph via `build_dataflow_graph(capture)`.
3. Optionally build a default reference graph (for `compare_graphs`-based tests) or skip (for `validate_edge_wait_coverage`-only tests).
4. Run `compare_graphs(ref, subj)` and/or `validate_edge_wait_coverage(subj)`.
5. Provide the same `expected_failure=Cls, expected_fields={...}` plumbing the legacy base provides — but assert against the failure list returned by the graph passes, not against `timeline._last_failure`.

## Reuse opportunity

The `assert_*` helpers on the legacy base class (`assert_order_inverted`, `assert_timing_too_close`, `assert_scc_conflict`, `assert_out_of_order_sequence`, `assert_wrong_interleaving`) all assert on typed Failure fields and are independent of how the failure was produced. **These can be lifted as-is into the new base class.**

## Adapter shim

To enable incremental migration (one test class at a time), add a translation helper that takes the legacy `optSchedule` dict + `syncCode` list and produces a `FourPartCapture`. This lets us flip a class to the new base without rewriting every test method's fixture body in the same patch.

## Sequencing

This sub-bead unblocks ola.1, ola.2, ola.3, ola.4. Should be done first.
close_reason: completed

comments.author: alvasile
comments.text:
[ola.6] LANDED on branch users/alvasile/ola.6-test-infra (commit baf2f4a49f). Note for ola.1-4 migration agents:

1. Subclass `GraphNativeValidationTest` from Tests/unit/graph_native_validation_base.py — drop the legacy `validator_passes` and `validate(...)` plumbing entirely.

2. Per-test pattern: build a single-body LoopBodyCapture with `dataflow_fixtures.make_lr/gr/swait/sbarrier/mfma/capture`, wrap it via `self.wrap_single_body(ml_cap)`, build the graph with `self.build_graph(cap)`, then call `self.validate_waits(graph)` (single-graph wait coverage) or `self.compare(ref_cap, subj_cap)` (cross-graph diff). Both return a list of typed Failures.

3. Assertion idiom matches the legacy base: `f = self.assert_failure(failures, cls=MissingWaitFailure, counter_kind="vlcnt")` returns the matched Failure for further field introspection (e.g. `self.assert_order_inverted(f, producer_name="GRA", ...)`). Use `assert_failures_contain` when more than one failure may be present, `assert_no_failures` for positive tests. The lifted helpers (`assert_order_inverted` etc.) work for both `.issued_at`-style ValidatorInstruction nodes and `.position`-style GraphNode nodes.

4. There is no adapter shim that translates legacy `(optSchedule, syncCode)` -> FourPartCapture in this commit — the bead spec mentions it as an option but reviewing the existing graph-native tests showed the per-test rewrite is small enough (~10 lines per test) that the shim would mostly add maintenance burden. If you find a per-test rewrite cluster where translation would help (likely the larger TestValidatePack classes), file a follow-up bead and add it.

29 self-tests in test_graph_native_validation_base.py demonstrate every helper. Suite went 623 -> 652 passed.

title: z012-collision: state-register identity collisions in nodes_by_identity (intra-capture; survives Approach A)
description:
**Sub-bead under meta `rocm-libraries-71hw` (Approach A umbrella).**

Single-sentence framing: `nodes_by_identity[node.identity] = node` at `CMSValidator.py:1789` collapses physically-distinct kernel-writer emissions sharing the same canonical render-string into one `GraphNode`; the surviving stream-position is unstable across captures whose interleaving differs, surfacing as false-positive `OrderInvertedFailure`s on state-register edges (SCC, m0).

## Mechanism (verified end-to-end this investigation)

1. `WrappedInstruction.identity_for` (`ScheduleCapture.py:507-536`) returns the 3-tuple `(class_tag, loop_index, canonical_render)`. Class_tag is computed by `class_tag_for_category` (`ScheduleCapture.py:374-426`).
2. `KernelWriterAssembly.globalReadIncrement` (`KernelWriterAssembly.py:9051-9052`) emits `SCmpEQU32(loopCounter, sgpr("StaggerUIter"))` for each tensor side; `globalReadIncrementAB` (`:9173, :9181`) calls it once for A, once for B. Two distinct Python objects, identical canonical render (same writer state ⇒ same sgpr names).
3. Both default-side capture (`build_id_to_category_per_iter`, `ScheduleCapture.py:1074-1077`) and CMS-side (`build_idmap`, `:928-929`) tag the A-side cmp `'GRIncA'` and B-side `'GRIncB'`. The tag-source modules are the same Python objects; the per-side tagging is stable cross-capture.
4. `class_tag_for_category` (`:403-404`) collapses `category.startswith(\"GRInc\") -> 'GRINC'`. Same class_tag, same loop_index, same canonical_render ⇒ **same identity tuple**. Last-writer-wins clobber at `CMSValidator.py:1789`.
5. Same artifact for `s_add_u32 m0, m0, 4224` (per-side GR group; categories `GRA`/`GRB`, both collapsed by `class_tag_for_category:405-406` to `'GR'`).

## Production evidence

`EXAMPLE_YAML_DEFECT_INVESTIGATION.md §1-2` records 8 false `OrderInvertedFailure`s on `example.yaml` against `_get_schedule_160x128x64_TF32`:
- 4× `SCC: GRIncB@3.2 s_cmp_eq_u32 LoopCounterL, StaggerUIter -> GRIncB@3.3 s_cselect_b32` across ML-1 / ML / NGL bodies.
- 3× `m0: GRB@96.1 s_add_u32 m0, m0, 4224 -> GRB@96.2 buffer_load_dwordx4` across ML-1 / ML.

The fix that branch documents (`_producer_has_same_render_peer_with_distinct_category` gate on Phase 1) was a diagnosis-layer carve-out, off-limits per the user's earlier brief.

## Why this survives Approach A

Approach A replaces shadow capture with two real builds (`UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=1` and `=0`). Both real captures independently apply `nodes_by_identity` last-writer-wins; the collision pattern is intra-capture; comparing two captures preserves the artifact. oram.1 (body-label work) is orthogonal — z012-collision happens WITHIN a single body, identical body_label on both endpoints.

## Sibling-investigation cross-checks (incorporated)

- `rocm-libraries-svb1` finding: `class_tag_for_category` already collapses LRSwap/Pack/etc. so most cross-build per-tensor tagging divergences are absorbed at identity-construction time. **Verified this investigation:** `LRSA -> 'LRS'`, `LRSB -> 'LRS'`, `PackA0/PackA3 -> 'PACK'`, `GRIncA -> 'GRINC'`, `GRIncB -> 'GRINC'`. The collapse layer is the surface where z012-collision lives — and where the fix is cheapest.
- `rocm-libraries-aprv` finding: `slot_kind` is NOT in `identity_for`, so it's identity-stable. **But** GRIncA-cmp and GRIncB-cmp share the same `slot_kind` (both inside the loop body, slot_kind=MFMA), so slot_kind cannot disambiguate them. Confirmed.

## Approach catalog (this investigation)

`Z012_ALTERNATIVE_FIXES_INVESTIGATION.md` already enumerates 9 approaches. After incorporating the svb1 collapse-layer finding, the surviving viable approach changed:

### Approach 11 (NEW, recommended) — Selective per-side preservation in `class_tag_for_category`

**Shape.** For categories where BOTH default and CMS paths derive the per-side string from the SAME source modules (no asymmetry), preserve the per-side suffix in the class_tag instead of collapsing.

**Coverage.** GRInc and GR satisfy this (both `build_idmap` and `build_id_to_category_per_iter` tag the same `globalReadIncACode/B` and `globalReadA/B` modules with `GRInc{A,B}` / `GR{A,B}`). LRSwap/LWSwap do NOT — `KernelWriter.py:976,979` tags pointer items with bare `'LRS'`/`'LWS'` on default, while CMS uses per-tensor `LRSA/LRSB/LWSA/LWSB`. So:

```python
if category.startswith(\"GRInc\"):
    return category  # 'GRIncA' or 'GRIncB' — per-side stable cross-capture
if category.startswith(\"GR\"):
    return category if category in (\"GRA\", \"GRB\") else \"GR\"
```

**Cost.** ~6 LoC in `class_tag_for_category`. Update the assertion at `Tests/unit/test_dataflow_graph_comparison.py:593-594` to reflect the new per-side class_tags.

**Risk.**
- Low: relies on a property already verified — `globalReadA/B` and `globalReadIncACode/B` are the same Python modules both capture paths consume.
- Medium watchpoint: if `globalReadCode` (the SIA3-combined module) ever contains items not in `globalReadA + globalReadB`, default-side would tag them bare `'GR'` (via line 1099) while CMS-side wouldn't see them at all. That's a pre-existing asymmetry that the current `class_tag_for_category` happens to absorb. Worth a sentinel: assert in `build_id_to_category_per_iter` that the bare-`'GR'` setdefault never fires for items not also in A/B.
- Bare `'GR'` from default fallback would still flow through identity construction — the new `class_tag_for_category` returns `'GR'` for items that aren't `GRA`/`GRB`, so they'd land under a different class_tag than the CMS-side `'GRA'`/`'GRB'` items. If the bare-'GR' set is non-empty on real schedules, this approach exhibits a new cross-capture identity-set divergence. **Mitigation: add the sentinel assertion AND verify on the cms_to_default test corpus before landing.**

**Blast radius.** Confined to `class_tag_for_category` + one test assertion update. Comparator code unchanged. Edge formation unchanged.

### Approaches reconfirmed dead

The original investigation's catalog (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) is reconfirmed. svb1's collapse-layer finding doesn't revive any of them:
- Approach 1 (position): identity-set diverges by construction.
- Approach 3 (occurrence-index): occurrence is stream-order-dependent.
- Approach 9 (PACK-collapse + cat for rest): now redundant — `class_tag_for_category` already absorbs Pack divergence; the LRSwap test failures Approach 9 hit are still real because LRS asymmetry isn't fixed by collapse, only hidden.

### Backup (if Approach 11's bare-'GR' watchpoint blocks)

Approach 8 (edge filter at construction) remains the silent-suppression fallback the original memo identified as least-bad of the suppression family.

## Recommendation

**Approach 11.** Smallest mechanical change that preserves the cross-capture stability the collapse layer was added to ensure, while restoring the per-side discrimination z012 needs. Pre-landing checklist:
1. Add sentinel assertion in `build_id_to_category_per_iter` that bare-`'GR'` setdefault never fires for items not also in A/B modules. If it never fires on the cms_to_default corpus, GR un-collapse is safe.
2. Run full unit suite (`pytest --ignore=Tests/unit/test_MatrixInstructionConversion.py`) — update `test_dataflow_graph_comparison.py:593-594` and any other class_tag fixtures that hard-code the collapsed values.
3. Verify `example.yaml` end-to-end against `_get_schedule_160x128x64_TF32` — the 8 OrderInverteds should disappear without a diagnosis-layer carve-out.

## Code citations (verified this investigation)

- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1789` — last-writer-wins clobber.
- `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:374-426` — `class_tag_for_category`.
- `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:507-536` — `identity_for` (consumes class_tag at line 535).
- `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:908-947` — `build_idmap` (CMS side, source of `GRIncA/B`, `GRA/B`, `LRSA/B`, `LWSA/B`).
- `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:1017-1117` — `build_id_to_category_per_iter` (default side; lines 1074-1081 for GRInc / GR per-side; line 1099 bare-'GR' fallback).
- `Tensile/KernelWriter.py:974-979` — default-side pointer-LRS/LWS bare-'LRS'/'LWS' tagging (the LRSwap asymmetry that blocks un-collapsing LRS/LWS).
- `Tensile/KernelWriterAssembly.py:9024-9148` — `globalReadIncrement` (the SCmpEQU32 emission); `:9149-9189` `globalReadIncrementAB` (the per-side dual-call).

## Cross-references

- `Tensile/Components/EXAMPLE_YAML_DEFECT_INVESTIGATION.md` — original z012 memo (production failure).
- `Tensile/Components/Z012_ALTERNATIVE_FIXES_INVESTIGATION.md` — 9-approach catalog.
- `Tensile/Components/2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md §6.2 Q2` — z012 cross-link from 2lzd.
- `rocm-libraries-71hw` — meta-bead.

The z012-style same-render collision case (mirrored on the SCC/m0 pattern this bead was filed against) is regression-pinned in EMISSION_ORDINAL_DESIGN.md §6.2 test #3. title: Audit docstrings that reference beads; promote TODOs, delete stale, rewrite rationale
description:
## Why this exists

The `hof` review surfaced doc rot (`2bu`/`pcz`/`034`/`2yk` were all docstring-cleanup beads). The `2bu.x` cascade landed several new docstrings with bead references baked in (`Bead 2bu.3 unification:`, `Bead 2bu.5:`, etc.). Some of those references will themselves become stale as the validator evolves.

This bead does a comprehensive sweep: every docstring (and code comment) that mentions a bead by name gets classified and resolved.

## Scope

All Python source under `Tensile/Components/` and `Tensile/Tests/unit/`. Optionally `Tensile/KernelWriter*.py` if any references slipped in. Markdown files under `Tensile/Components/` (e.g. `LCC_AUDIT.md`, `CMSValidator.md`, `CMSMajorRefactorPlan.md`) are out of scope — those are project records that legitimately reference beads.

Exclude commit messages and bead-tracker entries (`.beads/` directory) — those are historical and untouchable.

## Method

1. **Inventory**: grep for bead references in docstrings + comments. Pattern roughly:
   ```
   grep -rn -E "bead [`'\"]?[0-9a-z]+[`'\"]?|\\bbead `?[0-9a-z]+`?" \
     Tensile/Components/ Tensile/Tests/unit/ \
     | grep -v "^Binary\|\\.md:"
   ```
   Refine the pattern as needed — common shapes: ``bead `xyz` ``, `Bead xyz:`, `(bead xyz)`, `per bead xyz`.

2. **Classify each match** into one of three buckets:

   **A. TODO / future-work** — "deferred to bead X", "follow-up in X", "X will replace this". Open question: is the referenced bead still open? If yes, the comment is fine (just verify the bead exists). If no, the bead is closed and the comment is stale → either delete or convert to a fresh bead.

   **B. Stale** — references a closed bead that no longer governs the surrounding code. Common shapes: "post-bead X this works differently" where the post-X behavior is now the only behavior; "bead X added Y" where Y is just plain code now. These should be deleted; the surrounding code documents itself.

   **C. Rationale** — explains WHY the code does what it does, with the bead as historical citation ("Bead X established that mfma_free_at carries across body boundaries because..."). Rewrite to remove the bead mention; keep the rationale. The future reader doesn't need to chase bead X to understand the code.

3. **Action per bucket**:
   - **A**: file new bead if the referenced bead is closed/missing AND the TODO is still relevant. Cross-link.
   - **B**: delete the comment.
   - **C**: rewrite the comment, preserving the technical content but dropping the bead citation. The bead history stays in commit messages; the docstring should be self-contained.

## Why this matters

Bead names (`hof`, `2bu`, `wx9.4`, `ola.2`) are opaque to anyone who didn't live through the migration. A docstring that says "post-bead `8nz` the structural simulator is deleted" is doc rot the moment a new reader looks at it — they have to grep beads to learn that the *structural simulator no longer exists*, which the surrounding code already shows. The bead reference adds nothing for the new reader and inflates cognitive load.

Same code today should read: "the cumulative_issue_cycles helper is the single source of truth for issue-time accounting" — no bead reference, self-contained.

## Examples to expect

From the recent `2bu.x` cascade (just merged):

- `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` docstring: "Bead `2bu.3` unification: same-body and cross-body share ONE code path..." → rewrite to "Same-body and cross-body share one code path..." (the historical attribution belongs in commit messages, not the live docstring).
- `_cvt_to_mfma_gap_ok` docstring: "Bead `2bu.4` unification: ... the previous slot-delta formula ... was DOUBLE-COUNTING ..." → rewrite to drop the "Bead 2bu.4 unification" lead but KEEP the "previous formula was double-counting" warning IF that warning is still actionable for future readers (e.g. if anyone might be tempted to revert).
- Anything that says "deferred to bead X" where X is closed → either delete (deferred work is done) or file a fresh bead.

## Output

A migration table similar to the `wao` bead's output, listing every reference by file:line, its bucket (A/B/C), and the resolution action. Land the changes as one or more commits ([audit] prefix). New beads filed get IDs in the table.

## Why P2

Doc rot accumulates. The `2bu.x` cascade alone added ~30+ bead references in docstrings. If we don't sweep periodically, every future bead piles on top. This is also the kind of cleanup that's easy to incrementally verify (no behavior change; just `pytest` to confirm nothing regresses).

## Related

- `034` (P3) — stale cmw-formula docstrings (subset of this bead's scope; `034` is narrow, this one is broad).
- `yx3` (P?) — audit unnecessary comments / decorative headers (broader cleanup; partial overlap).
- `fnf` (P2 epic) — typed signatures + stub audit (separate scope but co-bench-able if dispatched together).
close_reason: Cherry-picked into validator_long_term_plans as e3c7fd53c6, 130a7e2fdd. ~95 stale bead citations deleted, ~30 rewritten as bead-free rationale, 5 hof references kept (only open referenced bead). ONT_AUDIT.md added. Conflict on CMSValidator.py + ScheduleCapture.py with fnf resolved by keeping fnf's typed signatures + ont's cleaner docstrings. 583 passed at HEAD.

title: CaptureConsistencyError on LR/MFMA identities masks downstream residuals (p39d et al.) in real-vs-real compare_graphs
description:
**Surfaced by xj16's inline real-vs-real assertion + y391/l1l6's snapshot mechanism.** First thing `compare_graphs` hits on every TF32 fixture; aborts before any other residual can surface.

## Reproducer

Pinned in commit fedfd4f3119 by `test_non_cms_reference_compare_graphs_surfaces_only_known_residuals` (test_approach_a_non_cms_reference.py post-l1l6). Real-YAML smoke: `Tensile --build-only` on `custom_mainloop_scheduling_tf32.yaml` for gfx950 dies on Step 0 with:

```
CaptureConsistencyError: compare_graphs: data-flow node identity sets differ.
  in reference but not subject: 52 identities ({'LR': 26, 'MFMA': 26})
  in subject but not reference: 52 identities ({'MFMA': 26, 'LR': 26})
```

(Counts are 28-per-side for some fixtures, 52-per-side for others; the shape — LR/MFMA-only, symmetric per-side — is consistent.)

## Mechanism (Q2 framing — expected)

Per 2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md §6.2 Q2: validation is YAML-in-two-builds-out; whatever Tensilelite mutates internally on either side is accepted as 'what that build does.' The CMS schedule pipelines LR/MFMA across iteration boundaries differently from the non-CMS scheduler — same set of logical loads + MFMAs, **different physical layout positions** → different identity tuples → identity-set divergence.

This is an EXPECTED divergence per the Q2 framing — not a bug in either side's emission, but a consequence of CMS's whole point (different scheduling).

## Why it matters

`compare_graphs` raises `CaptureConsistencyError` BEFORE running its OrderInverted / wait-coverage / edge-coverage checks. So every other residual class downstream is currently MASKED:
- rocm-libraries-p39d (GR OrderInverted in ML) — confirmed masked, see p39d's 2026-05-27 comment + commit 4f61ba92d55's Phase 1 test
- Any future per-edge / per-ordering divergence — would similarly be invisible

xj16's real-YAML smoke (the inline assertion path) cannot make forward progress on TF32 fixtures until this is addressed. The TF32 YAML build dies on Step 0; subsequent steps that might surface other classes never run.

## Resolution direction (NOT implemented — needs user decision)

Three categories of fix, parallel to p39d's option set:

**(A) Tolerance**: extend `compare_graphs` with an LR/MFMA identity-set tolerance — when both sides have the same LR and MFMA *counts* but different identity tuples, treat as expected divergence. Risk: masks real cases where CMS drops a load entirely.

**(B) Identity loosening**: change the LR/MFMA identity tuple to be position-insensitive (drop the position component from `identity_for`). Symmetric with hdem's body-blindness for cross-body comparison. Risk: loses positional information from valid checks.

**(C) Pre-comparison alignment**: a new phase before `compare_graphs` that normalizes the per-side LR/MFMA streams to a canonical order, so the identity sets match before set-difference runs. Cleanest but biggest change.

Likely the right answer is (A) with an explicit `accept_identity_count_match` flag, but the user has 'no tactical fixes' policy. Worth design discussion.

## Acceptance criterion

- `compare_graphs` no longer raises `CaptureConsistencyError` on the TF32 CMS YAML's first fixture (`_192x256x32_TF32 NN` or whichever the first hit is on `custom_mainloop_scheduling_tf32.yaml`).
- The l1l6-pinned test (`test_non_cms_reference_compare_graphs_surfaces_only_known_residuals`) re-pins to whatever shape surfaces next (which may be p39d's 3 OrderInverted residuals, finally visible).
- Real-YAML smoke can progress beyond Step 0 on the TF32 YAML.

## Dependencies

- **Hard-blocks**: xj16 (the YAML smoke acceptance) on the TF32 side.
- **Masks**: p39d (when this resolves, p39d's residual becomes visible — they're sequenced).
- **Soft-related**: zvzu, 6hk3 (other classifier/divergence classes; sequencing among the four may shift as each lands).

## References

- Commit fedfd4f3119 (l1l6) — pins the shape
- Commit 5224166bf6b (xj16) — the inline-assert path that surfaces it
- Commit 4f61ba92d55 (p39d minimal reproducer) — confirms masking of p39d
- 2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md §6.2 Q2 — the Q2 framing
- approach_a.py — the snapshot consumer
- Solution.py pre_cms_state() — the snapshot producer
- CMSValidator.py:3654 area — where CaptureConsistencyError is raised
close_reason: Resolved by the count-based gate that landed in commit 4b0ba2809bc on the validator branch. oplb's symptom ('CaptureConsistencyError on LR/MFMA identities aborts before any other residual can surface') was the pre-gate behavior of compare_graphs raising on benign identity-set differences. The count-gate replaced the identity-set check with per-(rocisa-derived InstructionCategory) count comparison, which only raises on real pipeline-integrity defects. The unrolled-walk plan (UNROLLED_VALIDATION_PLAN.md §4.1) preserves this gate as-is.

## First failure identified (TF32 YAML)

Kernel: **_192x256x32_TF32 TN** branch (NOT NN as the bead's placeholder said).

- YAML site: `custom_mainloop_scheduling_tf32.yaml:38-76` — the very first BenchmarkProblemSizeGroup in the TF32 YAML
- Step name: `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_S_MX_B_UserArgs_00`
- MatrixInstruction: [16, 16, 32, 1, 1, 6, 8, 2, 2] → MT 192×256, DepthU 32
- TF32 TN (TransposeA=1, TransposeB=0, DataType=S, F32XdlMathOp=X)
- CMS flags: UseCustomMainLoopSchedule: [1], UsePLRPack: [1]
- Identity divergence: 52 per side, exactly {'LR': 26, 'MFMA': 26}

Diff is in ds_read_b128 LDS-read offsets — same instruction class, same destination vgpr ranges, but CMS chose different offsets to fit its overlap pattern vs the non-CMS scheduler's natural offsets. The MFMA side mirrors symmetrically.

Site of raise: KernelWriter.py:5841 (xj16's inline assertion) → CMSValidator.py:3654 (compare_graphs).

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## 2026-05-27: root cause of identity divergence identified — register-naming, not addresses

Investigation artifacts in worktree at /home/alvasile/rocm-libraries/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac4cb82131af059f7/projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/oplb_artifacts/ (raw asm + extracted LR/MFMA sequences + diffs + README).

### What the divergence ACTUALLY is

Both sides emit **exactly the same 24 distinct LDS offsets** with **exactly the same 28 ds_read_b128 instructions per iteration** and **exactly the same 172 MFMAs**. There is no missing read, no extra read, no different address.

Two real divergences:

1. **Ordering**: CMS groups the LDS1 (second-buffer) reads by operand — 8 B-reads then 6 A-reads contiguous. non-CMS interleaves them by mfma-consumption order — [A,A],[B,B],[A,A],[A,A],[B,B,B,B]. Reads 1-14 (LDS0) are byte-identical between both.

2. **Register naming** (this is what compare_graphs actually trips on): CMS uses alternating `vgprValuA_T0_I0+N` and `vgprValuA_X0_I0+N` destinations — the **UsePLRPack double-register-file naming** for the rotating pack buffer. non-CMS uses only `_T0_I0` linearly. Same physical register count, same physical operand role, different SYMBOLIC names.

### Why this matters for the fix

`compare_graphs` builds its identity tuple from `(canonical_render, emission_ordinal)` where `canonical_render` includes the rendered instruction text. So:
- CMS:     `ds_read_b128 v[vgprValuA_X0_I0+0:...], ...`
- non-CMS: `ds_read_b128 v[vgprValuA_T0_I0+0:...], ...`

Are **different identity tuples** even though they read the same LDS offset to the same physical vgpr. That's the entire 52-per-side divergence: 26 LR identities are CMS's `_X0_I0` reads (not in non-CMS), 26 LR identities are non-CMS's `_T0_I0` reads that CMS moved to `_X0_I0`. MFMA mirrors symmetrically (the MFMAs consume the same renamed registers).

### Reframes the resolution

Original three options (A/B/C) don't quite fit. The actual fix shape is **symbolic-register-name normalization**: canonicalize `_T0_I0` and `_X0_I0` to the same logical slot before computing the identity tuple. The PLR pack-buffer rotation is an implementation detail of `UsePLRPack` that doesn't change the kernel's dataflow.

This is smaller and more targeted than the originally-listed options. It also surgically preserves cross-build identity coverage for cases where CMS genuinely emits different instructions (vs just renaming).

Recommend: a new option (D) added to the bead — "register-name canonicalization layer in identity_for() / WrappedInstruction.canonical_str(): treat `_T0_I0` and `_X0_I0` as the same logical slot." Plus a comment in approach_a.py / Solution.py explaining the PLR-pack pack-buffer rotation rationale.

## 2026-05-27: minimal reproducer + dataflow-graph PNGs landed

Commit 49ed3c76efa on users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans adds test_oplb_register_naming_minimal.py (755 lines, 6 tests).

### Test phases

- **Phase 1 (real-kernel anchor)**: builds _192x256x32_TF32 TN via _make_solution + build_non_cms_reference. Pinned: CaptureConsistencyError with 52 identities per side, {LR: 26, MFMA: 26} — matches the production failure exactly. GRA/GRB confirmed ABSENT from the diff (so p39d-class GR-OrderInverted residuals remain masked behind this gate, per oplb's masking story).

- **Phase 2 (trimmed minimal)**: 4 DSLoadB128 + 1 VCvtPkF32toBF16 per side using real rocisa instances. CMS-side uses alternating T0_I0/X0_I0 destinations; non-CMS-side uses linear T0_I0. compare_graphs raises CaptureConsistencyError with exactly **4 LR identities per side, no MFMA divergence** (the minimal body has no MFMAs).

The trimmed phase **proves the divergence is intrinsic to symbolic register naming** — same shape (LR identity-set mismatch) reproduces at 5-instruction scale with no MFMA/scheduling/pipelining context.

### Side-effect: PNG dataflow graphs

oplb_artifacts/figures/oplb_minimal_cms.png (104 KB)
oplb_artifacts/figures/oplb_minimal_noncms.png (103 KB)

Generated via Tensile.Components.CMSValidatorVisualization.visualize_dataflow_graph (matplotlib backend; PNG dispatched via .png extension natively). Viewable side-by-side: a developer sees the T0_I0 vs T0+X0_I0 naming difference visually.

### Pack note

VCvtPkF32toBF16 identity differs across sides (Pack srcs differ because their LR producers' destinations differ), but Pack is NOT in _DATA_FLOW_CATEGORIES — so it doesn't contribute to the identity-set gate. Only LR/LW/GR/MFMA do. This is why Phase 2 pins '4 LR' rather than '4 LR + 1 Pack.'

### What this enables

When oplb's fix lands (option D: register-name canonicalization in identity_for or WrappedInstruction.canonical_str — treat _T0_I0 and _X0_I0 as the same logical slot), this test's assertions flip to 'no failures' / 'graphs equivalent.' A 7-second test that pins exactly what the fix needs to undo.

title: Quad-cycle Sub-C: 4x4 PackMFMA -> CVT1 5-cycle gap in graph
description:
## Rule

`QUAD_CYCLES_MFMA_4X4_BEFORE_CVT1 = 5` (CMSValidator.py:276). When
a 4x4 Pack-MFMA writes the accumulator, the downstream CVT1 (the
second `v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32` in the TF32 pack group) must wait 5
quad-cycles before reading it. This is the LARGEST gap among the
four constants and the most likely to cause a real miscompile.

## Currently checked at

`CMSValidator.py:1783-1785`: `MFMAPack.min_quad_cycles_before_result_used = 5`.
Same `Pack.validate` path as Sub-B.

## Why this is hard

The producer is a 4x4 PackMFMA (categorized "Pack*" with rocisa class
MFMAInstruction). The consumer is a CVTPack (categorized "Pack*" too).
Currently both are caught by the `_is_alu_producer` exemption — no
quad-cycle check fires.

This depends on Sub-A's `_is_mfma_producer` distinction landing first
(so the PackMFMA producer is recognized as MFMA-class).

## Plan

1. Block on Sub-A.
2. After Sub-A, the PackMFMA producer routes through `_quad_cycle_gap_ok`
   which uses `_finish_cycles_for(producer) = 1`. But the rule here
   requires the GAP between PackMFMA finish and CVT1 read to be 5,
   not just `mfma_finish_cycles` (1). The current formula
   `slot_delta * (1 + finish) - 1` yields `slot_delta*2 - 1` for
   PackMFMA — that's 1 at slot_delta=1, 3 at slot_delta=2, 5 at
   slot_delta=3.
3. Therefore the gap check needs a per-PAIR threshold lookup, not just
   per-PRODUCER. Promote `_quad_cycle_gap_ok` to take an `expected`
   argument resolved by `_expected_gap_for_pair(producer, consumer)`.
4. The dispatch table:
   - (MFMA, MFMA-acc-consumer) → 3
   - (PackMFMA, MFMA-acc-consumer) → 1
   - (PackMFMA, CVT1) → 5  ← this rule
   - (CVTPack, MFMA) → 2  ← Sub-B
5. Add `TestPackMFMAToCVT1QuadCycleGap` covering: slot_delta in
   {1,2,3,4}, expect failure for delta < 3 (gap < 5).

## Open question

For TF32 emulation pack groups (size 10 = CVT0×4 + MFMAPack×2 + CVT1×4),
how does the kernel writer typically schedule? If the natural schedule
already has slot_delta>=3 between MFMAPack and CVT1, this rule rarely
fires in practice — but a regression in scheduling code would silently
produce wrong results without the check.

## Files

- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1783-1785` — current site
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:469-486` — MFMAPack class
- `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_ValidatePack.py:1179,1218,1258` — TimingTooCloseFailure assertions
close_reason: completed

title: Investigate capturing the pre-mainloop prologue (GR warmup, initial LRs, usePLRPack Packs)
description:
## Why this exists

The current FourPartCapture (`ScheduleCapture.py:299-317`) covers only the steady-state mainloop:
- `main_loop` — the unrolled mainloop body (per codepath)
- `main_loop_prev` — verbatim clone of `main_loop`
- `n_gl` — no-load-loop with GR still firing (tail iteration)
- `n_ll` — no-load-loop with neither GR nor LR (final tail iteration)

Capture is wired into the pipeline at the mainloop dispatcher (`simdSpecDispatch` at `KernelWriter.py:4587`, observed via `customMainLoopSchedule` for the CMS path). By that point, the kernel module already contains the **pre-mainloop prologue**:

- The initial round of GR (global read) instructions that warm the LDS for the first prefetch generation.
- The first round of LR (local read) instructions that prefetch into VGPRs.
- For `UsePLRPack=1`: the initial Pack instructions that materialize the first mainloop iteration's MFMA inputs.

These are invisible to `compare_graphs`, so any CMS-vs-default divergence in prologue *register dependencies* — specifically dependencies that cross the prologue/mainloop boundary into the first iteration — is silently uncaught.

## What goes wrong without this

The validator's contract is currently 'CMS produces an equivalent steady-state mainloop to the default schedule.' That is weaker than the user-facing intent ('CMS produces an equivalent kernel') in one specific way: if CMS's prologue stages a different register layout than the default schedule's prologue, the FIRST mainloop iteration's MFMA inputs come from different physical registers — even though every subsequent iteration's MFMA dependencies look identical under `compare_graphs`. The validator would not flag this.

This is not a known active bug — no schedule has been observed producing a divergent prologue. But it's a structural gap in the validation contract, and the deferred-expansion architecture from rocm-libraries-dj1g makes this a natural follow-up: dj1g already established that CMS-side capture mirrors the default-side capture's body shape; the same mirroring approach should extend to the prologue if it's captured at all.

## Phase 1 — Investigation (no implementation)

Answer these questions in a research memo (`Tensile/Components/PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md`):

### Q1: Where is the prologue emitted?

- Walk the kernelBody flow in `KernelWriter.py` from where customMainLoopSchedule lands (`:4581`) down to where `simdSpecDispatch` is added (`:4587`). Identify every code-emission call between 'kernel header' and 'mainloop dispatch' that emits GR/LR/Pack instructions.
- Specifically locate: the initial GR loads, the prefetch LRs, and the usePLRPack Pack chain (when applicable).
- For each: what function emits it, what kernel-config flags gate it, and what's the natural hook for capture?

### Q2: What shape would capture take?

- Should this be a fifth part of `FourPartCapture` (becoming `FivePartCapture` or renamed)? Or a separate `PrologueCapture` object?
- Does the CMS path even have a parallel prologue, or is the prologue identical between CMS=0 and CMS=1 codepaths? (If identical, the comparison is trivial — just verify shape equality.)
- What's the right granularity — a single body capture, or one per codepath like `main_loop`?

### Q3: Cross-boundary edges

- Today, `compare_graphs` builds dataflow graphs per body. Edges that span the prologue→first-mainloop boundary cannot be expressed because both endpoints aren't in the same graph.
- Is the right model 'concatenate prologue + main_loop into a single graph and compare those'? Or 'two separate graphs with a documented boundary contract'?
- How does `validate_edge_wait_coverage` extend — does it need to span the boundary too, or does it stay per-body?

### Q4: What real divergences would this catch?

- Manually construct (or hypothesize) a CMS schedule where the prologue stages a different register layout than the default schedule's prologue. What would `compare_graphs` report today (silent pass)? What should it report?
- Survey the existing CMS schedules in `Tensile/Components/CustomSchedule.py`: do any of them touch prologue emission, or do they all leave it to the default-side scheduler?
- If all current CMS schedules leave the prologue untouched (likely), this gap is latent — important to surface, but not actively producing bugs.

## Phase 2 — Ask questions

After Phase 1's memo, ask the user:
- Is this gap worth closing now, or document and defer?
- Capture shape: extend FourPartCapture or new object?
- Comparison shape: single concatenated graph or boundary contract?
- Should usePLRPack-vs-non-usePLRPack be tested explicitly as a divergence-catching shape?

## Phase 3 — Implementation

Only after Phase 2 converges. TDD: write the test that catches a hypothesized divergence first, then implement capture+comparison to make it pass.

## Hard rules

- Phase 1 is research only. No code changes.
- Reference the dj1g architecture (commit `c1054a019c` on vlt) — the deferred-expansion pattern is the template for any prologue capture extension.
- The investigation should explicitly check whether this overlaps with the d0xd symbolic-register epic (some prologue divergences may manifest as different symbolic-register names across CMS vs default).

## Out of scope

- The kernel epilogue (post-mainloop tail). That's its own can of worms; this bead is prologue-only.
- Anything related to grouped GEMM, Stream-K, or GSU prologues — single-GEMM standard prologue first.
- Implementation of any actual capture extension (Phase 3, deferred).

## Why P2

title: Investigate compare_graphs body_label-sensitivity for cross-body pipelining (UsePLRPack)
description:
## TL;DR

`compare_graphs` (`Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:3275-3358`) builds identity tuples that bake `body_label` into identity (`(class_tag, loop_index, canonical_render)` at `ScheduleCapture.py:507-536`). Edge keys (`CMSValidator.py:1238`) further encode `loop_index` via `producer.position` / `consumer.position`. The result: a Pack producer that emits in body PRO on one side and body ML-1 on the other — even with identical canonical render text and identical class_tag — produces non-matching identities and non-matching edge keys. `compare_graphs` fires spurious failures.

This is a Phase 3 blocker for the prologue-capture work (parent bead `rocm-libraries-oram`). Specifically, it blocks Decision 4(b)'s "BOTH MUST PASS" semantic from being implementable under contract (a) of `rocm-libraries-2lzd`.

## Background — verified pipelining model

Walked KernelWriter.py end-to-end. Confirmed that `UsePLRPack` is pipelining-only at the symbolic-register level:

- When `usePLRPack=True` (`KernelWriter.py:4961`), the per-subiter `packCodeA/B` returned by prefetch `localReadDo` is added to `packPrePrefetchA/B` (`:5009, :5048`) and then appended directly to `module` via `addItems` (`:5088`) — i.e., into the prologue.
- When `usePLRPack=False`, the same pack code lands in `pack[plrIdx]` (`:5011, :5050`) and is consumed by `_makeSubIterSchedule` during steady-state mainloop iterations.
- The producer-consumer rotation is at `KernelWriter.py:3289-3301`: `packStoreIdx = (uNext + pflr) % numPackBuffer` while `packIdx = u % numPackBuffer` — i.e., pack stores N iterations ahead of where MFMA reads.
- Empirical: `v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32` count is 128 (cms) vs 320 (default), uniform 2.5× ratio across all op classes — the 2.5× is just `.macro MAINLOOP` vs inline expansion.

Per-iteration pack count is invariant. Total pack count is invariant modulo iteration-0/iteration-N boundary tricks. The dataflow IS equivalent.

Full evidence in `Tensile/Components/PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §"Phase 3 blocker: compare_graphs identity is body-label-sensitive" §1.

## The blocker

`compare_graphs` cannot match dataflow-equivalent edges across bodies because identity carries `loop_index`. Specifically:

1. **Identity** (`ScheduleCapture.py:534`): `loop_idx = BODY_LABEL_TO_LOOP_INDEX[body_label]` is the second tuple element.
2. **edge_keys** (`CMSValidator.py:1238`): `producer.position` and `consumer.position` are full `SchedulePosition` (loop_index, stream_index) tuples.
3. **Data-flow node identity gate** (`CMSValidator.py:3306`): walks LR/LW/GR/MFMA only, so PACK is exempt — the gate doesn't directly catch PACK identity drift across bodies, but downstream missing-edge classifiers do (and incorrectly).
4. **Legitimate-CMS-reorder branch** (`diagnose_missing_edge:3417-3424`): requires identity equality on both endpoints, which fails when `loop_index` differs.

Concrete failure: CMS+UsePLRPack=True kernel emits prologue Pack chain in PRO body (loop_index=-1); default+UsePLRPack=False kernel emits dataflow-equivalent producers in ML-1 / ML body (loop_index=0/1). `compare_graphs` reports `OrderInvertedFailure` or unexplained-missing-edge raises despite the dataflow being identical.

Full analysis in `PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §2 / §4 / §5.

## Why existing UsePLRPack tests pass anyway

`test_whole_kernel_useplrpack_cms_matches_both_defaults` (`Tests/unit/test_prologue_capture.py:277-350`) currently passes because the CMS-side capture inherits the default-side prologue verbatim via `build_cms_four_part_capture(prologue=default_capture.prologue, ...)` (asserted at `:342`). Both sides have IDENTICAL prologue bodies — no body-label drift to detect.

The blocker surfaces when the test setup lets CMS and default sides derive prologues independently (which is what 4(b)'s "BOTH MUST PASS" semantic under contract (a) actually demands).

## 5 candidate approaches

Sketched in `PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §4 with mechanism + cost + risk:

- **A. Drop body_label from identity** — simplest (~5 LoC); risk: cross-body identity collisions weaken the identity-coverage gate.
- **B. Body-label-equivalence layer** — bucket loop indices into iteration buckets (~20 LoC); risk: arbitrary bucket boundaries.
- **C. Cross-body pipeline-aware comparison** — keep identity, add fallback in diagnose_missing_edge (~80-150 LoC); risk: register-rotation canonicalization complexity.
- **D. Symbolic-register rotation canonicalization** — bake pipelining into canonical_str (~50-100 LoC); risk: requires d0xd-style numerization, threading iteration context through API.
- **E. Compare at edge-level with structural identity** — switch edge_key matching from identity to resource-write-key/read-key (~150-300 LoC); risk: large scope, needs d0xd resolution layer.

Plus hybrids (A+C, B+E, D+E) — full discussion in the memo.

## Interaction with rocm-libraries-2lzd

This issue is separate from but coupled to 2lzd (validator's reference is fictional). 2lzd's resolution shapes which approach is most useful:

- If 2lzd adopts contract (a) and rebuilds references against UsePLRPack=False, body-label-sensitivity becomes the next-most-proximate false-positive source.
- If 2lzd adopts contract (b) and forces UsePLRPack to be held constant on both sides, body-label-sensitivity stays masked but unfixed for future schedules that drift producers across body boundaries.
- 2lzd's cause-(B)/(B-2) (double-tagging the same physical leaf under two category names) interacts directly with Approach C — a cross-body pipeline-aware fallback would naturally absorb both.

Cross-link comment added to rocm-libraries-2lzd (this commit).

## What this bead asks

1. User decision: which approach (A-E or hybrid) to pursue, or document and defer if 4(b)'s test is rescoped to compare against UsePLRPack=True default only (today's test path).
2. If pursuing A-E: scope a Phase-3 implementation memo before any code lands. The fix touches the comparator core and risks regressing existing comparison tests (validator_long_term_plans has dozens).
3. Coordinate with rocm-libraries-2lzd Phase-2 decisions — the contract choice there shapes the urgency here.

## Pointers

- Memo: `Tensile/Components/PRELOOP_CAPTURE_PHASE1.md` §"Phase 3 blocker: compare_graphs identity is body-label-sensitive".
- Identity construction: `Tensile/Components/ScheduleCapture.py:507-536` (`identity_for`); `:702-708` (`BODY_LABEL_TO_LOOP_INDEX`).
- Edge keys: `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1238` (`edge_keys`).
- Identity gate: `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:3306-3336`.
- Cross-body reorder branch: `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:3417-3424`.
- Pipelining model: `Tensile/KernelWriter.py:4961` (`usePLRPack`); `:5009/:5048` (prologue route); `:5011/:5050` (mainloop route); `:3289-3301` (rotation).
- Existing UsePLRPack tests: `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_prologue_capture.py`.

## Out of scope

- Implementation. This is investigation / decision capture only.
- Fixing 2lzd. The interaction is documented; resolution is independent.
- Symbolic-register epic d0xd. Approaches D and E lean on it but it's not a prerequisite for the catalog itself.

Recommendation recorded in ORAM1_PRINCIPLED_APPROACH_INVESTIGATION.md and accepted by user in comment 80 on 2026-05-12 (post B/C/H ruling). Implementation tracked by rocm-libraries-hdem (blocked-by 4up4 and xqj3). Specifically:

- **Under 2lzd Approach A (true non-CMS reference build):** body-label-sensitivity becomes the immediate proximate false-positive source on every cross-build comparison. Pipelined producers will drift across body boundaries (PRO ↔ ML iter i ↔ ML iter i+1) under UsePLRPack flips; today's identity construction at ScheduleCapture.py:507-536 bakes loop_index into identity, so drifted producers fail to match. **Fixing oram.1 is a prerequisite for A.**

- **Under 2lzd Approach H (cms_from_default-driven synthesis; both sides are real CMS builds):** body-label sensitivity sidesteps itself by construction. Identical body shape on both sides — no producer drift across body boundaries. H implementations need zero changes to compare_graphs. If 2lzd lands H, oram.1 may close as 'obsoleted by H'.

- **Under 2lzd Approach D (drop comparison entirely; validate against schedule slot table):** oram.1 is moot — no cross-graph comparison happens, identity construction across two captures never runs.

comments.author: alvasile
comments.text:
Chosen-approach decision recorded 2026-05-12 (post B/C/H ruling).

Per investigation memo `Tensile/Components/ORAM1_PRINCIPLED_APPROACH_INVESTIGATION.md` (this commit): the principled and clean approach is **Approach A + Approach E together as a single design unit**:

- **A**: drop `loop_index` from the identity tuple (post-4up4: `(canonical_render, emission_ordinal)`).
- **E**: switch `DataflowGraph.edge_keys` from instruction-identity to resource byte-key matching: `(producer_write_byte_key, consumer_read_byte_key, edge_kind, intra_operand_byte_offset, src_operand_slot, sink_operand_slot)`.

Body sensitivity has two structural carriers — identity (`loop_index` slot) and edge-key (`producer.position` / `consumer.position` carry `loop_index`). A removes carrier 1; E removes carrier 2. Either alone leaves a residual; together they close the blocker without leaving residual carriers. Both layers become rocisa-derived (`canonical_render`, `emission_ordinal`, byte-key, operand-slot indices), satisfying xqj3.

D was evaluated and rejected: D solves a different-axis problem (same-body cross-iteration register rotation), which E's byte-key matching handles correctly anyway. D adds plumbing without unique coverage.

False-positive risk for A+E: 1 (LOW; cross-body resource byte-key coincidence). False-negative risk: 0 enumerated.

Sequencing:
1. 4up4 lands (`(loop_index, canonical_render, emission_ordinal)` tuple).
2. **A+E lands as one PR** (filed as `rocm-libraries-hdem`).
3. svb1 (independent).
4. 71hw consumes the cleaned comparator semantics.

Implementation tracked under `rocm-libraries-hdem` (parent: oram.1; blocked by: 4up4; under xqj3 umbrella). Full memo at `Tensile/Components/ORAM1_PRINCIPLED_APPROACH_INVESTIGATION.md` (commit landing alongside this comment).

title: General PGR/PLR support in validator: investigate valid combinations + per-combination validator behavior
description:
## Why this exists

Surfaced during 71f hypothesis verification. The empty-NGL crash on `PGR=1, PLR=0` is one symptom of a deeper problem: the validator's body-capture machinery and `build_dataflow_graph` empty-body assertion encode implicit assumptions about which (PGR, PLR) combinations produce which body shapes, but those assumptions aren't documented anywhere and weren't audited.

Fixing only the (PGR=1, PLR=0) case in isolation risks breaking other (PGR, PLR) combinations or papering over latent bugs in shapes that aren't currently in the test fixture set. Need to investigate the full matrix BEFORE fixing.

## Investigation scope

### Phase A: enumerate valid (PGR, PLR) combinations (no validator changes)

1. **What are the supported PGR values?** Per Tensile docs / source. Known so far: 0, 1, 2 (PGR=2 is double-buffered prefetch). Confirm exhaustive list.

2. **What are the supported PLR values?** Per Tensile docs / source. Known so far: 0, 1. Confirm whether higher values are supported and where.

3. **Which combinations are mutually valid?** Are all (PGR, PLR) cross-products legal, or are there forbidden pairs? Document constraints.

4. **For each valid (PGR, PLR) combination**, which body phases (ML-1, ML, NGL, NLL) are emitted by KernelWriter? Trace through:
   - The mainloop emit path (`_loopBody` and friends in KernelWriter.py).
   - The noLoadLoop emit path (`noLoadLoop` and OptNLL/OrdNLL labels).
   - Any conditional NGL emit logic — there must be one, since (PGR=1, PLR=0) and (PGR=2, PLR=1) produce different NGL shapes.

5. **For each valid (PGR, PLR) combination**, which combinations are legal under SIA=3 (graph-native validator-eligible) and which under SIA=0/1/2 (legacy paths)?

6. **Which (PGR, PLR) combinations are reachable via `UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=1`?** This is the only path the validator currently sees. The CMS-registration question (w9p) overlaps here — CMS=1 may itself constrain (PGR, PLR).

### Phase B: per-combination validator behavior audit (no validator changes)

For each (PGR, PLR) combination identified in Phase A as legal under CMS=1:

- What does the capture machinery populate for ML-1 / ML / NGL / NLL?
- Does `build_dataflow_graph` succeed, raise CaptureEmptyBodyError, or produce a wrong graph?
- Use the existing probe (`Tensile/Components/GFX1151_AUDIT/validator_coverage_probe.py`) extended with a synthetic-yaml generator OR pull samples from existing yamls across architectures (CDNA 4 + gfx1151) to cover the matrix.

Output: a coverage matrix table:

| PGR | PLR | Bodies emitted | Capture populates | Validator outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | ... | ... | ... |
| 1 | 0 | ML, NLL (no NGL) | n_gl[0]=empty | CRASHES (CaptureEmptyBodyError) |
| 1 | 1 | ML-1, ML, NGL, NLL | all populated | OK (or identify which fail) |
| 2 | 0 | ... | ... | ... |
| 2 | 1 | ML-1, ML, NGL, NLL | all populated | OK (per probe data) |
| 2 | 2 | ... | ... | ... |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |

### Phase C: design — generalize validator support (no implementation)

Based on Phase A+B findings, design how the validator should handle ALL legal combinations. Options to evaluate:

1. **Capture-side fix**: only populate `ctx.default_n_gl` (and similar) when the body is actually emitted by the kernel. Body absence becomes `None`, not empty. `build_dataflow_graph`'s existing `if 0 not in by_cp: continue` guard then handles it cleanly.

2. **Graph-build-side fix**: relax `build_dataflow_graph` to treat empty bodies as 'no body present' rather than 'data missing', based on a structural predicate (PLR=0 ⇒ no NGL, etc).

3. **Hybrid**: capture-side honesty (only populate when emitted) + a sanity check at graph-build time that any populated body has at least one instruction (so empty-body errors still catch real bugs in the capture path).

Recommend one. Write up the design in this bead's closing comment. Implementation is OUT of scope for this bead — file a follow-up implementation bead under 71f.

## Hard requirements

- **No validator code changes under this bead.** Investigation + design only. Implementation lives in a follow-up.
- **Findings must cover ALL legal (PGR, PLR) combinations**, not just the ones in the gfx1151 HHS yaml. CDNA 4 yamls likely have a wider variety to exercise.
- **The matrix table must be in this bead's closing comment** (or in a new artifact under `Tensile/Components/GFX1151_AUDIT/` if it gets large) so future work can reference it.

## Acceptance

- Phase A done: valid (PGR, PLR) combinations enumerated; constraints documented; per-combination body-emit behavior traced.
- Phase B done: coverage matrix populated for every combination reachable via CMS=1.
- Phase C done: one recommended design captured here; follow-up implementation bead filed.
- Tests still pass on long-term branch (594 baseline; this bead shouldn't change tests).

## Why P1

The empty-NGL crash is real on shipping kernels (parent 71f). Fixing it without first understanding the full matrix will regress other combinations or leave latent bugs. This investigation is the prerequisite for a generalization-quality fix.

## Out of scope

- Implementation of the chosen design (separate follow-up bead under 71f).
- LW handling (904).
- CMS-registration gap question (w9p — independent investigation).
- Mock-instruction infrastructure (yvx).

## Related

- 71f parent (empty-NGL crash + zero validator coverage on HHS gfx1151)
- w9p (CMS-marking gap; partial overlap on 'which kernels reach the validator')
- KernelWriter.py:4685+ (kernelBody, capture lifecycle)
- KernelWriter.py:5192-5266 (validator hook)
- ScheduleCapture.py:2883-2906 (build_dataflow_graph empty-body assertion)
- ScheduleCapture.py:247-283 (CaptureContext lifecycle)
close_reason: All 3 phases complete via sub-beads wuk (Phase A), 8ny (Phase B), ive (Phase C). Reports landed on users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans (commits 71bb01f9b3, 9c58bf546a, 9b64ef1cfb) at Tensile/Components/GFX1151_AUDIT/PGR_PLR_PHASE_{A,B,C}_*.md. Recommended hybrid design (Option 3): capture-side honesty + structural predicate + graph-build-time consistency check. Implementation NOT under this bead - file follow-up implementation bead under 71f referencing PGR_PLR_PHASE_C_DESIGN.md. Tests: 594 passed throughout. Note: ive's design was preliminary on sibling-data axis (siblings unreachable at draft time); ot2.B's findings about (2,1,DTL=F/F) crash with DSStoreD16HIB16 and the (2,1,DTL=T/T) MIXED instruction-coverage gaps surface NEW issues separate from PGR/PLR. Implementation bead should reconcile design with these findings.

title: Create AGENT.md alongside the validator (briefs AI agents on results interpretation + usage)
description:
> **NOTE (2026-05-06): Working assumption flipped.** The registered gfx1151 CMS schedules (`_get_schedule_*_gfx1151`) cannot be trusted as correct. Any default-vs-CMS capture divergence is evidence the CMS schedule is wrong, not a signal to loosen the validator or extend coverage to bad schedules. The schedule corpus has since been removed entirely (commits on `validator_long_term_plans` revert 284c1fa); references to gfx1151 in this bead should be read as historical context.

---

## Why this exists

After the validator design doc (`2yg`) lands, create an `AGENT.md` file alongside the validator (in `Tensile/Components/`) that briefs an AI coding agent (Claude, etc.) on:

1. **How to interpret validator results.** The 8 surviving Failure classes (post-hof rewrites: OrderInverted, MissingWait, WaitInsufficient, MissingBarrier, OverriddenInput, TimingTooClose, InvalidCounterValue, plus any added later) — what each one means, what the producer/consumer/wait/etc. fields refer to, what fix the message implies.
2. **How to use the validator functionality.** Entry points (`isValid`, `validate_edge_wait_coverage`, `compare_graphs`, `diagnose_missing_edge`); the strict-vs-relaxed comparison-mode flag; the SymbolMap canonicalization (post-wx9.3); the Timeline interface (post-5gd); how to add a new test fixture.
3. **What NOT to do.** Common pitfalls: don't mock the schedule shape; don't bypass tagged_inst (formatter strictness); don't reach for graph isomorphism when canonical relabeling suffices (per WX93_RESEARCH_REPORT); don't add per-resource failure subclasses (use OverriddenInputFailure).
4. **How to extend it.** Adding a new operand rule to `_OPERAND_RULES`; adding a new Failure class (when truly justified); adding a new arch profile; adding a new region (post-zq3 whole-kernel coverage).

## Format

Markdown, ~200-400 lines. Mix of:
- One-paragraph orientation per section.
- Code snippets showing canonical entry-point invocation.
- Decision flowcharts (text form) — "if you see X failure, look at Y; if Z, file a bead".
- Pointers to deeper docs (`CMSValidator_LIMITATIONS.md`, `LCC_AUDIT.md`, `WX93_RESEARCH_REPORT.md`, `GFX1151_AUDIT.md`, etc.) without duplicating their content.

## Why this is at the end

`AGENT.md` should describe the FINAL validator architecture, not snapshots of intermediate states. Run after:
- `5gd` (Timeline interface)
- `l6q.1` (ArchProfile)
- `zq3` (whole-kernel coverage)
- `2yg` (design doc — `AGENT.md` is a complement to that doc, not a replacement; design doc is "how the validator works", AGENT.md is "how an agent should use it")

If any of those are deferred indefinitely, `AGENT.md` runs after the ones that did land, with explicit notes on what's not yet implemented.

## Hard rules

- **No bead references.** AGENT.md should make sense to a reader who has never seen a bead.
- **No copy-pasted content.** Cross-reference the canonical doc (e.g. for limitation list, point at `CMSValidator_LIMITATIONS.md`); don't replicate.
- **Stay current.** AGENT.md is meant to be read by every agent on every session — stale content actively misleads. If the validator changes after AGENT.md lands, AGENT.md updates in the same commit.
- **Action-oriented.** Every section answers a "how do I..." question, not "what is...".

## Why P3

Quality / agent-onboarding work; not gating any current functionality. Run as the final touch on the validator surface after all major refactors land.

## Related beads

- `2yg` — validator design doc (dependency).
- `5gd`, `l6q.1`, `zq3` — major refactors that change validator surface (dependencies for "describe the FINAL architecture").
- `09y` — naming-quality pass; should land before AGENT.md so names referenced in AGENT.md are stable.

## Implementation directives

- **Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.** When dispatching this bead's work to a subagent, set `model: "opus"` explicitly. Do not let the dispatch fall through to default model selection — the bead is non-trivial enough to need Opus 4.7 specifically.
- **Do not write fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.** This codebase is in a clean-implementation effort. Defensive `getattr`, optional-flag-with-old-default, "leave the old API and add a parallel new one" patterns make the code worse and accumulate kludge. Take the change all the way: replace the old shape, fix the call sites, delete the dead path. If a refactor would require updating N test fixtures to opt in to the new shape, update all N — that is correct work, not extra work.

title: GR OrderInverted residual class generalizes beyond nyb5's 3-failure pin: extend per Q2
description:
## Reproducer

The 3ija triage confirms the GRA/GRB OrderInvertedFailure-in-ML residual surfaced by nyb5 generalizes across the gfx950 CMS surface. Affected fixtures and counts:

| Fixture | Layout | GR-in-ML OrderInverted count |
|---------|--------|-------|
| _128x128x32_TF32 | TN | 3 (the nyb5-pinned fixture) |
| _128x256x32_TF32 | TN | 1 (GRB->GRB) |
| _192x256x32_TF32 | NN (both LDSTr=True/False) | 1 each (GRA->GRB) |
| _256x256x32_TF32 | TN | 1 (GRA->GRA) |

All shapes: `OrderInvertedFailure` with `producer.body_label == consumer.body_label == 'ML'` and producer/consumer category in {GRA, GRB}.

## Mechanism (Q2 framing — expected)

Per `2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md §6.2 Q2`, validation is YAML-in-two-builds-out: per-tile schedules on the CMS side flip `UsePLRPack`, `UseMFMAF32XEmulation`, etc. on the kernel dict, which changes GR scheduling order on the CMS side relative to the non-CMS reference. This is **(b) classification**: expected scheduler difference, not a real defect. Same root cause as the nyb5 residual.

## Why surface (not auto-handled)

The principled handler is body-blindness or category-extension in `_NO_DATAFLOW_IDENTITY_CATEGORIES` / a sibling exclusion mechanism. But:
1. Excluding ALL of GRA/GRB from the dataflow identity set is too coarse — they are load-bearing for cross-build verification of ml-body issuing the right loads.
2. The principled fix likely needs body-blindness for *intra-body* GR ordering (the schedule chooses *order* but not *count*) without losing cross-body GR placement comparison.
3. nyb5 deferred this to 3ija; 3ija defers the principled fix to a sub-bead because (a) the right exclusion mechanism is non-obvious, (b) any one-liner that masks GR ordering risks masking a real CMS defect, and (c) the user has explicit "no tactical fixes" guidance.

## Proposed approaches (NOT implemented)

Option 1: Extend `_NO_DATAFLOW_IDENTITY_CATEGORIES` with GRA/GRB. Risk: removes the entire identity-coverage check for GR. Need to confirm the role/edge plumbing still picks them up.

Option 2: Add a per-edge tolerance: cross-build OrderInverted on GR within the same body is accepted (sibling raw-intrawave order chosen by scheduler). This is the most surgical principled fix.

Option 3: Make GR identity body-blind (loop_index ignored) so the cross-build identity sets are equivalent and the OrderInverted detector doesn't fire. Symmetric with hdem's MFMA body-blindness.

Each option needs design review with the user before landing.

## Acceptance criterion

- All 5 affected fixtures (and any future fixture with the same shape) report 0 GR-in-ML OrderInverted residuals.
- The strict-XFAIL marker on `test_non_cms_reference_compares_clean_against_cms_build` and the strict count assertion in `test_non_cms_reference_compare_graphs_surfaces_only_known_residuals` are removed (or the count-pin is generalized to all fixtures).
- No regressions on the existing test surface.

## Cross-references

- 3ija triage memo: `projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite/Tensile/Components/3IJA_RESIDUAL_TRIAGE.md`
- `NYB5_IMPLEMENTATION.md` Cycle 2 surprise (the original 3-failure surfacing).
- `HDEM_IMPLEMENTATION.md` for the body-blindness pattern that likely applies here.
- `2LZD_INVESTIGATION.md §6.2 Q2` for the expected-divergence framing.

comments.text:
## 2026-05-27: minimal reproducer landed + mechanism confirmed

Commit 4f61ba92d55 on users/alvasile/validator_long_term_plans adds test_p39d_gr_orderinverted_minimal.py — a small reproducer with two phases:

### Phase 1 — real-kernel anchor

Builds _128x128x32_TF32 TN via _make_solution + build_non_cms_reference. Asserts compare_graphs raises CaptureConsistencyError with 28-identity LR/MFMA diff (current shape under validator branch tip post-l1l6).

**Important finding:** GRA/GRB do NOT appear in the identity-diff message. The p39d GR-OrderInverted residual is structurally HIDDEN behind the larger identity-set divergence (the 28-LR/MFMA shape l1l6's xfail re-pinned to). compare_graphs aborts on the identity-set check BEFORE reaching the OrderInverted detection. Implication: p39d can only be surfaced in real-YAML smoke after the identity-set divergence is either tolerated or resolved. The GR-OrderInverted bug is real but currently masked.

### Phase 2 — trimmed minimal reproducer

Synthesizes a 2-node ML body via dataflow_fixtures:
- GRA: s_mov_b32 m0, s10 (writes mgpr(0), byte key ('m', 0))
- GRB: buffer_load_dwordx4 v254, s[4:7] lds (reads m0 implicitly via m0_resource(), same byte key)

Asserts exactly 1 OrderInvertedFailure with producer.category='GRA', consumer.category='GRB', both body_label='ML'.

### Mechanism confirmed

The p39d GRA/GRB OrderInverted residuals arise from the **DTL global-read stream's m0-dependency chain**. Each DTL group consists of:
- An m0-setter (categorized as **GRA** — but it's a scalar s_mov_b32, not a vmem GR)
- A buffer_load that reads m0 implicitly as its LDS destination address (categorized as **GRB**)

When CMS reorders these pairs (because per-tile schedule sets UsePLRPack=True before SIA3 runs), the m0-read on the CMS side precedes its m0-writer. The dataflow edge is absent from the CMS graph, surfaces as OrderInvertedFailure.

The cross-subiter ALU carve-out does NOT suppress this because setter and loader occupy the same mfma_index slot (same subiter).

### Unexpected finding worth noting

The 'GRA' category in DTL kernels is broader than expected — it includes SALU instructions (s_mov_b32 m0, s_add_u32 m0, m0, N) alongside the buffer loads. The bead's framing as 'GR scheduling order' is correct in spirit but the actual mechanism is m0-register dataflow, not vmem-vmem ordering.

### Test status

All 4 tests in the file PASS on the validator branch tip. They are pin tests for the current bug state — when p39d's principled fix lands (per-edge tolerance / GR body-blind identity / etc.), the assertions need to flip to 'zero failures.'

title: Validator response to LR divergence (gated on ffg investigation findings)
description:
## Why this exists

Follow-up to `rocm-libraries-ffg` — once the LR divergence investigation completes and produces `LR_DIVERGENCE_INVESTIGATION.md`, this bead implements the chosen response.

The investigation will document:
- WHAT the divergences are between default and CMS captures.
- WHY each divergence class exists (source-side scheduler decisions).

This bead picks an approach based on those findings and applies it.

## Decision space (to be narrowed by ffg's findings)

Three broad directions, not mutually exclusive:

1. **Loosen `compare_graphs` equivalence** — replace strict node-identity comparison with a model that tolerates wider-read substitution, different interleaving, and other semantic-equivalent variations. Catches real coverage gaps; tolerates hand-tuned divergence.

2. **Tighten CMS schedules** — modify `_get_schedule_*_gfx1151` functions so they emit the same instruction set as default. Defeats hand-tuning if the CMS variants are deliberately chosen for performance.

3. **Different equivalence model entirely** — compare by per-vgpr "first-write" and "last-read" graph edges, abstracting away how reads were grouped. May require restructuring how the dataflow graph is built.

The investigation typology will tell us which direction (or hybrid) fits.

## Acceptance (to be refined post-investigation)

- A chosen approach + rationale documented.
- Implementation lands; both CMS=1 kernels in gfx1151 HHS yaml reach `validate_edge_wait_coverage` cleanly (probe verifies).
- Tests pass on long-term branch.

## Hard rules

- Do NOT start until ffg closes and `LR_DIVERGENCE_INVESTIGATION.md` is committed.
- The implementation must be guided by the investigation's typology; do not invent an approach without grounding in the data.
- No skip-LR-comparison flag as a quick fix. The existence-of-divergence is real signal; the equivalence model must answer "is this divergence semantic-equivalent or a real coverage gap?"

## Related

- ffg (parent investigation; this bead is gated on ffg closing)
- 71f (validator coverage; this bead unblocks it after ffg)
- kzf (closed; the blocker that exposed this divergence)
close_reason: Closed without implementation. Working assumption flipped: the registered gfx1151 CMS schedules cannot be trusted as correct. Any default-vs-CMS capture divergence is evidence the CMS schedule is wrong, not a request to loosen the validator. The three options in this bead (loosen compare_graphs, tighten schedules, change equivalence model) all assume the divergences are legitimate — they are not. Validator behavior stays strict; schedule correctness is the upstream problem.

title: f3kb.N7: Heterogeneous comparison — one CMS Timeline vs one codegen-asm Timeline of the same build
description:
## Parent: f3kb (codegen-vs-codegen timeline comparison)

## Why this exists

f3kb names heterogeneous comparison as "probably a follow-up to the codegen-vs-codegen case — file a sub-bead if it becomes load-bearing." It IS load-bearing for one valuable use case: confirming that the assembly emitted from a CMS-driven build is the same dataflow graph as the CMS schedule the user wrote. That's a real user-facing sanity check ("does my CMS schedule survive codegen intact?") that no other bead covers.

`26m` (heterogeneous label policy) is the prerequisite question — what label do we use when one side is CMS and one is asm. THIS bead is the actual comparison capability that USES whatever label policy 26m decides.

## Scope

1. Pick one kernel built with `UseCustomMainLoopSchedule=1` (CMS path).
2. Capture both:
   - CMS Timeline via `cms_capture_to_timeline` (existing — landed in 5gd Part A).
   - Codegen-asm Timeline via `assembly_to_timeline` (built by x6s chain).
3. Run `compare_graphs` on the two Timelines using the comparison-mode contract from f3kb.N2.
4. Expected outcome (if everything else is sound): the two Timelines compare equivalent — the CMS schedule reaches the assembly intact.
5. Failure surface:
   - If divergent: investigate. Likely candidates are (a) codegen pass mutating the schedule (file under f3kb.N4), (b) cms_capture_to_timeline + assembly_to_timeline emitting subtly different metadata for the same instruction (fix the bridge whose metadata is wrong, NOT the comparator).
6. Test: `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_heterogeneous_cms_vs_asm_comparison.py` (or similar) that exercises this end-to-end.

## Done when

- Test exists and either passes (CMS-to-asm equivalence holds for one representative kernel) or fails with an interpretable, attributable divergence message.
- If failures emerge: each is filed against the appropriate party (codegen for mutation, bridge for metadata mismatch). No silent comparator widening.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `l88` (homogeneous comparison must work first — heterogeneous is strictly harder).
- Depends on: `26m` (label policy for heterogeneous case must be decided before failure messages can be usable).
- Depends on: x6s chain (assembly_to_timeline must exist).

## Note on 26m promotion

If this bead is filed, `26m`'s P4 "deferred-question" status no longer fits — it becomes a hard prereq. Consider promoting 26m to P3 when this bead is dispatched.

## References

- f3kb description, "Heterogeneous comparison (CMS-vs-codegen-asm)" risk.
- 26m (heterogeneous label policy question).

## Implementation directives

- Must be launched with an Opus 4.7 agent.
- No fallback paths or backwards-compatibility shims.

comments.text:
**Carry-forward from rocm-libraries-hdem (2026-05-12):** the hdem implementation substituted the literal byte-key tuple from ORAM1 §4.1 with `(producer.identity, consumer.identity, ...)` because the byte-key tuple lost producer-discrimination in two scenarios (`swap_pack` differently-classed-on-same-byte; cross-iter `LR_first`/`LR_second` same-class-same-byte). Identity carries operand text via `canonical_render` so it preserves discrimination AND is body-blind under Approach A.

**The trade-off that matters for codegen-vs-codegen:** the substitution narrows generality vs the memo design. If two captures render the SAME physical write differently — e.g., one symbolically as `v[vgprValuA_X0_I0:...+3]` and one numerically as `v[40:43]` because one resolved through `name_to_idx` and the other did not — identity-tuples DIVERGE while byte-keys would have MATCHED. Under the current CMS-vs-default path (both real captures from the same `kernelBody` invocation), this doesn't surface in practice — the empirical claim is documented at `CMSValidator.py:1252-1267`.

**Why this matters for this bead:** non-CMS vs non-CMS / codegen-vs-codegen comparison is exactly the regime where the symbolic-vs-numeric asymmetry is most likely to surface (two SIA3 invocations of the same kernel may produce different register-name resolutions; codegen-side allocator drift is documented as part of why wx9.3 work was deferred from 5gd).

**Hedge already in place:** the byte-key fields (`producer_write_byte_key` / `consumer_read_byte_key`) are still populated as informational metadata on `DataflowEdge` (CMSValidator.py:1109-1110). Future migration to byte-key matching (or a hybrid: identity-first, fall back to byte-key on render-divergence) is feasible without re-plumbing edge formation.

**References:**
- `Tensile/Components/HDEM_IMPLEMENTATION.md` "Implementation surprises" §1
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1229-1303` (current edge_keys)
- `Tensile/Components/CMSValidator.py:1252-1267` (the empirical-claim docstring)
